Another option is to translate, “the wound of his blow.” In this case the pronominal suffix might refer to the Lord, not the people, yielding the translation, “the wound which he inflicted.”

rashi.heb:
*שבעתים כאור שבעת הימים.* 
שבעתים שבע שבעיות כאור של שבעת הימים הרי ארבעים ותשע שביעיות העולים לשלש מאות וארבעים ושלשה:
rashi.eng: *sevenfold.* (שִׁבְעָתַיִּם.) This means seven sevens as the light of the seven days, i.e., forty nine sevens, equaling three hundred forty- three.

notes.1316: (sn): The “name” of the Lord sometimes stands by metonymy for the Lord himself, see Exod 23:21; Lev 24:11; Pss 54:1 (54:3 HT); 124:8. In Isa 30:27 the point is that he reveals that aspect of his character which his name suggests – he comes as Yahweh (“he is present”), the ever present helper of his people who annihilates their enemies and delivers them. The name “Yahweh” originated in a context where God assured a fearful Moses that he would be with him as he confronted Pharaoh and delivered Israel from slavery in Egypt. See Exod 3.
notes.1317: (tn, Heb): “his anger burns, and heaviness of elevation.” The meaning of the phrase “heaviness of elevation” is unclear, for מַשָּׂאָה (masa’ah, “elevation”) occurs only here. Some understand the term as referring to a cloud (elevated above the earth’s surface), in which case one might translate, “and in heavy clouds” (cf. NAB “with lowering clouds”). Others relate the noun to מָשָׂא (masa’, “burden”) and interpret it as a reference to judgment. In this case one might translate, “and with severe judgment.” The present translation assumes that the noun refers to his glory and that “heaviness” emphasizes its degree.
notes.1318: (tn, Heb): “his lips are full of anger, and his tongue is like consuming fire.” The Lord’s lips and tongue are used metonymically for his word (or perhaps his battle cry; see v. 31).

rashi.heb:
*שם ה'.* 
גבורתו שתהא לו לשם מה שיעשה סנחריב:
rashi.eng: *the Name of the Lord.* His might, which will be for Him as a name, viz., what He will do to Sennacherib.

rashi.heb:
*בא ממרחק.* 
להאמין מה שהבטיח זה ימים רבים:
rashi.eng: *comes from long ago.* (מִמֶּרְחָק, lit. from afar.) To realize what He promised long ago.

rashi.heb:
*משאה.* 
ה"א יתירה ואינו אלא כמו משא לפיכך נקודה רפי:
rashi.eng: *the burden.* (מַשָּׂאָה) The ‘heh’ is superfluous, and it is only like מַשָּׂא. Therefore, the ‘heh’ is silent, not punctuated by a mappiq.

notes.1319: (tn, Heb): “his breath is like a flooding river.” This might picture the Lord breathing heavily as he runs down his enemy, but in light of the preceding verse, which mentions his lips and tongue, “breath” probably stands metonymically for the word or battle cry that he expels from his mouth as he shouts. In Isa 34:16 and Ps 33:6 the Lord’s “breath” is associated with his command.
notes.1320: (tn, Heb): “shaking nations in a sieve of worthlessness.” It is not certain exactly how שָׁוְא (shav�’, “emptiness, worthlessness”) modifies “sieve.” A sieve is used to separate grain from chaff and isolate what is worthless so that it might be discarded. Perhaps the nations are likened to such chaff; God’s judgment will sift them out for destruction.
notes.1321: (tn, Heb): “and a bit that leads astray [is] in the jaws of the peoples.” Here the nations are likened to horse that can be controlled by a bit placed in its mouth. In this case the Lord uses his sovereign control over the “horse” to lead it to its demise.

rashi.heb:
*כנחל שוטף.* 
אשר העובר בו יחצה בו עד צוארו שאין בו שום כח לעמוד בפני שטף המים:
rashi.eng: *is like a flooding stream.* which divides the one who crosses it, up to his neck, for he has no strength to stand against the current of the water.

rashi.heb:
*להנפה.* 
להניף אווני"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *to wave.* (לַהֲנָפָה) to wave, vaner in O.F.

rashi.heb:
*בנפת שוא.* 
לא להועיל להם והם סבורים להועיל:
rashi.eng: *with a vain waving.* Not to avail them, but they think it will avail.

rashi.heb:
*רסן.* 
פרומבי"א פרינ"ק בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and a bit.* (רֶסֶן) a bit, freynk in O.F., (a rein or curb).

notes.1322: (tn, Heb): “[you will have] joy of heart, like the one going with a flute to enter the mountain of the Lord to the Rock of Israel.” The image here is not a foundational rock, but a rocky cliff where people could hide for protection (for example, the fortress of Masada).

rashi.heb:
*השיר יהיה לכם.* 
בליל הפסח תבא לכם שמחה זו:
rashi.eng: *This song shall be to you.* On the night of Passover shall this joy come to you.

rashi.heb:
*כליל התקדש חג.* 
כמו שאמרת' שיר של הפסחים במצרים ונראה מקרא זה כאילו בא ללמד על סנחרב ולימד על פרעה שאמרו הלל בליל אכילת פסחים מדרש תהלים:
rashi.eng: *as the night of the sanctification of the festival.* Just as you recited a song over the Paschal sacrifices in Egypt [It appears from this verse as though he wishes to teach us about Sennacherib, but he teaches us about Pharaoh, that they recited Hallel on the night of the eating of the Paschal sacrifices. In Midrash Tehillim (1:20)].

rashi.heb:
*כהולך בחליל.* 
ותשמחו במפלת סנחריב כשמחת מביאי ביכורים שהיה החליל מכה לפניהם לבוא בהר ה', כמו ששנינו במס' בכורים:
rashi.eng: *like one who goes with a flute.* And you shall rejoice with the downfall of Sennacherib like the joy of those who bring the First Fruits, before whom the flute would play, to come upon the mountain of God, as we learned in Tractate Bikkurim (3:4).

notes.1323: (tn, Heb): “the Lord will cause the splendor of his voice to be heard.”
notes.1324: (tn, Heb): “and reveal the lowering of his arm.”
notes.1325: (tn, Heb): “and a flame of consuming fire.”

rashi.heb:
*ונחת זרועו.* 
אין זה ל' נוח אלא ל' נוחות פושלמנ"ט בלע"ז כמו וינח בכל גבול מצרים (שמות יז) הנחת גבורתו יראה בלהב אש שנשרפו אוכלוסי סנחריב:
rashi.eng: *and the laying down of His arm.* This is not an expression of resting but an expression of placing, posement in O.F. Comp. (Exod. 10:14) “And placed it (וַיָּנַח) throughout the entire boundary of Egypt.” The placing of His might He will show in a flame by which the armies of Sennacherib were burnt.

rashi.heb:
*נפץ.* 
ל' שיבור יותר:
rashi.eng: *bursting.* (נֶפֶץ) an expression of more intense breaking, (shattering).

rashi.heb:
*וזרם.* 
קילוח מטר סוחף:
rashi.eng: *and storming rain.*

notes.1326: (tn, Heb): “Indeed by the voice of the Lord Assyria will be shattered.”

rashi.heb:
*מקול ה' יחת אשור.* 
אזנים פתח להם ושמעו שירה מפי חיות ומתו באגדת חלק:
rashi.eng: *from the Lord’s voice Assyria shall be broken.* he opened up their ears, and they heard the song from the mouth of the Chayoth, and they died. In the Aggadah of Chapter Chelek.

rashi.heb:
*בשבט יכה.* 
אשור אשר היה רגיל להכותך בשבטו:
rashi.eng: *with a rod he would smite.* Assyria, who was wont to smite you with his rod.

notes.1327: (tc): The Hebrew text has “every blow from a founded [i.e., “appointed”?] cudgel.” The translation above, with support from a few medieval Hebrew mss, assumes an emendation of מוּסָדָה (musadah, “founded”) to מוּסָרֹה (musaroh, “his discipline”).
notes.1328: (tn, Heb): “which the Lord lays on him.”
notes.1330: (tn): The Hebrew text reads literally, “and with battles of brandishing [weapons?] he will fight against him.” Some prefer to emend וּבְמִלְחֲמוֹת (uv�milkhamot, “and with battles of”) to וּבִמְחֹלוֹת (uvimkholot, “and with dancing”). Note the immediately preceding references to musical instruments.

rashi.heb:
*והיה כל מעבר מטה מוסדה.* 
כל מעברות תוקף יסודות אוכלוסיו כל המקומות אשר עברו שם והשחיתום וביום מפלתם יניח ה' עליהם על שמועת מפלתם והם יהיו בתפים ובכינורות, וכה פתרון המקרא בסירוס והיה בתפים ובכינורות כל מעבר מטה מוסדה אשר יניחם ה' עליו ובמלחמות תנופת שוא מעלה ומוריד נלחם בם הקב"ה, ומדרש אגדה תנופת קציר העומר עמדה לישראל באותה מלחמה כי ליל ששה עשר בניסן היה:
rashi.eng: *And it shall be, every place where the established staff shall pass.* All the crossings of the strength of the foundations of his armies; all the places they passed and destroyed, and on the day of their downfall the Lord shall grant peace upon them through the news of their downfall, and they shall be joyful with drums and harps. And this is the interpretation of the verse in inverted order: And it shall be with drums and harps, every passing of the established staff upon which the Lord shall grant peace, and with wars of vain waving, lifting and lowering, did the Holy One, blessed be He, fight against them. And, according to Midrash Aggadah, the waving of the harvest of the Omer stood up for Israel in that war, for it was the night of the sixteenth of Nissan.

notes.1332: (tc): The Hebrew text reads literally, “for arranged from before [or “yesterday”] is [?].” The meaning of תָּפְתֶּה (taf�teh), which occurs only here, is unknown. The translation above (as with most English versions) assumes an emendation to תֹּפֶת (tofet, “Topheth”; cf. NASB, NIV, NLT) and places the final hey (ה) on the beginning of the next word as an interrogative particle. Topheth was a place near Jerusalem used as a burial ground (see Jer 7:32; 19:11).
notes.1333: (tn): The Hebrew text reads literally, “Also it is made ready for the king, one makes it deep and wide.” If one takes the final hey (ה) on תָּפְתֶּה (taf�teh) and prefixes it to גָּם (gam) as an interrogative particle (see the preceding note), one can translate, “Is it also made ready for the king?” In this case the question is rhetorical and expects an emphatic affirmative answer, “Of course it is!”
notes.1334: (tn, Heb): “its pile of wood, fire and wood one makes abundant.” Apparently this alludes to some type of funeral rite.

rashi.heb:
*כי ערוך מאתמול.* 
יום שני לבריאת עולם יום שיש לו תמול ואין לו שלשום:
rashi.eng: *For… is set up from yesterday.* The second day of the Creation of the world a day that has a yesterday but not a day before yesterday.

rashi.heb:
*תפתה.* 
גיהנם שכל המתפתה ביצרו נופל שם:
rashi.eng: *Tophteh.* Gehinnom, for whoever is enticed (מִתְפַּתֶּה) by his temptation falls into there.

rashi.heb:
*למלך הוכן.* 
לצורך סנחריב וחילו:
rashi.eng: *has been prepared for the king.* For the necessity of Sennacherib and his army.

rashi.heb:
*מדורתה.* 
לשון אש נסקת מערכת עצים על האש קרויה מדורה:
rashi.eng: *its pile.* (מְדֻרָתָהּ) an expression of a heated fire. An arrangement of wood on the fire is called מְדוּרָה.

rashi.heb:
*נשמת ה'.* 
נפיחת רוחו:
rashi.eng: *the breath of the Lord.* the blowing of His breath.

rashi.heb:
*בוערה.* 
בוערת:
rashi.eng: *burning.* (בֹּעֲרָה) equivalent to בּוֹעֶרֶת.

notes.1335: (tn, Heb): “Woe [to] those who go down to Egypt for help.”
notes.1336: (tn, Heb): “and trust in chariots for they are many.”
notes.1337: (tn, Heb): “and in horsemen for they are very strong [or “numerous”].”
notes.1338: (sn): See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

rashi.heb:
*הוי.* 
על הושע ועשרת השבטים היורדים מצרימה לעזרה אשר שלחו מלאכים אל סוא מלך מצרים (מלכים ב י״ז:ד׳):
rashi.eng: *Woe.* Concerning Hoshea and the ten tribes who went down to Egypt for aid, who sent emissaries to So, king of Egypt (II Kings 17).

rashi.heb:
*ועל סוסים.* 
הבאים משם שהם קלים לרוץ:
rashi.eng: *on horses.* that come from there, for they are swift runners.

rashi.heb:
*ישענו.* 
(כמו ולא שעו אל קדוש ישראל) כמו שעשה חזקיה שנ' (מלכים ב י״ח:ה׳) בה' אלהי ישראל בטח וימרוד במלך אשור:
rashi.eng: *rely.* (יִשָּׁעֵנוּ) and they did not rely on the Holy One of Israel as Hezekiah did, concerning whom it is written: (II Kings 18:5, 7): “He trusted in the Lord God of Israel… and he rebelled against the king of Assyria.”

notes.1339: (sn): This statement appears to have a sarcastic tone. The royal advisers who are advocating an alliance with Egypt think they are wise, but the Lord possesses wisdom as well and will thwart their efforts.
notes.1340: (tn, Heb): “and he does not turn aside [i.e., “retract”] his words”; NIV “does not take back his words.”
notes.1341: (tn, Heb): “and he will arise against the house of the wicked.”
notes.1343: (tn, Heb): “and against the help of the doers of sin.”

rashi.heb:
*ואת דבריו לא הסיר.* 
אשר אמר והשיבך ה' מצרים באניות (דברים כ״ח:ס״ח) מדה כנגד מדה שאמרתי לך (שם) לא תוסיף עוד לראותה ואתה הלכת מדעתך סופך לילך בגלות על כרחך:
rashi.eng: *and His words He did not retract.* What He said, “And the Lord shall take you back to Egypt in ships” (Deut. 28:68). This is payment in kind, for I said to you, “You shall no longer see it (ibid.),” and you went there of your own free will. Eventually, you shall go there in exile against your will.

rashi.heb:
*וקם.* 
על עשרת השבטים שהם בית מרעים ועל מצרים אשר הם להם לעזרה:
rashi.eng: *and He rose.* on the ten tribes, who are a house of evildoers, and on the Egyptians who came to their aid.

notes.1344: (tn, Heb): “will extend”; KJV, ASV, NASB, NCV “stretch out.”
notes.1345: (tn, Heb): “together all of them will come to an end.”

rashi.heb:
*יטה ידו.* 
שהקב"ה סומך הכל בידו וכשיטה אותה יפלו כזה שאוחז דבר בכפו וכשהוא מרכין כפו הוא נופל כך ומדרש אגדה וי"ת ירים יד מחת גבורתיה:
rashi.eng: *shall turn His hand.* For the Holy One, blessed be He, supports everything with His hand, and when He turns it, they will fall, like one who holds something in his hand, and when he inclines his hand, it falls. So is the Midrash Aggadah (Mechilta, Exodus 15:12). Jonathan, however, renders: shall raise the blow of His might.

notes.1346: (tn, Heb): “As a lion growls, a young lion over its prey.” In the Hebrew text the opening comparison is completed later in the verse (“so the Lord will come down…”), after a parenthesis describing how fearless the lion is. The present translation divides the verse into three sentences for English stylistic reasons.
notes.1347: (tn, Heb): “Though there is summoned against it fullness of shepherds, by their voice it is not terrified, and to their noise it does not respond.”
notes.1348: (tn): Some prefer to translate the phrase לִצְבֹּא עַל (litsbo’ ’al) as “fight against,” but the following context pictures the Lord defending, not attacking, Zion.

rashi.heb:
*כאשר יהגה.* 
המיית קול כמו וכיונים הגו נהגה (לקמן נט):
rashi.eng: *As… growls.* (יֶהְגֶּה) a roaring sound. Comp. (infra 59:11) “And like doves we will moan (נֶהְגֶּה הָגֹה).”

rashi.heb:
*אשר יקרא עליו מלא רועים.* 
יאספון עליו בקריאת קול המון:
rashi.eng: *although a band of shepherds gather against him.* (יִקָּרֵא, lit., will be called.) They will gather upon him with a stirring shout.

rashi.heb:
*מלא רועים.* 
אסיפת רועים וכן קראו אחריך מלא (ירמיהו י״ב:ו׳) וכן יחד עלי יתמלאון (איוב ט״ז:י׳) כולם ל' קיבוץ:
rashi.eng: *band of shepherds.* (מְלֹא) a gathering of shepherds. Comp. (Jer. 12:6) “They called after you a band (מָלֵא).” Comp. also (Job 16:10) “Together they gather (יִתְמַלָּאוּן) against me.” All of these are expressions of gathering.

rashi.heb:
*לא יענה.* 
לא יכנע לא יעשה עצמו עני וכן לענות מפני (שמות יא) וכן וענה גאון ישראל (הושע ה׳:ה׳):
rashi.eng: *he is not subdued.* (יַעֲנֶה) he will not humble himself, he will not make himself as a poor man. Comp. (Exodus 10:3) “To humble yourself (לֵעָנוֹת) from before Me.” Comp. also (Hosea 5:5) “And the pride of Israel shall be humbled (וְעָנָה).”

rashi.heb:
*כן ירד.* 
ולא יפחד מהמון האומות:
rashi.eng: *so shall… descend.* (This intimates that God will descend) and will not be afraid of the stirring (or the multitude) of the nations.

notes.1349: (tn, Heb): “just as birds fly.” The words “over a nest” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.1350: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.1351: (tn): The only other occurrence of this verb is in Exod 12:13, 23, 27, where the Lord “passes over” (i.e., “spares”) the Israelite households as he comes to judge their Egyptian oppressors. The noun פֶּסַח (pesakh, “Passover”) is derived from the verb. The use of the verb in Isa 31:5 is probably an intentional echo of the Exodus event. As in the days of Moses the Lord will spare his people as he comes to judge their enemies.

rashi.heb:
*פסוח.* 
דילוג ויש עוד לפותרו לשון חיים:
rashi.eng: *passing over.* (פָּסוֹחַ) passing over. Alternatively, it may be interpreted as an expression of sparing.

rashi.heb:
*והמליט.* 
יוציא את ישראל מן הצרה ל' המלטה אישקמוציי"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and rescuing.* He will extricate Israel from the strait. This is an expression of rescue (esmoucer in O.F.).

notes.1352: (tn, Heb): “Return to the one [against] whom the sons of Israel made deep rebellion.” The syntax is awkward here. A preposition is omitted by ellipsis after the verb (see GKC 446 �138.f, n. 2), and there is a shift from direct address (note the second plural imperative “return”) to the third person (note “they made deep”). For other examples of abrupt shifts in person in poetic style, see GKC 462 �144.p.

rashi.heb:
*שובו.* 
למי שהעמקתם מחשבות היאך לסור ממנו וסרתם מעליו עתה שובו אליו:
rashi.eng: *Return.* To the One about Whom you have thought deeply how to turn away from Him, now return to Him.

notes.1354: (tn, Heb): “reject” (so NIV); NRSV, TEV, CEV, NLT “throw away.”
notes.1355: (tn, Heb): “the idols of their idols of silver and their idols of gold which your hands made for yourselves [in] sin.” חָטָא (khata’, “sin”) is understood as an adverbial accusative of manner. See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:573, n. 4.

notes.1356: (tn, Heb): “Assyria will fall by a sword, not of a man.”
notes.1357: (tn, Heb): “and a sword not of humankind will devour him.”
notes.1358: (tn, Heb): “he will flee for himself from before a sword.”

notes.1359: (tn, Heb): “rocky cliff” (cf. ASV, NASB “rock”), viewed metaphorically as a place of defense and security.
notes.1360: (tn, Heb): “His rocky cliff, because of fear, will pass away [i.e., “perish”].”
notes.1361: (tn, Heb): “and they will be afraid of the flag, his officers.”
notes.1362: (sn): The “fire” and “firepot” here symbolize divine judgment, which is heating up like a fire in Jerusalem, waiting to be used against the Assyrians when they attack the city.

rashi.heb:
*וסלעו ממגור יעבור.* 
וחזקו מרוב פחד יחלוש:
rashi.eng: *And his rock shall pass from fear.* And his strength shall be weakened from great fear.

rashi.heb:
*וחתו מנס.* 
מפני הניסים שיראו שהקב"ה עושה לישראל:
rashi.eng: *shall be dismayed at the miracle.* Because of the great miracles that the Holy One, blessed be He, performs for Israel.

rashi.heb:
*אשר אור לו בציון.* 
שם יהיה האש מוכן לשורפם:
rashi.eng: *whose fire is in Zion.* There the fire will be prepared to burn them.

rashi.heb:
*הן לצדק ימלך מלך.* 
הן אין משפט מלך למלוך כי אם לעשות משפט צדק:
rashi.eng: *Behold, for righteousness shall a king reign.* Behold a king has no right to reign except to execute righteous judgment.

rashi.heb:
*ולשרים למשפט ישורו.* 
ועל מי יש לו למלוך על שרים אשר למשפט ישורו, ואמר הנביא זאת על אחז שהיה רשע אבל חזקיהו בנו ימלוך וכדי הוא:
rashi.eng: *and over princes who rule with justice.* And over whom should he reign? Over princes who rule with justice. The prophet says this concerning Ahaz, who was a wicked man, but Hezekiah his son shall rule, and he is worthy. ([Manuscripts read:] And he is worthy of reigning.)

notes.1365: (tn, Heb): “a man,” but אִישׁ (’ish) probably refers here to “each” of the officials mentioned in the previous verse.

rashi.heb:
*והיה איש.* 
הגבור ביראת הקב"ה הוא חזקיה יהיה לישראל:
rashi.eng: *And the man shall be.* The hero in the fear of the Holy One, blessed be He - that is Hezekiah - shall be for Israel.

rashi.heb:
*כמחבא רוח.* 
כמחסה סלע שנחבאים בו מפני רוח ונסתרים שם מפני חורב כן יבטחו בו הנותרים מי' השבטי':
rashi.eng: *as a hiding place from the wind.* As a shelter of a rock, where people hide because of the wind, and they hide there because of the heat ([mss. read:] because of the rain), so will those remaining from the ten tribes trust in him.

rashi.heb:
*בציון.* 
ל' יובש ציה:
rashi.eng: *in an arid land..* (בְּצָיוֹן) an expression of dryness, desolation (צִיָּה).

rashi.heb:
*כצל סלע כבד בארץ עיפה.* 
במקום שמש שהארץ עיפה שם וחריבה ותאבה לצל:
rashi.eng: *as the shade of a huge rock in a weary land.* In a sunny place, where the earth is weary and dry and yearning for shade.

notes.1367: (tn): The Hebrew text as vocalized reads literally “will not gaze,” but this is contradictory to the context. The verb form should be revocalized as תְּשֹׁעֶינָה (t�sho’enah) from שָׁעַע (sha’a’, “be blinded”); see Isa 6:10; 29:9.

rashi.heb:
*ולא תשעינה עיני רואים.* 
לא כמות שהם עכשיו אזניו הכבד ועיניו השע (לעיל ו) ל' טוח:
rashi.eng: *And the eyes of them that see shall not be sealed.* (Heb. תִשְׁעֶינָה) Not as they are now, that “his ears are becoming heavy, and his eyes are becoming sealed (הָשַׁע)” (supra 6:10), an expression of sealing.

notes.1369: (tn, Heb): “the heart of rashness will understand knowledge”; cf. NAB “The flighty will become wise and capable.”

rashi.heb:
*ולבב נמהרים יבין לדעת.* 
לא כמו שעכשיו השמן לב העם (שם):
rashi.eng: *And the heart of the hasty shall understand to know.* Not like now, that “this people’s heart is becoming fat” (ibid.).

rashi.heb:
*ולשון עלגים וגו'.* 
ולא כמו שעכשיו כי בלעגי שפה (לעיל כח):
rashi.eng: *and the tongue of the stammerers, etc..* Not like now, “for with distorted speech” (supra 28:11).

rashi.heb:
*עלגים.* 
כל מי שאינו יודע לכוין דיבורו להיות צח קרוי עלג ונלעג:
rashi.eng: *stammerers.* Anyone who does not know how to direct his speech to be clear is termed עִלֵּג or נִלְעַג.

rashi.heb:
*ולכילי.* 
רמאי נוכל חורש רעים:
rashi.eng: *deceitful.* (כִּילַי) a plotting deceiver, who plots evil.

rashi.heb:
*שוע.* 
ל' אדון שהכל שועין ופונין אליו:
rashi.eng: *noble.* (שׁוּעַ) an expression of a lord, to whom everyone turns (שׁוֹעִין).

notes.1370: (tn): Or “foolishness,” in a moral-ethical sense. See 9:17.
notes.1371: (tn, Heb): “and his heart commits sin”; KJV, ASV “his heart will work iniquity”; NASB “inclines toward wickedness.”
notes.1372: (tn, Heb): “in order to do [or “so that he does”] what is godless [or “defiled”].”
notes.1373: (tn, Heb): “so that he leaves empty the appetite [or “desire”] of the hungry.”
notes.1374: (tn, Heb): “and the drink of the thirsty he causes to fail.”

rashi.heb:
*נבלה ידבר.* 
מדבר ל' הוה הוא:
rashi.eng: *speaks villainy.* (יְדַבֵּר) like מְדַבֵּר, a present tense.

rashi.heb:
*יעשה און.* 
יקבץ מחשבות און כמו (דברים ח׳:י״ז) עשה לי החיל הזה:
rashi.eng: *works iniquity.* (יַעֲשֶׂה) Gathers thoughts of iniquity. Comp. (Deut. 8:17) “Gathered (עָשָׂה) for me this wealth.”

rashi.heb:
*לעשות חונף.* 
חושב מחשבות איך יוכל לעשות חנופה, חונף שם דבר לכך טעמו למעלה ונקוד פתח:
rashi.eng: *to practice flattery.* (לֲעֲשׂוֹת) He thinks thoughts how he can practice flattery. חֹנֵף is a noun; therefore, the accent is on the first syllable, it is vowelized with a ‘pattah’ (now called a ‘segol’).

rashi.heb:
*ומשקה צמא יחסיר.* 
לפי פשוטו שגוזלין העניים ותרגומו פתגמי אורייתא דאינון כמיא לצחייא מדמן לבטלא:
rashi.eng: *and the drink of the thirsty he causes to fail.* According to the simple meaning, they rob the poor. The Targum, (however, paraphrases:) The words of the Torah, which are like water to the thirsty, they plan to nullify.

notes.1375: (tn, Heb): “as for a deceiver, his implements [or “weapons”] are evil.”
notes.1376: (tn): Or “he plans evil things”; NIV “he makes up evil schemes.”
notes.1377: (tn, Heb): “to ruin the poor with words of falsehood, even when the needy speak what is just.”

rashi.heb:
*ובדבר אביון משפט.* 
לחבל אביון במשפטו, משפט זה ל' תחלת דברים במשפט כשמדבר האביון טענותיו זה יועץ מזימו' להכשילו בנכליו משפט משמש שלשה לשונו' תחלת טענת דשריינמנ"ט בלע"ז וגמר הדין יואיימנ"ט בלע"ז ומשטר ששוטרין אותו ביסורין יושטיצ"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and when the needy speaks a plea.* (מִשְׁפָּט) To destroy the needy in his plea (מִשְׁפָּטוֹ). This word מִשְׁפָּט is an expression denoting the initial presentation of the case; when the needy presents his pleas, this one plans wicked plots to trap him with his devices. The word מִשְׁפָּט has three meanings: the initial pleas (derajjsnement in O.F.), the sentence (joujjment), and the execution of the verdict, that they discipline him with chastisement (joustize in O.F.).

notes.1378: (tn, Heb): “and he upon honorable things stands.”

rashi.heb:
*על נדיבות יקום.* 
בשביל נדיבותיו תהיה לו תקומה:
rashi.eng: *because of generous deeds, shall stand.* Because of his generous acts, he will have preservation.

notes.1379: (tn): Or “self-assured”; NASB, NRSV “who are at ease.”

rashi.heb:
*נשים שאננות.* 
מדינן דיתבן שליון:
rashi.eng: *Complacent women.* Provinces that dwell in tranquility [from Jonathan].

rashi.heb:
*בנות בוטחות.* 
כרכין דיתבין לרוחצן:
rashi.eng: *confident daughters.* Walled cities that dwell confidently [from Jonathan].

rashi.heb:
*ימים על שנה.* 
כמו (לעיל כט) ספו שנה על שנה ותמיד עונותיכם מתגברין וסוף תרגזנה אלו שהן עכשיו לבטח כי יכלה מהם בציר הענבים ואוסף התבואה לא יבוא אל הבית:
rashi.eng: *Year after year.* (lit., ‘days upon a year.’) Comp. (supra 29:1) “Add year to year,” and your sins are constantly becoming more serious, until eventually you shall be troubled, those who are now confident, for the vintage of the grapes shall be over for them, and the ingathering of the grain shall not come into the house.

rashi.heb:
*אוסף.* 
שם דבר לכך טעמו למעלה ונקוד פתח:
rashi.eng: *the ingathering.* (אֹסֶף) This is a noun; therefore, its accent is on the first syllable and it is vowelized with a ‘pattah’ (now called a ‘segol’).

notes.1383: (tn): The imperatival forms in v. 11 are problematic. The first (חִרְדוּ, khirdu, “tremble”) is masculine plural in form, though spoken to a feminine plural addressee (שַׁאֲנַנּוֹת, sha’anannot, “complacent ones”). The four imperatival forms that follow (רְגָזָה, r�gazah, “shake with fear”; פְּשֹׁטָה, p�shotah, “strip off your clothes”; עֹרָה, ’orah, “expose yourselves”; and חֲגוֹרָה, khagorah, “put on”) all appear to be lengthened (so-called “emphatic”) masculine singular forms, even though they too appear to be spoken to a feminine plural addressee. GKC 131-32 �48.i suggests emending חִרְדוּ (khirdu) to חֲרָדָה (kharadah) and understanding all five imperatives as feminine plural “aramaized” forms.

rashi.heb:
*רגזה.* 
כמו לרגז:
rashi.eng: *to be troubled.* (רְגָזָה) to be troubled. (This is an infinitive despite the absence of the ‘lammed.’)

rashi.heb:
*פשוטה.* 
כמו לפשוט:
rashi.eng: *to undress.* (פְּשֹׁטָה) to undress. (This too is an infinitive with the ‘lammed’ missing.)

rashi.heb:
*ועורה.* 
כמו לערות ל' עריה (מיכה א):
rashi.eng: *and to bare.* (וְעֹרָה) An expression of ‘naked’ (עֶרְיָה) (Micah 1:11).

rashi.heb:
*וחגורה.* 
כמו לחגור לכך טעמו למעלה וכן תירגם יונתן שלחו איתערטילו ואסרו על חרצין מתוך שיפשיטו ויתערמו מבגדיהם לא יחגרו על בגדיהם כי על מתניהם:
rashi.eng: *and to gird.* (וַחֲגוֹרָה) Therefore, the accent is before the last syllable, and so did Jonathan render: Undress and bare yourselves and gird on your loins. Since they will undress and bare themselves of their garments, they will not gird on their garments but on their loins.

notes.1384: (tc): The Hebrew text has “over mourning breasts.” The reference to “breasts” would make sense in light of v. 11, which refers to the practice of women baring their breasts as a sign of sorrow (see J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah [NICOT], 1:585). However, one expects the preposition עַל (’al) to introduce the source or reason for mourning (see vv. 12b-13a) and the participle סֹפְדִים (sofedim, “mourning”) seems odd modifying “breasts.” The translation above assumes a twofold emendation: (1) שָׁדַיִם (shadayim, “breasts”) is emended to [ם]שָׂדַי (saday[m], “field,” a term that also appears in Isa 56:9). The final mem (ם) would be enclitic in this case, not a plural indicator. (The Hebrew noun שָׂדֶה (sadeh, “field”) forms its plural with an וֹת- [-ot] ending). (2) The plural participle סֹפְדִים is emended to סְפֹדָה (s�fodah), a lengthened imperatival form, meaning “mourn.” For an overview of various suggestions that have been made for this difficult line, see Oswalt, 586, n. 12).

rashi.heb:
*על שדים סופדים.* 
יטפחו על לבם:
rashi.eng: *on the breasts, lamenting.* They shall beat their heart.

rashi.heb:
*על שדי חמד.* 
על שדות) חמדתן, ומ"א על חכמי סנהדראות שהם כשדי' המניקי' יספדו, ועל עיר חמדתן שתחרש כשדה ועל גפן פוריה הם ישראל שנקראו גפן כמ"ש גפן ממצרי' תסיע:
rashi.eng: *for the desirable fields.* For the fields of their desire. The Midrash Aggadah (See twenty-fourth poem to Lamentations Rabbah) states: For the sages of the Sanhedrin, who are like breasts that nurture, they will lament, and for the city of their desire that will be plowed up like a field, and for the fruitful - vine that is Israel, called a vine, as it is said (Psalms 80:9): “You plucked a vine out of Egypt.”

notes.1385: (tn): “Mourn” is supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons. In the Hebrew text vv. 12-13 are one long sentence.
notes.1386: (tn, Heb): “indeed, over all the houses of joy.” It is not certain if this refers to individual homes or to places where parties and celebrations were held.
notes.1387: (sn): This same phrase is used in 22:2.

rashi.heb:
*קוץ שמיר.* 
הובאי ובור כי כל חורבן זה יהיה על כל בתי משוש ועל:
rashi.eng: *Thorns and briers.* The Targum renders: הוּבֵאִי וּבוּר various types of thorns, for all this destruction shall be on all houses of joy, and on

rashi.heb:
*קריה עליזה.* 
ירושלים שהיא משוש לכל הארץ (איכה ב):
rashi.eng: *the joyful city.* Jerusalem, which is “the joy of all the land” (Lamentations 2:15).

notes.1389: (tn): Hebrew עֹפֶל (’ofel), probably refers here to a specific area within the city of Jerusalem. See HALOT 861 s.v. II עֹפֶל.
notes.1390: (tn): The Hebrew text has בְעַד מְעָרוֹת (v�’ad m�’arot). The force of בְעַד, which usually means “behind, through, round about,” or “for the benefit of,” is uncertain here. HALOT 616 s.v. *מְעָרָה takes מְעָרוֹת (m�’arot) as a homonym of “cave” and define it here as “cleared field.” Despite these lexical problems, the general point of the statement seems clear – the city will be uninhabited.
notes.1391: (tn, Heb): “the joy of wild donkeys, a pasture for flocks.”

rashi.heb:
*כי ארמון.* 
היכל המלך מלך יהודה נוטש:
rashi.eng: *For the palace.* The king’s palace has been forsaken.

rashi.heb:
*והמון עיר.* 
גלה:
rashi.eng: *the multitude of the city.* has been exiled.

rashi.heb:
*עופל ובחן.* 
בית מקדשי שהיה להם למבצר:
rashi.eng: *rampart and tower.* My Temple, which was a fortification for them.

rashi.heb:
*היה בעד מערות.* 
יהיה בתוך חורבות מערת ל' ערו ערו (תהילים קל״ז:ז׳), ובעד כמו הבעד ערפל ישפוט (איוב כ״ב:י״ג):
rashi.eng: *are amidst ruins.* (הָיָה בְּעַד מְעָרוֹת), shall be amidst ruins. מְעָרוֹת is an expression similar to (Psalms 137:7) “Raze it, raze it (עָרוּ עָרוּ).” בְּעַד is like “(Job 22:13) Can He judge through (הַבְעַד) a thick cloud?”

rashi.heb:
*עד עולם.* 
עד עת קץ עופל ובחן. שניהם ל' מבצר:
rashi.eng: *forever.* Until the time of the end.

rashi.heb:
*משוש פראים.* 
לתאות ישמעאל (ולמרעה אדום) ולחיילותיו:
rashi.eng: *a joy for wild donkeys.* For the lust of Ishmael and his hosts.

notes.1392: (tn, Heb): “until a spirit is emptied out on us from on high.” The words “this desolation will continue” are supplied in the translation for clarification and stylistic purposes. The verb עָרָה (’arah), used here in the Niphal, normally means “lay bare, expose.” The term רוּחַ (ruakh, “spirit”) is often understood here as a reference to the divine spirit (cf. 44:3 and NASB, NIV, CEV, NLT), but it appears here without an article (cf. NRSV “a spirit”), pronominal suffix, or a genitive (such as “of the Lord”). The translation assumes that it carries an impersonal nuance “vivacity, vigor” in this context.
notes.1393: (sn): The same statement appears in 29:17b, where, in conjunction with the preceding line, it appears to picture a reversal. Here it seems to depict supernatural growth. The desert will blossom into an orchard, and the trees of the orchard will multiply and grow tall, becoming a forest.

rashi.heb:
*עד יערה עלינו.* 
ישפוך עלינו כמו ותער כדה (בראשית כ״ד:כ׳) ל' שפיכה נופל על הרוח כמו ושפכתי על בית דוד רוח חן (יואל ג׳:א׳) וכן אשפוך רוחי על כל בשר (זכריה י״ב:י׳):
rashi.eng: *Until… be poured upon us.* (יֵעָרֶה) He shall pour upon us. Comp. (Gen. 24:2) “And she emptied (וַתְּעַר) her pitcher.” An expression of pouring applies to spirit. Comp. (Zech. 12:10) “And I will pour upon the house of David… a spirit of grace.” Comp. also (Joel 3:1) “I will pour My spirit upon all flesh.”

rashi.heb:
*ליער יחשב.* 
קירוין סגיאין כיער הזה שהוא מלא עצים:
rashi.eng: *shall be regarded as a forest.* (Jonathan renders:) Great cities, like this forest, which is full of trees.

notes.1394: (sn): This new era of divine blessing will also include a moral/ethical transformation, as justice and fairness fill the land and replace the social injustice so prevalent in Isaiah’s time.

rashi.heb:
*ושכן במדבר משפט.* 
בירושלים שהיא כמדבר:
rashi.eng: *And justice shall dwell in the desert.* In Jerusalem, which is like a desert.

rashi.heb:
*וצדקה בכרמל.* 
היא ארץ ישראל שתהא באותן הימים ככרמל:
rashi.eng: *and righteousness shall reside in the fruitful field.* That is the land of Israel, which in those days shall be like a fruitful field.

notes.1395: (tn, Heb): “and the product of fairness will be peace.”
notes.1396: (tn, Heb): “and the work of fairness [will be] calmness and security forever.”

notes.1397: (tn): Or “in safe resting places”; NAB, NRSV “quiet resting places.”

notes.1398: (tn, Heb): “and [?] when the forest descends.” The form וּבָרַד (uvarad) is often understood as an otherwise unattested denominative verb meaning “to hail” (HALOT 154 s.v. I ברד). In this case one might translate, “and it hails when the forest is destroyed” (cf. KJV, ASV, NASB, NIV). Perhaps the text alludes to a powerful wind and hail storm that knocks down limbs and trees. Some prefer to emend the form to וְיָרַד (v�yarad), “and it descends,” which provides better, though not perfect, symmetry with the parallel line (cf. NAB). Perhaps וּבָרַד should be dismissed as dittographic. In this case the statement (“when the forest descends”) lacks a finite verb and seems incomplete, but perhaps it is subordinate to v. 20.
notes.1399: (tn, Heb): “and in humiliation the city is laid low.”

rashi.heb:
*וברד ברדת היער.* 
על כרחך אין ברד זה שם דבר שהרי נקוד חציו קמץ וחציו פתח בל' פעל וכן פתרונו ל' פעולה כמו ורחץ וישב ועמד, וברד ויברוד את ברידת היער ויהי' הבי"ת של ברדת מן יסוד כמו עטרת עקרת כלומ' וימטיר הקב"ה את מטר פחי הרשעים שהם עכשיו בנויים ומלאים ערים כיער:
rashi.eng: *And He shall hail down the hailing of the forest.* (וּבָרַד בְּרֶדֶתהַיָּעַר) Perforce, this word וּבָרָד is not a noun, since half of it is vowelized with a ‘kamatz’ and half of it with a ‘pattah’ in an expression of פָּעַל. (Rashi distinguishes בָּרַד from בָּרָד, the noun denoting hail.) And so is its interpretation, an expression of an action, like ‘and he shall wash’ (וְרָחַץ), ‘and he shall sit’ (וְיָשַׁב), ‘and he shall stand’ (וְעָמַד). Here too, וּבָרַד ‘and He shall hail down the hailing of the forest.’ Then the ‘beth’ of בְּרֶדֶת is a radical, like עֲטֶרֶת, ‘a crown,’ עֲקֶרֶת ‘a barren woman.’ That is to say that the Holy One, blessed be He, shall rain down the rain of the coals of the wicked, those who are now built up and full of cities like a forest.

rashi.heb:
*ובשפלה.* 
שנשפלו ישראל עד עכשיו:
rashi.eng: *and into the low state.* Into which Israel has been humbled until now.

rashi.heb:
*תשפל העיר.* 
מטרפולין של פרס ודוגמא כן תרגם יונתן ויחות ברדא ויקטול משריית עממיא:
rashi.eng: *shall the city be humbled.* shall the metropolis of Persia (Seir, Edom, [according to various mss.]) be humbled. In a similar manner did Jonathan render it: And hail will come down and kill the camps of the nations.

notes.1401: (tn, Heb): “who set free the foot of the ox and donkey”; NIV “letting your cattle and donkeys range free.” This verse seems to anticipate a time when fertile land is available to cultivate and crops are so abundant that the farm animals can be allowed to graze freely.

rashi.heb:
*אשריכם.* 
ישראל, שהצליחה זריעת צדקתכם כזורעים על מים מעתה תקצרו ותאספו תבואת שכרכם הטוב תשלחו רגל השור לדוש התבואה והחמור להביא אל הבית כך ת"י כלומר תקבלו שכר פעולתכם הטובה:
rashi.eng: *Fortunate are you.* Israel, that the sowing of your righteousness has succeeded like those who sow by all waters. From now on, you shall reap and gather the grain of your good reward; you shall send forth the feet of the ox to thresh the grain, and the donkey to bring it into the house. So did Jonathan render it: You shall receive the reward of your good work.

notes.1402: (tn, Heb): “Woe [to] the destroyer.” In this context “the destroyer” appears to refer collectively to the hostile nations (vv. 3-4). Assyria would probably have been primary in the minds of the prophet and his audience.
notes.1403: (tn, Heb): “and the deceitful one”; NAB, NIV “O traitor”; NRSV “you treacherous one.” In the parallel structure הוֹי (hoy, “woe [to]”) does double duty.
notes.1404: (tc): The form in the Hebrew text appears to derive from an otherwise unattested verb נָלָה (nalah). The translation follows the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa in reading ככלתך, a Piel infinitival form from the verbal root כָּלָה (kalah), meaning “finish.”

rashi.heb:
*הוי.* 
האויב שאתה שודד תמיד ואתה לא שדוד ובוגד אתה תמיד ואין אדם בוגדך ובוזזך:
rashi.eng: *Woe.* To the enemy, that you constantly spoil, but you are not spoiled, and you constantly deal treacherously, but no man deals treacherously with you or spoils you.

rashi.heb:
*כהתימך.* 
להיות שודד ככלותך שדידתך באותם שנגזרה גזרה עליהם להיות שדודים על ידך תושד:
rashi.eng: *when you finish.* being a spoiler, when you finish your spoiling of those upon whom it was decreed to be spoiled by you, you shall be spoiled.

rashi.heb:
*כנלותך לבגוד.* 
מנחם חיבר כנלותך עם לא יטה לארץ מנלם בחלק אחד ומנלם המ"ם הראשונה בו יסוד נופל כמו מ"ם של מאמר ושל מדע ויתכן להיות ל' כליון לפי הענין:
rashi.eng: *when you finish dealing treacherously.* (כַּנְּלֹתְךָ) Menahem classified כַּנְלֹתְךָ with (Job 15:29) “And their destruction (מִנְלָם) shall not fall to the earth,” in one group (Machbereth Menahem, p. 123). In the word מִנְלָם, the first ‘mem’ is a radical which sometimes is absent, like the ‘mem’ of מַאֲמָר, a statement, and of מַדָּע, knowledge, and it is possibly an expression of ending, according to the context.

rashi.heb:
*כנלותך.* 
ל' ככלותך ולא יטה לארץ מנלם כליון הנגזר עליהם לא יטה לארץ להיות בטל והולך אלא הולך וחזק:
rashi.eng: *when you finish .* כַּנְּלֹתְךָ is an expression of ‘when you finish.’“And מִנְלָם shall not fall to the earth,” the destruction decreed upon them shall not fall to the earth to become progressively void, but will become progressively stronger.

notes.1405: (tn, Heb): “Be their arm each morning.” “Arm” is a symbol for strength. The mem suffixed to the noun has been traditionally understood as a third person suffix, but this is contrary to the context, where the people speak of themselves in the first person. The mem (מ) is probably enclitic with ellipsis of the pronoun, which can be supplied from the context. See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:589, n. 1.
notes.1406: (tn, Heb): “[Be] also our deliverance in the time of distress.”

rashi.heb:
*היה זרועם.* 
של שדודים ביד השודד:
rashi.eng: *Be their arm.* of the spoiled ones in the hand of the spoiler. (Note that we followed other editions of Rashi. Nach Lublin is erroneous in this passage.)

rashi.heb:
*לבקרים.* 
מדי יום יום כשהוא מיצר להם אף ישועתינו תהיה בעת צרה:
rashi.eng: *every morning.* Daily, when they are in straits, also You be our salvation in time of trouble.

notes.1407: (tn, Heb): “at the sound of tumult the nations run away.”
notes.1408: (tn, Heb): “because of your exaltation the nations scatter.”

rashi.heb:
*מקול המון.* 
הבא מלפניך נדדו עמים עד הנה כשהפלאת לנו נסיך:
rashi.eng: *From the sound of roaring.* that emanated from before You, peoples wandered until here when You performed wondrous miracles for us.

notes.1409: (tn): The pronoun is plural; the statement is addressed to the nations who have stockpiled plunder from their conquests of others.
notes.1410: (tn, Heb): “and your plunder is gathered, the gathering of the locust.”
notes.1411: (tn, Heb): “like a swarm of locusts swarming on it.”

rashi.heb:
*ואוסף שללכם.* 
זה מוסב על כנלותך לבגוד יבגדו בך ואוסף שללכם אתם הבוגדים את עמי בבא פקודתכם יבוז אתכם שארית עמי ויאספו שללכם כאסיפת חסיל שאוסף לו תבואה בקיץ כל א' לעצמו אף כאן יבוזו איש לו:
rashi.eng: *And your booty shall be gathered.* This refers back to “when you finish dealing treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with you,” and your booty, you, who spoil My people, when your reckoning comes, the remnant of My people shall plunder you and gather your booty like the gathering of locusts, each one of whom gathers grain for himself in summer; here too, each one will plunder for himself.

rashi.heb:
*כמשק גבים שוקק.* 
כקול נהם מים הנאספים ונופלין בגבים בנהם כן ינהמו הבאים לשלול ולבוז, משק ל' נהם כמו (משלי כ״ח:ט״ו) ארי נוהם ודוב שוקק, וכן ממשק חרול (צפניה ב׳:ט׳) כשהרוח מנשבת בחרולים והם מכים זה על זה נותנים קול וכן בעיר ישוקו (יואל ב):
rashi.eng: *like the roaring of the cisterns.* Like the sound of the roar of water gathering and falling into the cisterns in the river, so will those coming to plunder and pillage, roar. מַשַּׁק is an expression of roaring. Comp. (Prov. 28:15) “A roaring lion and a growling (שׁוֹקֵק) bear.” Also (Zeph. 2:9), “The noise (מִמְשַׁק) of the thorns.” When the wind blows on the thorns, and they knock against one another, they produce a sound. Comp. also, (Joel 2:9) “In the city they roar (יָשֹׁקּוּ).”

rashi.heb:
*גבים.* 
כמו לחשוף מים מגבא ורבותינו דרשוהו באגדת חלק בביזת אוכלוסי סנחרב:
rashi.eng: *cisterns.* (גֵּבִים) like (supra 30:14) “or to scoop water from a cistern (מִגֶּבֶא).” Our Sages expounded it in the Aggadah of Chapter Chelek (San. 94b) as referring to the booty of Sennacherib’s soldiers.

notes.1414: (tn, Heb): “on high” (so KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV); CEV “in the heavens.”

rashi.heb:
*כי שוכן מרום.* 
הראה גבורתו שהוא רם על כל וידו על העליונה:
rashi.eng: *for He dwells on high.* He demonstrated His might, that He is exalted above all, and He has the upper hand.

notes.1415: (tn, Heb): “and he is the stability of your times.”
notes.1416: (tn, Heb): “a rich store of deliverance, wisdom, and knowledge.”
notes.1417: (tn, Heb): “the fear of the Lord, it is his treasure.”

rashi.heb:
*והיה אמונת עתיך וגו'.* 
והיה לחוסן ישועות ולחכמה ודעת את אשר תאמין לבוראך עתים שקבע לך לתרומות ולמעשרות בעת הפרשתן ללקט שכחה ופיאה בעתם לקיים שמיטין ויובלות בעתם ד"א:
rashi.eng: *And the faith of your times, etc..* And it shall be for you for strength of salvations and for wisdom and knowledge, that you will be faithful to your Creator concerning the times that He set for you for terumoth and tithes at the time of their separation, for gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field in their time, to leave them over for the poor, to keep release years and jubilee years in their time. Another explanation is:

rashi.heb:
*אמונת עתך.* 
את שהאמנת בהקב"ה בעתים שעברו עליך וצפית לישועה תהיה לך לחוסן:
rashi.eng: *faith of your times.* What you believed in the Holy One, blessed be He, in times that passed over you, and you hoped for salvation, shall become your strength.

rashi.heb:
*יראת ה'.* 
שתירא מלפניו היא אוצר טוב להפתח לך מאתו על ידה:
rashi.eng: *fear of the Lord.* That you shall fear Him - that is a good treasure to open up for you from before Him.

notes.1418: (tn): The meaning of the Hebrew word is unknown. Proposals include “heroes” (cf. KJV, ASV “valiant ones”; NASB, NIV “brave men”); “priests,” “residents [of Jerusalem].” The present translation assumes that the term is synonymous with “messengers of peace,” with which it corresponds in the parallel structure of the verse.
notes.1419: (tn, Heb): “messengers of peace,” apparently those responsible for negotiating the agreements that have been broken (see v. 8).

rashi.heb:
*הן אראלם צעקו חוצה.* 
היה הנביא מתנבא נחמות ואומר שהפורענות כבר אכלוהו ומעתה אקום ואנשא לגאלם, הן על אראלים שלהם הוא המזבח כבר צעקו וספדו בחוצותם וברחובות' בבכי ונהי:
rashi.eng: *Behold [for] their altar they have cried in the street.* The prophet was prophesying consolations and saying that the retribution had already been completed, and from now I will rise and exalt Myself to redeem them. Behold for their Arel - that is the altar (see above 29:1) - they have already cried and lamented in their streets and in their squares with weeping and wailing.

rashi.heb:
*מלאכי שלום.* 
מלאכי שליחותם שהיו רגילין לבשר שלום מר יבכיון ואומרים נשמו מסילות שבת עובר אורח:
rashi.eng: *ambassadors of peace.* And the ambassadors whom they send, who were wont to bring tidings of peace, cry bitterly and say, “Highways have become desolate, the wayfarer has stopped.”

notes.1421: (tn, Heb): “the one passing by on the road ceases.”
notes.1422: (tn, Heb): “one breaks a treaty”; NAB “Covenants are broken.”
notes.1423: (tc): The Hebrew text reads literally, “he despises cities.” The term עָרִים (’arim, “cities”) is probably a corruption of an original עֵדִים (’edim, “[legal] witnesses”), a reading that is preserved in the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa. Confusion of dalet (ד) and resh (ר) is a well-attested scribal error.
notes.1424: (tn, Heb): “he does not regard human beings.”

rashi.heb:
*הפר.* 
האויב ברית שכרת לישראל:
rashi.eng: *he has abrogated the treaty.* The enemy has abrogated the treaty he made with Israel.

rashi.heb:
*מאס ערים.* 
ביזה בעיניו כל שונא אינו חושב אנוש:
rashi.eng: *despised cities.* He despised in his eyes; no enemy considers any man.

notes.1426: (tn): Or “mourns” (BDB 5 s.v. I אָבַל). HALOT 6-7 lists homonyms I אבל (“mourn”) and II אבל (“dry up”). They propose the second here on the basis of parallelism. See 24:4.
notes.1427: (tn, Heb): “Lebanon is ashamed.” The Hiphil is exhibitive, expressing the idea, “exhibits shame.” In this context the statement alludes to the withering of vegetation.
notes.1428: (sn): Sharon was a fertile plain along the Mediterranean coast. See 35:2.
notes.1430: (sn): Both of these areas were known for their trees and vegetation. See 2:13; 35:2.
notes.1431: (tn, Heb): “shake off [their leaves]” (so ASV, NRSV); NAB “are stripped bare.”

rashi.heb:
*אבל.* 
ל' אבילות:
rashi.eng: *mourns.* (אָבֵל) an expression of mourning.

rashi.heb:
*קמל.* 
יבש ונכרת:
rashi.eng: *it was cut off.* Dried and cut off.

rashi.heb:
*היה.* 
ל' עבר הוא:
rashi.eng: *became.* (הָיָה, lit. was.) This is the past tense.

rashi.heb:
*השרון.* 
שם מחוז מרעה בהמות כמו ששנינו אילים ממואב עגלים משרון:
rashi.eng: *the Sharon.* The name of a region of pasture for animals, as we learned (Men. 87a): Rams from Moab, calves from Sharon.

rashi.heb:
*כערבה.* 
חורבה:
rashi.eng: *like the plain.* a ruin.

rashi.heb:
*ונוער.* 
ל' תשנוק כמו (שמות יד) וינער ה':
rashi.eng: *have become emptied.* (וְנֹעֵר) An expression of shaking out. Comp. (Ex. 14:27): “And the Lord shook (וַיְנַעֵר).”

notes.1432: (tn): Or “lift myself up” (KJV); NLT “show my power and might.”

rashi.heb:
*עתה אקום.* 
מרוב רעות שעשה האויב לעמי לא אתאפק עוד עתה אקו' וארומם ואנשא:
rashi.eng: *Now I will rise.* Because of the many evils the enemy perpetrated against My people, I will no longer restrain Myself; now I will rise, be raised and be exalted.

notes.1433: (tn): The second person verb and pronominal forms in this verse are plural. The hostile nations are the addressed, as the next verse makes clear.
notes.1434: (sn): The hostile nations’ plans to destroy God’s people will come to nothing; their hostility will end up being self-destructive.

rashi.heb:
*חשש.* 
מין מוץ דבר שנוח לידלק:
rashi.eng: *chaff.* (חֲשַׁשׁ) a kind of chaff, something that is easily ignited.

rashi.heb:
*רוחכם אש.* 
מגופכם תצא רוח אש ותאכל החשש והקש:
rashi.eng: *your breath is fire.* From your body shall emanate breath of fire and will consume the chaff and the stubble.

notes.1435: (tn, Heb): “will be a burning to lime.” See Amos 2:1.

rashi.heb:
*כסוחים.* 
קצוצים, כסוחים כמו (ויקרא כה, ד) לא תזמר ת"א לא תכסח:
rashi.eng: *severed.* (כְּסוּחִים) Comp. (Lev. 25:4) “You shall not prune.” Onkelos renders: לָא תִכְסָח.

rashi.heb:
*רחוקים.* 
המאמינים בי ועושים רצוני מנעוריהם:
rashi.eng: *you far-off ones.* Those who believe in Me and do My will from their youth.

rashi.heb:
*קרובים.* 
בעלי תשובה שנתקרבו אלי מחדש:
rashi.eng: *you near ones.* Repentant sinners who have recently drawn near to Me.

notes.1436: (tn): Or “trembling” (ASV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NLT “shake with fear.”
notes.1437: (tn): Or “the defiled”; TEV “The sinful people of Zion”; NLT “The sinners in Jerusalem.”
notes.1438: (tn): The words “they say” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.1439: (tn): Or “perpetual”; or “everlasting” (KJV, ASV, NAB, NIV, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*פחדו בציון חטאים.* 
היאך ימצאו פתח לתשובה:
rashi.eng: *Sinners in Zion were afraid.* How they would find an opening to repent.

rashi.heb:
*מי יגור לנו אש אוכלה.* 
כלומר מי יעמוד בעדנו לשכך חימה בוערת, ל"א מי יגור לנו פי' מי הוא לנו שיגור בציון עם הצור שהוא אש אוכלה והוא משיב אוהב צדקות וגו':
rashi.eng: *Who will stand up for us against a consuming fire?.* (lit., Who will live for us a consuming fire?) I.e., who will stand up for us to appease burning wrath? Alternatively, who among us will dwell, i.e., who among us will dwell in Zion with the Rock, Who is a consuming fire? And he replies, “He who walks righteously, etc.”

notes.1442: (tn, Heb): “[who] shakes off his hands from grabbing hold of a bribe.”
notes.1443: (tn, Heb): “[who] shuts his ear from listening to bloodshed.”
notes.1444: (tn, Heb): “[who] closes his eyes from seeing evil.”

rashi.heb:
*הולך צדקות.* 
מי הוא ימצא הולך צדקות:
rashi.eng: *He who walks righteously.* Who will be found? One who walks righteously.

rashi.heb:
*נוער כפיו.* 
אשקו"ט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *who shakes his hands.* (eskot in O.F.).

rashi.heb:
*אוטם.* 
סותם וכן שקופים אטומים (מלכי' א ו'):
rashi.eng: *closes his ear.* (אֹטֵם) Comp. (I Kings 6:4) “transparent but closed (אֲטֻמִים).”

rashi.heb:
*עוצם.* 
סוגר וכן (לעיל כט) ויעצם את עיניכם:
rashi.eng: *and closes.* (וְעֹצֵם) Comp. (supra 29:10) “And He has closed (וַיְעַצֵּם) your eyes.”

notes.1445: (tn, Heb): “he [in the] exalted places will live.”
notes.1446: (tn, Heb): “mountain strongholds, cliffs [will be] his elevated place.”

rashi.heb:
*לחמו נתן.* 
לא יהא מבקש לחם כי מן השמים יספיקו לו מזון:
rashi.eng: *his bread shall be given.* He will not seek bread, for it will be supplied to him from heaven.

rashi.heb:
*מימיו נאמנים.* 
מקור מימיו לא יכזב, כלומר זרעו יגדל וכל צרכיו יסופקו:
rashi.eng: *his water sure.* The source of his water will not fail. I.e., his seed will become great, and all his wants will be supplied.

notes.1447: (tn, Heb): “your eyes will see a king in his beauty”; NIV, NRSV “the king.”
notes.1448: (tn, Heb): “a land of distances,” i.e., an extensive land.

rashi.heb:
*מלך ביפיו תחזינה עיניך.* 
פי' תזכה לראות מארץ מרחקים מלכך בהדר גאונו, או פי' (הקב"ה שהוא מלך אותו תחזה מארץ מרחקים שאתה עומד תראה הניסים והגדולה שאעשה לך ועם נועז עמקי שפה לא יראה שכינת המלך ביפיו ע"כ, כל זה בספרים אחרים אינו):
rashi.eng: *The King in His beauty shall your eyes behold.* (The Holy One, blessed be He, Who is a King, Him you shall see from a distant land where you are standing. You shall see the miracles and the greatness that I will perform for you, and a people of a strange tongue, of obscure speech, shall not see the Shechinah of the King in His beauty. [This does not appear in many editions.])

rashi.heb:
*מלך ביפיו תחזינה עיניך.* 
לך הצדיק אני אומר שתזכה לראות זיו שכינתו של מקום:
rashi.eng: *The King in His beauty shall your eyes behold.*  To you, O righteous man, I say that you shall merit to see the splendor of the Shechinah of the Omnipresent.

rashi.heb:
*תראינה ארץ מרחקים.* 
תירגם יונתן תסתכל ותחזי בנחתי ארע גיהנם:
rashi.eng: *they shall see [from] a distant land.* Jonathan renders: You shall look and see those who go down to the land of Gehinnom.

notes.1449: (tn, Heb): “your heart will meditate on terror.”
notes.1450: (tn): The words “and you will ask yourselves” are supplied in the translation for clarification and stylistic reasons.
notes.1451: (sn): The people refer to various Assyrian officials who were responsible for determining the amount of taxation or tribute Judah must pay to the Assyrian king.

rashi.heb:
*לבך יהגה אימה.* 
כשתראה השרים והחכמים של עכו"ם שהיו שליטים בחייהן והרי הם נידונים בגיהנם יהגה לבך אימה ותאמר איה חכמתן וגדולתן של אלו איה שהיה סופר בחייו ושוקל כל דבר חכמה שהיו שואלין ממנו כל עצת מלכות:
rashi.eng: *Your heart shall meditate [in] fear.* When you see the princes and the savants of the heathens, who ruled during their lifetime, and who are now being judged in Gehinnom, your heart will meditate in terror, and you will say, "Where is the wisdom and the greatness of these men? Where is the one who, during his lifetime, would count and weigh every word of wisdom, for they would ask him every counsel of the kingdom?

rashi.heb:
*איה סופר את המגדלים.* 
פירוש שהיה סופר המגדלים אשר בעיר ועיר כי אותם הבתים הגבוהים היו חשובים ונותנים יותר במס וכל אותה המחשבה והפחד לא יהיה לך עוד:
rashi.eng: *Where is he who counts the towers.* This too is a matter of the kingdom. He is appointed over the houses of the kingdom, how many they are, and how many towers a certain city requires. Comp. (Ps. 48:13) “Encircle Zion and surround it, count its towers,” how many towers it requires.

notes.1452: (tn): The Hebrew form נוֹעָז (no’az) is a Niphal participle derived from יָעַז (ya’az, an otherwise unattested verb) or from עָזָז (’azaz, “be strong,” unattested elsewhere in the Niphal). Some prefer to emend the form to לוֹעֵז (lo’ez) which occurs in Ps 114:1 with the meaning “speak a foreign language.” See HALOT 809 s.v. עזז, 533 s.v. לעז. In this case, one might translate “people who speak a foreign language.”
notes.1453: (tn, Heb): “a people too deep of lip to hear.” The phrase “deep of lip” must be an idiom meaning “lips that speak words that are unfathomable [i.e., incomprehensible].”
notes.1454: (tn, Heb): “derision of tongue there is no understanding.” The Niphal of לָעַג (la’ag) occurs only here. In the Qal and Hiphil the verb means “to deride, mock.” A related noun is used in 28:11.

rashi.heb:
*את עם נועז.* 
כמו לועז אלו אשור ובבל שאין לשונם לשון הקודש:
rashi.eng: *A people of a strange tongue.* (נוֹעָז) like לוֹעֵז. These are all the heathens, whose language is not the holy tongue. ([Other editions read:] These are Assyria and Babylon, whose language is not the holy tongue.) ([Manuscripts read:] These are all the nations whose language is not the holy tongue.)

rashi.heb:
*לא תראה.* 
לא תחשוב בלבך כי כולם יהיו חשכים ושפלים:
rashi.eng: *you shall not see.* You shall not esteem in your heart, for they shall all be dark and humble.

rashi.heb:
*עמקו שפה.* 
כמו ויהי כל הארץ שפה אחת (בראשית י״א:א׳):
rashi.eng: *speech… obscure.* (שָׂפָה, lit. lip.) Comp. (Gen. 11:1) “And all the land was one speech (שָׂפָה).”

rashi.heb:
*נלעג לשון.* 
עגלים, ועמקי שפה (לעיל כג) כל זה לשון נכרית שאינן מכירין בלשון הקודש:
rashi.eng: *of stammering tongue.* (נִלְעָג לָשׁוֹן). Comp. (32:4) “The tongue of the stammerers (לְשׁוֹן עִלְּגִים),” (and of obscure speech. All this is a foreign language, for they do not understand the holy tongue.)

notes.1456: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.1457: (tn): Or “that does not travel”; NASB “which shall not be folded.”

rashi.heb:
*חזה ציון.* 
ואת מי תראה בלבך להחשב מלוכה ושררה את ציון אשר היא קרית בית וועד לנו:
rashi.eng: *See Zion.* But whom will you see in your heart to be regarded as a kingdom and a ruling power? Zion, which is the city of our meeting place.

rashi.heb:
*בל יצען.* 
בל יסח ודומה לו אילון בצעננים (שופטי' ד') ומתרג' מישר אגניא והם נקעי' שבשדו' שקורין פושי"ץ בלע"ז כמו אגני דארעא מקרי שהמים נאספי' שם מן ההרי' והגבשושיו' ובי"ת של בצעננים אומר אני שאינה נשרשת בתבה אלא משמשת היא:
rashi.eng: *that shall not fall.* (יִצְעָן) shall not be lowered. Comp. (Jud. 4:11) “Elon-bezaanannim (אֵלוֹן בְּצַעֲנַנִּים),” which is rendered as: the plain of pits (מִישׁוֹר אַגְנַיָּא), which are pits in the fields, called kombes in O.F. Comp. (Baba Kamma 61b) “The pits of the earth (אַגְנֵי דְאַרְעָא) they are considered,” where water gathers from the mountains and the hills. I believe that the ‘beth’ of the word בְּצַעֲנַנִּים is not radical, but is a prefix.

rashi.heb:
*בל יסע יתדותיו.* 
היתדות שקושרין בו מיתרי האהל בל יסע אותם מן הארץ ממקום תקיעתם כמו ויסיעו אבנים גדולות (מלכים א ה׳:ל״א) וכן ויסעם עם הבריח (שופטים ט״ז:ג׳) ל' תלישה:
rashi.eng: *whose pegs shall never be moved.* (יִסַּע) The pegs with which they tie the ropes of the tent he shall not move them from the earth, from the place into which they are thrust. Comp. (I Kings 5:31) “And they quarried (וַיַּסִּעוּ) great stones.” Also (Jud. 16:3), “And he plucked them (וַיִּסּעֵם) together with the bolt,” an expression of uprooting.

notes.1458: (tn, Heb): “But there [as] a mighty one [will be] the Lord for us.”
notes.1459: (tn, Heb): “a place of rivers, streams wide of hands [i.e., on both sides].”
notes.1460: (tn, Heb): “a ship of rowing will not go into it.”
notes.1461: (tn, Heb): “and a mighty ship will not pass through it.”

rashi.heb:
*כי אם שם.* 
כי אם מוסב על בל יסע יתדותיו ועל בל ינתקו, הרעה לא תהיה כי אם הטובה ה' יהיה שם אדיר לנו והעיר תהיה מקום נהרים יאורים כענין שנא' (ביחזקאל ד) וימד אלף ויעבירני נחל אשר לא אוכל לעבור וכן ניבא יואל ומעין מבית ה' יצא (יואל ד יח) והוא הנחל שיהא מתגבר והולך:
rashi.eng: *But there.* ‘But’ refers back to ‘whose pegs shall never be moved,’ and ‘shall not be torn.’ The evil shall not be, only the good. There the Lord shall be mighty for us, and the city shall be a place of rivers and streams, in the manner it is said in Ezekiel (47:4): “And He measured a thousand (cubits), and He led me… a stream that I could not cross.” And so did Joel prophesy (4:18) “And a spring shall emanate from the house of the Lord,” that it shall become progressively stronger.

rashi.heb:
*אני שיט.* 
אניה השטה במים:
rashi.eng: *a galley with oars.* a ship that floats on the water.

rashi.heb:
*וצי אדיר.* 
ובורני רבתא:
rashi.eng: *and a great ship.* (וְצִי אַדִּיר) and a great ship [from Jonathan].

rashi.heb:
*כי ה' שופטינו.* 
שר ושופט שלנו:
rashi.eng: *For the Lord is our judge.* Our prince and judge.

notes.1462: (tn): The words “though at this time” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The first half of the verse is addressed to Judah and contrasts the nation’s present weakness with its future prosperity. Judah is compared to a ship that is incapable of sailing.
notes.1463: (tn, Heb): “they do not fasten the base of their mast.” On כֵּן (ken, “base”) see BDB 487 s.v. III כֵּן and HALOT 483 s.v. III כֵּן.
notes.1465: (tn, Heb): “then there will be divided up loot of plunder [in] abundance.”
notes.1466: (sn): Judah’s victory over its enemies will be so thorough there will be more than enough plunder for everyone, even slow-moving lame men who would normally get left out in the rush to gather the loot.

rashi.heb:
*נטשו חבליך.* 
המושכים את הספינה את רומי החייבת:
rashi.eng: *Your ropes.* that draw the ship, you sinful city. ([Mss. yield:] you, sinful Rome.)

rashi.heb:
*כן.* 
הכן היטב:
rashi.eng: *properly.* prepared well.

rashi.heb:
*תרנם.* 
תורן הספינה:
rashi.eng: *a sail.* Heb. נס, the sail of a ship.

rashi.heb:
*בל פרשו נס.* 
לא יוכלו לפרוס וילון המנהיג את הספינה:
rashi.eng: *they did not spread out a sail.* They will not be able to spread the sail that guides the boat.

rashi.heb:
*אז חולק עד שלל.* 
עדאה:
rashi.eng: *then plunder [and] booty were divided.* (עד) related to עֲדָאָה, plunder, in Aramaic.

rashi.heb:
*מרבה.* 
הרבה יחלקו שלל סנחריב:
rashi.eng: *by many.* Many will divide the plunder of the heathens. ([Mss. yield:] the plunder of Edom.) ([Others:] the nations.) ([Still others:] Sennacherib.)

rashi.heb:
*פסחים.* 
(ישראל) שהיו עד עכשיו חלשים:
rashi.eng: *lame.* Israel, who were weak until now.

notes.1467: (tn): The words “of Zion” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*ובל יאמר שכן.* 
של ישראל:
rashi.eng: *And the neighbor shall not say.* (I.e., the neighbor of) Israel.

rashi.heb:
*חליתי.* 
בשביל האומה הזאת באתני הרעה כי:
rashi.eng: *“I am sick”.* Because of this nation, this misfortune has befallen me, for

rashi.heb:
*העם.* 
ישראל שנקראו עם היושב בירושלים יהיה סלוח עון:
rashi.eng: *The people.* Israel, who is called a people, that dwells in Jerusalem, shall be forgiven of sin.

notes.1468: (tn, Heb): “the world and its offspring”; NASB “the world and all that springs from it.”

notes.1469: (tn, Heb): “will be cast aside”; NASB, NIV “thrown out.”
notes.1470: (tn, Heb): “[as for] their corpses, their stench will arise.”
notes.1471: (tn, Heb): “hills will dissolve from their blood.”

notes.1472: (tc, Heb): “and all the host of heaven will rot.” The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa inserts “and the valleys will be split open,” but this reading may be influenced by Mic 1:4. On the other hand, the statement, if original, could have been omitted by homoioarcton, a scribe’s eye jumping from the conjunction prefixed to “the valleys” to the conjunction prefixed to the verb “rot.”
notes.1473: (tn, Heb): “like the withering of a leaf from a vine, and like the withering from a fig tree.”

rashi.heb:
*ונמקו כל צבא השמים.* 
יפחדו כשאשליך את שרי אשור ובבל:
rashi.eng: *And all the host of heaven shall melt.* They shall be frightened when I cast down the princes of the heathens.([Mss. yield:] the princes of the nations.) ([Warsaw edition:] of Assyria and Babylon.)

rashi.heb:
*ונגולו.* 
ל' גולל ונגלו כספר השמים ת"י ויתמחון מתחות שמיא כמא דאמר עליהן בסיפרא ואני מפרשו לפי הענין מפני שעכשיו הטובה והאורה לרשעים לכשיתמחו ויחרבו יהיה דומם העולם חשך עליהם כאילו נגלל השמש והאור כגלילת ספר:
rashi.eng: *shall be rolled.* (וְנָגֹלּוּ) an expression of rolling. And the heavens shall be rolled like a scroll. Jonathan renders: And they shall be erased from beneath the heavens, as it is stated about them in the Book. But I explain it according to the context, for now, the kingdoms of the Ishmaelites (the nations [ms.]) (the wicked [Warsaw ed.]) have fortune and light. When they are erased and destroyed, it will be as though the world has darkened for them, as though the sun and the light are rolled up like the rolling of a scroll.

rashi.heb:
*יבול.* 
יכמוש:
rashi.eng: *withers.* (יִבּוֹל) withers.

rashi.heb:
*וכנובלת מתאנה.* 
כמושה באילן קרויה נובלת וזהו שפירשו רבותינו (ברכות מ) מאי נובלות בושלי כומרא שנתבשלו בכומר לאחר לקיטתן צוברן ומתחממות ומתבשלות:
rashi.eng: *and as a withered [fig] from a fig tree.* The withered fruit of a tree is called נוֹבְלוֹת. This is what our Rabbis (Ber. 40b) explained: What are ‘noveloth’? Fruit ripened in the heater, that become ripe in the heater. After they are picked, he gathers them and they become heated and ripen.

notes.1474: (tn): The words “he says” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The Lord speaks at this point.
notes.1475: (tn, Heb): “indeed [or “for”] my sword is drenched in the heavens.” The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa has תראה (“[my sword] appeared [in the heavens]”), but this is apparently an attempt to make sense out of a difficult metaphor. Cf. NIV “My sword has drunk its fill in the heavens.” In v. 4 the “host of the heaven” refers to the heavenly luminaries (stars and planets, see, among others, Deut 4:19; 17:3; 2 Kgs 17:16; 21:3, 5; 23:4-5; 2 Chr 33:3, 5) that populate the divine/heavenly assembly in mythological and prescientific Israelite thought (see Job 38:7; Isa 14:13). As in 24:21, they are viewed here as opposing God and being defeated in battle.
notes.1476: (sn): Edom is mentioned here as epitomizing the hostile nations that oppose God.

rashi.heb:
*כי רותה בשמים חרבי.* 
להרוג שרים של מעלה ואחר כך תרד על עמלק למטה שאין כל אומה לוקה עד שילקה שר שלה במרום:
rashi.eng: *For My sword has become sated in the heaven.* To slay the heavenly princes, and afterward it shall descend on the nation Ishmael ([mss. and Kli Paz:] Edom) ([Warsaw ed.:] Babylonians) below, for no nation suffers until its prince suffers in heaven.

rashi.heb:
*עם חרמי.* 
עם מלחמתי ל' משנה (כתובות יז) בשעת חירום שנו וכן (מלכים א כ׳:מ״ב) את איש חרמי דאחאב:
rashi.eng: *the nation with whom I contend.* (עַם חֶרמִי), the nation with whom I battle. This is a Mishnaic expression: (Keth. 17b) They taught this in connection with time of strife (חֵרוּם). Comp. (I Kings 20:42) “The man with whom I contend (אִישׁ חֶרְמִי),” referring to Ahab.

notes.1477: (tn): The verb is a rare Hotpaal passive form. See GKC 150 �54.h.
notes.1478: (tn): The words “it drips” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.1479: (tn): The words “and is covered” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.1480: (tn, Heb): “for there is a sacrifice to the Lord.”
notes.1481: (sn): The Lord’s judgment of Edom is compared to a bloody sacrificial scene.
notes.1482: (tn, Heb): “great” (so KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*כרים עתודים.* 
שרים ושלטונים:
rashi.eng: *lambs and goats.* princes and governors.

rashi.heb:
*בבצרה.* 
מארץ מואב היא אבל לפי שהעמידה מלך לאדום שנאמר וימת חושם וימלוך תחתיו יובב בן זרח מבצרה (בראשית לו) לפיכך תלקה עמהם, בפסיקתא:
rashi.eng: *in Bozrah.* It is from the land of Moab, but since it supplied a king for Edom, as it is stated (Gen. 36:33): “And Jobab son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead,” it will, therefore, suffer with them. This is found in Pesikta.

notes.1483: (tn, Heb): “will go down”; NAB “shall be struck down.”
notes.1484: (tn, Heb): “and bulls along with strong ones.” Perhaps this refers to the leaders.

rashi.heb:
*ראמים עמם.* 
עם העתודים הכתובים למעל':
rashi.eng: *wild oxen with them.* Kings with governors, wild oxen with the goats mentioned above.

rashi.heb:
*אבירים.* 
פרים בריאים וגדולי' כמה דאת אמר עם אבירי בשן כתרוני:
rashi.eng: *fat bulls.* (אַבִּירִים) fat and large bulls, as it is stated (Ps. 22:13): “Fat bulls (אַבִּירֵי) of Bashan surrounded me.”

notes.1485: (tn, Heb): “for a day of vengeance [is] for the Lord.”
notes.1486: (tn, Heb): “a year of repayment for the strife of Zion.” The translation assumes that רִיב (riv) refers to Edom’s hostility toward Zion. Another option is to understand רִיב (riv) as referring to the Lord’s taking up Zion’s cause. In this case one might translate, “a time when he will repay Edom and vindicate Zion.”

rashi.heb:
*שלומים לריב ציון.* 
שישלם גמול על עיסקי ריב ציון הצועקת לפניו לשופטה מן המריעים לה:
rashi.eng: *retribution for the plea of Zion.* That He will mete out punishment (lit., pay a reward) for the plea of Zion, who cries before Him to judge her from those who harm her.

notes.1487: (tn, Heb): “her”; the referent (Edom) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ונהפכו נחליה.* 
של בבלים:
rashi.eng: *And its streams shall turn.* (I.e., the streams) of the heathens. ([Mss. yield:] of Edom.)

rashi.heb:
*מדור לדור.* 
מאותו דור עד דור אחרון, ד"א היא קללת משה (שמות י״ז:ט״ז) מלחמה לה' בעמלק מדור דור מדורו של משה לדורו של שאול ומשם לדורו של מרדכי ומשם לדורו של מלך משיחנו:
rashi.eng: *from generation to generation.* From that generation until the last generation. Another explanation is that this is Moses’ curse (Ex. 17:16): “The Lord has a war against Amalek from generation to generation.” From Moses’ generation to Saul’s generation, and from there to Mordecai’s generation, and from there to the generation of the King Messiah.

notes.1489: (tn): קָאַת (qa’at) refers to some type of bird (cf. Lev 11:18; Deut 14:17) that was typically found near ruins (see Zeph 2:14). קִפּוֹד (qippod) may also refer to a type of bird (NAB “hoot owl”; NIV “screech owl”; TEV “ravens”), but some have suggested a rodent may be in view (cf. NCV “small animals”; ASV “porcupine”; NASB, NRSV “hedgehog”).
notes.1491: (tn): The Hebrew text has יַנְשׁוֹף וְעֹרֵב (yanshof v�’orev). Both the יַנְשׁוֹף (“owl”; see Lev 11:17; Deut 14:16) and עֹרֵב (“raven”; Lev 11:15; Deut 14:14) were types of wild birds.
notes.1492: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.1493: (tn, Heb): “stones,” i.e., the stones used in a plumb bob.
notes.1494: (sn): The metaphor in v. 11b emphasizes that God has carefully planned Edom’s demise.

rashi.heb:
*וקפוד.* 
עוף הפורח בלילה צואיט"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *owl.* (קִפֹּד) a bird that flies at night (chouette in French), an owl.

rashi.heb:
*קו תהו.* 
משפט של שממה:
rashi.eng: *a line of waste.* A judgment of desolation.

rashi.heb:
*ואבני בהו.* 
משקלות של דין חורבן כמו (דברים כה) אבן שלמה:
rashi.eng: *and weights of destruction.* Weights of the judgment of destruction. (אַבְנֵי, lit., stones.) Comp. (Deut. 25:15) “a whole weight (אֶבֶן).”

notes.1495: (tn, Heb): “will be nothing”; NCV, TEV, NLT “will all be gone.”

rashi.heb:
*חוריה ואין שם מלוכה יקראו.* 
שרים שלה עומדים ואין אחד מהם קורא על עצמו שם שררה ומלוכה:
rashi.eng: *As for its nobles, there are none who proclaim the kingdom.* Its princes stand, and none of them calls upon himself the name of ruling and kingdom.

rashi.heb:
*אפס.* 
כלייה:
rashi.eng: *nothing.* Destruction.

notes.1496: (tn): The words “will grow” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.1497: (tc, Heb): “and she will be a settlement for wild dogs, a dwelling place for ostriches.” The translation assumes an emendation of חָצִיר (khatsir, “grass”) to חָצֵר (khatser, “settlement”). One of the Qumran scrolls of Isaiah (1QIsaa) supports this emendation (cf. HALOT 344 s.v. II חָצִיר)

rashi.heb:
*ועלתה ארמנותיה סירים.* 
כך דרך חורבות לצמוח בהם קוצים וסנאים והוא קימוש והוא חוח כולם מיני קוצים הם כגון אורטיא"ש וכיוצא בהם:
rashi.eng: *And its palaces shall grow thorns.* So is the nature of ruins to grow thorns and briers, and that is ‘kimosh’ and that is ‘choach’; they are all types of thorns, e.g., ortias, (nettles,) and the like.

rashi.heb:
*נוה תנים.* 
הוא מדבר שהוא דרך להיו' בו תנים שהוא מין חיה רעה:
rashi.eng: *the habitat of jackals.* (תַּנִּים) That is a desert, which is usually frequented by ‘tannim,’ which is a species of wild animal.

notes.1498: (tn, Heb): “will meet” (so NIV); NLT “will mingle there.”
notes.1499: (tn, Heb): “and a goat will call to its neighbor.”
notes.1500: (tn): The precise meaning of לִּילִית (lilit) is unclear, though in this context the word certainly refers to some type of wild animal or bird. The word appears to be related to לַיְלָה (laylah, “night”). Some interpret it as the name of a female night demon, on the basis of an apparent Akkadian cognate used as the name of a demon. Later Jewish legends also identified Lilith as a demon. Cf. NRSV “Lilith.”
notes.1501: (tn, Heb): “and will find for themselves a resting place.”

rashi.heb:
*ופגשו ציים את איים.* 
ויערען תמון בחתולין כך תירגם יונתן תמון נמיו' מרטרינ"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *And martens shall meet cats.* And martens shall meet with cats. In this matter Jonathan rendered it. תַּמְוָן is נִמִּיּוֹת (martrines in O. F.), martens.

rashi.heb:
*ושעיר.* 
שד:
rashi.eng: *and a satyr.* A demon.

rashi.heb:
*הרגיעה.* 
לשון מרגוע:
rashi.eng: *rests.* (הִרְגִּיעָה) an expression related to מַרְגּוֹעַ, rest.

rashi.heb:
*לילית.* 
שם שידה:
rashi.eng: *lilith.* The name of a female demon.

notes.1502: (tn): Hebrew קִפּוֹז (qippoz) occurs only here; the precise meaning of the word is uncertain.
notes.1503: (tn): For this proposed meaning for Hebrew מָלַט (malat), see HALOT 589 s.v. I מלט.
notes.1504: (tn, Heb): “and brood [over them] in her shadow.”
notes.1505: (tn): The precise meaning of דַּיָּה (dayyah) is uncertain, though the term appears to refer to some type of bird of prey, perhaps a vulture.

rashi.heb:
*קננה.* 
לשון קן צפור (דברים כב):
rashi.eng: *has made its nest.* (קִנְּנָה) an expression related to ‘a bird’s nest’ (קַן) (Deut. 22:6).

rashi.heb:
*קפוז.* 
הוא קפוד:
rashi.eng: *owl.* (קִפּוֹז) that is the owl (קִפֹּד).

rashi.heb:
*ותמלט.* 
ותלד ביצה:
rashi.eng: *and she has laid.* She laid eggs.

rashi.heb:
*ובקעה.* 
היא יציאת האפרוחים מן הביצה וכן הוא אומר ביצי צפעוני בקעו (לקמן נט):
rashi.eng: *and hatched.* This is the emerging of the chicks from the egg. Comp. (below 59:5) The eggs of the viper have hatched.

rashi.heb:
*ודגרה.* 
היא קריאת העוף שהעוף קורא בגרונו להמשיך אפרוחים אחריו גלוציי"ר בלע"ז וכן (ירמיה יז) קורא דגר:
rashi.eng: *and gathered.* This is the call that the bird calls with its throat to draw the chicks after it, gloussera in French. Comp. (Jer. 17:11) “A cuckoo gathers (דָגָר) what it did not lay.”

rashi.heb:
*דיות.* 
ולטוייר"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *vultures.* (דַיּוֹת) voltojjrs in O.F.

rashi.heb:
*אשה רעותה.* 
כמו אל רעותה:
rashi.eng: *each one to her friend.* (lit., each one her friend,) like to her friend.

notes.1506: (tn, Heb): “Seek from upon the scroll of the Lord and read.” It is uncertain what particular scroll is referred to here. Perhaps the phrase simply refers to this prophecy and is an admonition to pay close attention to the details of the message.
notes.1507: (tn, Heb): “one from these will not be missing.” הֵנָּה (hennah, “these”) is feminine plural in the Hebrew text. It may refer only to the birds mentioned in v. 15b or may include all of the creatures listed in vv. 14b-15 (all of which are identified with feminine nouns).
notes.1508: (tn, Heb): “each its mate they will not lack.”
notes.1509: (tc): The Hebrew text reads literally, “for a mouth, it has commanded.” The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa and a few medieval mss have פִּיהוּ (pihu, “his mouth [has commanded]”), while a few other medieval mss read פִּי יְהוָה (pi y�hvah, “the mouth of the Lord [has commanded]”).
notes.1510: (tn, Heb): “and his spirit, he gathers them.” The pronominal suffix (“them”) is feminine plural, referring to the birds mentioned in v. 15b or to all of the creatures listed in vv. 14b-15 (all of which are identified with feminine nouns).

rashi.heb:
*דרשו מעל ספר ה'.* 
קראו מעל ספר בראשית כשהביא המבול גזר שיתקבצו כל הבריות להסגר בתיבה זכר ונקבה. אחת מהנה לא נעדרה מלבא על אחת כמה וכמה כשיגזור עליה' זאת ולהקבץ לשתות דם לאכול בשר וחלב:
rashi.eng: *Seek out of the Book of the Lord.* Read out of the Book of Genesis; when He brought the Flood, He decreed that all the creatures gather in the Ark, male and female, and none of them was missing. How much more will this be so when He decrees this upon them, to gather to drink blood and to eat flesh and fat!

rashi.heb:
*לא פקדו.* 
לא חסרו כמו (במדבר ל״א:מ״ט) לא נפקד ממנו איש:
rashi.eng: *did not miss.* (פָקָדוּ) Comp. (Num. 31:49) “Not a man was missing (נִפְקַד) of us.”

rashi.heb:
*כי פי הוא צוה.* 
שיבואו ורוחו של פי הוא קבצן רוחו מוסב על פי כמו (תהילים ל״ג:ו׳) וברוח פיו כל צבאם אף כאן רוחו של פי הוא קבצן :
rashi.eng: *for My mouth it has commanded.* that they come, and the breath of My mouth it gathered them. The antecedent of ‘its breath’ is ‘My mouth.’ Comp. (Ps. 33:6) “And with the breath of His mouth all their host.” Here too, the breath of My mouth it gathered them.

notes.1511: (tn, Heb): “and he causes the lot to fall for them.” Once again the pronominal suffix (“them”) is feminine plural, referring to the birds mentioned in v. 15b or to all of the creatures listed in vv. 14b-15 (all of which are identified with feminine nouns).
notes.1512: (tn, Heb): “and his hand divides for them with a measuring line.” The pronominal suffix (“them”) now switches to masculine plural, referring to all the animals and birds mentioned in vv. 11-15, some of which were identified with masculine nouns. This signals closure for this portion of the speech, which began in v. 11. The following couplet (v. 17b) forms an inclusio with v. 11a through verbal repetition.
notes.1513: (tn, Heb): “will possess it” (so NIV); NCV “they will own that land forever.”

rashi.heb:
*והוא הפיל להן.* 
עכשיו הנביא אומר על הקב"ה והוא הפיל להם לאותן החיות והעופו' גורל שיעלו אלו לחלקם:
rashi.eng: *And He cast… for them.* Now the prophet says concerning the Holy One, blessed be He, “And He cast lots for them,” for all those beasts and fowl, that these shall fall to their share.

notes.1514: (tn): The final mem (ם) on the verb יְשֻׂשׂוּם (y�susum) is dittographic (note the initial mem on the following noun מִדְבָּר [midbar]). The ambiguous verbal form is translated as a jussive because it is parallel to the jussive form תָגֵל (tagel). The jussive is used rhetorically here, not as a literal command or prayer.

rashi.heb:
*ישושום.* 
ישישו עליהם כמו ישושו מהן, כמו בני יצאוני (ירמיהו י׳:כ׳) שפתרונו יצאו ממני וכן בשלם הבשר (מלכים א י״ט:כ״א) בשל להם הבשר:
rashi.eng: *shall rejoice over them.* (יְשֻׂשׂוּם) This is usually the sign of the direct object, inappropriate here in the case of an intransitive verb. (like יָשׂוּשׂוּ מֵהֶם, shall rejoice from them). Comp. (Jer. 10:20) “My sons have gone away from me (יְצָאֻנִי).” Also, (I Kings 19:21) “He cooked the meat for them (בִּשְּׁלָם),” equivalent to בִּשֵּׁל לָהֶם, “He cooked the meat for them.”

rashi.heb:
*מדבר וציה.* 
ירושלי' הקרוי' ציה וציון הקרוי' מדבר הן ישושו על מפלתם של גבורי שעיר (ובצרה):
rashi.eng: *Desert and wasteland.* Jerusalem, called ‘wasteland,’ and Zion, called ‘desert,’ they shall rejoice over the downfall of the mighty of the heathens and Persia ([Manuscripts yield:] of Edom and Bozrah). ([The Warsaw edition reads:] the mighty of Seir (and Bozrah).)

rashi.heb:
*ותגל ערבה.* 
של ירושלים:
rashi.eng: *and the plain shall rejoice.* the plain of Jerusalem.

notes.1516: (tn): The ambiguous verb form תִּפְרַח (tifrakh) is translated as a jussive because it is parallel to the jussive form תָגֵל (tagel).
notes.1517: (tn, Heb): “and let it rejoice, yes [with] rejoicing and shouting.” גִּילַת (gilat) may be an archaic feminine nominal form (see GKC 421 �130.b).
notes.1518: (tn): Or “glory” (KJV, NIV, NRSV); also a second time later in this verse.

rashi.heb:
*ורנן.* 
כמו ולרנן:
rashi.eng: *and to sing.* (lit., and sing,) like: and to sing.

rashi.heb:
*הלבנון.* 
בית המקדש:
rashi.eng: *the Lebanon.* The Temple.

rashi.heb:
*הדר.* 
כבודו לציון:
rashi.eng: *the beauty of.* His glory will be given to Zion.

notes.1519: (tn, Heb): “staggering knees”; KJV, ASV, NRSV “feeble knees”; NIV “knees that give way.”

rashi.heb:
*חזקו ידים רפות.* 
כל הנביאים מבשרי ישועה נחמו את ישראל וחזקו את ידיהם הרפות, חזקו ל' משקל כבד ופתרונו חזקו את אחרים ואם היה בא לומר חזקו אתם שידכם רפות היה לינקד חזקו ואמצו (דברי הימים ב ל״ב:ז׳) עכשיו שאומר להם לחזק ולאמץ אחרי' נקוד חזקו אמצו חזקו אל תיראו. זה נקוד חזקו ל' קל חזקו אתם מאליכם כמו שיאמר ליחיד חזק ואמץ (יהושע א׳:ו׳) ולא יאמר חזק:
rashi.eng: *Strengthen weak hands.* (חַזְּקוּ) All the prophets who brought tidings of salvation consoled Israel and strengthened their weak hands. (The word) is in the intensive conjugation, and its meaning is (the causative, i.e.,) strengthen others. If he intended to say, “Be strong, you whose hands are weak,” it would be vowelized like (2 Chron. 32:7) “Be strong (חִזְקוּ) and be firm (וְאִמְצוּ).” Now that he says to them to strengthen others and to make others firm, it is vowelized, חַזְּקוּ, אַמְּצוּ.“Be strong (חִזְקוּ), do not fear” is vowelized חִזְקוּ, a form of the ‘kal’ conjugation, meaning ‘you be strong by yourselves,’ as one says to singular (Jos. 1:6), “Be strong and be firm (חֲזַק ֶמָץ),” and he does not say, חַזֵּק.

notes.1520: (tn, Heb): “Say to the hasty of heart,” i.e., those whose hearts beat quickly from fear.
notes.1521: (tn): The jussive form וְיֹשַׁעֲכֶם (v�yosha’akhem), which is subordinated to the preceding imperfect with vav conjunctive, indicates purpose.

rashi.heb:
*לנמהרי לב.* 
שממהרין את הגאולה ומצירין על איחורה:
rashi.eng: *to the hasty of heart.* Who hurry the redemption and are troubled by its delay.

rashi.heb:
*נקם יבא.* 
כמו בנקם יבא:
rashi.eng: *[with] vengeance He shall come.* (lit., vengeance He shall come,) with vengeance He shall come.

rashi.heb:
*גמול אלהים.*
