notes.1698: (sn): The implied answer to the rhetorical questions of v. 12 is “no one but the Lord. The Lord, and no other, created the world. Like a merchant weighing out silver or commodities on a scale, the Lord established the various components of the physical universe in precise proportions.

rashi.heb:
*מי מדד וגו'.* 
כל זה היה בו כח לעשות וכ"ש שיש בו כח לשמור הבטחות הללו:
rashi.eng: *Who measured etc..* He had the power to do all this, and surely He has the power to keep these promises.

rashi.heb:
*בשעלו.* 
בהליכתו שנא' דרכת בים סוסיך (חבקוק ג׳:ט״ו), בשעלו כמו (במדבר כ״ב:כ״ד) במשעול הכרמים שביל, ד"א שעל שם כלי הוא וכן בשעלי שעורים (יחזקאל יג):
rashi.eng: *with his gait.* Heb. בְּשָׁעֳלוֹ, with his walking, as it is said (Habakkuk 3:15): “You trod with Your horses in the sea.” Comp. (Num. 22:24) “In the path (בְּמִשְׁעוֹל) of the vineyards, a path (for walking).” Another explanation is that שַׁעַל is the name of a receptacle. Comp. (Ezekiel 13:19) “For measures (בְּשַׁעֲלוֹ) of barley.”

rashi.heb:
*תכן.* 
אמולאי"ר בלע"ז ל' מדה ומנין כמו ותוכן לבנים תתנו (שמות ה):
rashi.eng: *measured.* Amolad in O.F., an expression of measure and number. Comp. (Ex. 5:18) “And the number (וְתֹכֶן) of bricks you shall give.”

rashi.heb:
*וכל בשליש.* 
ומדד בשלישיו' שליש מדבר שליש ישוב שליש ימי' ונהרות, ל"א בשליש מגודל עד אמה שלישי לאצבעות, ומנחם פי' שהוא שם כלי וכן ותשקמו בדמעות שליש (תהלים ס):
rashi.eng: *and measured by thirds.* Heb. בַּשָּׁלִשׁ, and measured by thirds, one third wilderness, one third civilization, and one third seas and rivers. Another interpretation: בַּשָּׁלִשׁ, from the thumb to the middle finger, the third of the fingers. Menahem explains it as the name of a vessel. Comp. (Ps. 80:6) “And You gave them to drink tears with a vessel (שָׁלִישׁ).”

rashi.heb:
*ושקל בפלס הרים.* 
הכל לפי הארץ הר כבד תקע בארץ קשה והקלים בארץ רכה:
rashi.eng: *and weighed mountains with a scale.* Everything according to the earth, a heavy mountain He inserted into hard earth, and the light ones into soft earth.

notes.1699: (tn): Perhaps the verb is used metonymically here in the sense of “advises” (note the following line).
notes.1700: (tn): In this context רוּחַ (ruakh) likely refers to the Lord’s “mind,” or mental faculties, rather than his personal Spirit (see BDB 925 s.v.).
notes.1701: (tn, Heb): “or [as] the man of his counsel causes him to know?”

rashi.heb:
*מי תכן.* 
את רוח הקודש בפי הנביאים ה' תכנו וכדאי הוא להאמן:
rashi.eng: *Who meted.* the Holy Spirit in the mouth of the prophets? The Lord prepared it, and He is worthy of belief.

rashi.heb:
*ואיש עצתו יודיענו.* 
רוחו כן ת"י ולפי משמעו ואיש עצתו מוסב לראש המקרא מי תכן את רוחו ומי איש עצתו אשר יודיענו להקב"ה עצה:
rashi.eng: *and His adviser who informs Him.* [and the one with whom He takes counsel He informs] of His spirit. So did Jonathan render it. [Who meted out the spirit? The Lord, and the one with whom He takes counsel He informs him, i.e., the righteous in whom God confides, He informs of His plans for the future.] But, according to its context, עֲצָתו ֹוְאִישׁ refers back to the beginning of the verse. Who meted out His spirit and who is His adviser who informs the Holy One, blessed be He, of counsel?

notes.1702: (tn, Heb): “With whom did he consult, so that he gave discernment to him?”
notes.1703: (tn, Heb): “and taught him.” The vav (ו) consecutive with prefixed verbal form continues the previous line. The translation employs an interrogative pronoun for stylistic reasons.
notes.1704: (tn): The phrase אֹרַח מִשְׁפָּט (’orakh mishpat) could be translated “path of justice” (so NASB, NRSV), but in this context, where creative ability and skill is in view, the phrase is better understood in the sense of “the way that is proper or fitting” (see BDB 1049 s.v. מִשְׁפָּט 6); cf. NIV, NCV “the right way.”
notes.1705: (tn, Heb): “or the way of understanding causes him to know?” The implied answer to the rhetorical questions in vv. 13-14 is, “No one.” In contrast to Marduk, the creator-god of Mesopotamian myths who receives help from the god of wisdom, the Lord neither needs nor receives any such advice or help. See R. Whybray, Heavenly Counsellor (SOTSMS), 64-77.

rashi.heb:
*את מי נועץ ויבינהו.* 
את מי מן העכו"ם נועץ כמו שנועץ עם הנביאי' כמו שנא' באברהם וה' אמר המכסה אני מאברהם (בראשית כו) וגו':
rashi.eng: *With whom did He take counsel and give him to understand.* With which of the heathens ([mss., K’li Paz:] nations) did He take counsel, as He took counsel with the prophets, as it is said concerning Abraham (Gen. 18:17): “Do I conceal from Abraham…?”

rashi.heb:
*ויבינהו וילמדהו באורח משפט.* 
את מי מן העכו"ם עשה כן שלמדו חכמה כמו שעשה לאברהם שנתן לב להכירו מאליו ולהבין בתור' שנא' וישמור משמרתי ואומר למען אשר יצוה (שם יח) וגו' וכליותיו היו נובעות חכמה שנא' אף לילות יסרוני כליותי (תהלים טז) (את מי נועץ ויבינהו. האיש להקב"ה הן כל גוים לפניו כמר מדלי ואיך ילמדו לו):
rashi.eng: *and give him to understand, and teach him in the way of justice.* With which one of the heathens ([mss., K’li Paz:] nations) did He do so, that He taught him wisdom as He did to Abraham, to whom He gave a heart to recognize Him by himself and to understand the Torah, as it is said (ibid. 26:5): “And he kept My charge,” and Scripture states further (ibid. 18:19), “For he commands etc.” And his kidneys would pour forth wisdom to him, as it is said (Ps. 16:7): “Even at night my kidneys chastised me.”

rashi.heb:
*(את מי נועץ ויבינהו..* 
האיש להקב"ה הן כל גוים לפניו כמר מדלי ואיך ילמדו לו):
rashi.eng: *(With whom did He take counsel and who gave Him to understand.* [With which man did He take counsel and which] man gave the Holy One, blessed be He, [to understand?] Behold all the nations are like a drop in a bucket, and how could they teach Him?)

rashi.heb:
*הן גוים כמר מדלי.* 
העכו"ם הממאנים להכיר את בוראם ואין חשובין לו להעמיד מהם לנביאים לגלות סודו:
rashi.eng: *Behold the nations are like a drop from a bucket.* And are not worthy to Him to appoint some of them as prophets to reveal His secret.

rashi.heb:
*כמר מדלי.* 
כטיפה מרה המטפטפת משולי הדלי ומשקע טנופת המים ורוקבין העץ, לימוניד"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *like a drop from a bucket.* Heb. כְּמַר, like a bitter drop that drips from the bottom of the bucket, bitter from the putrid water that is embedded in the bucket and the decay of the wood, limonede in O.F.

rashi.heb:
*וכשחק מאזנים.* 
שהנחוש' מעלה עיפוש ומשתחק:
rashi.eng: *and like the dust of a balance.* for the copper corrodes and wears off.

rashi.heb:
*כדק.* 
אבק דק:
rashi.eng: *like fine.* fine dust.

rashi.heb:
*יטול.* 
כאבק הנישא ועולה על ידי רוח כדק אשר ינטל:
rashi.eng: *that blows away.* [lit. that will be taken.] Like dust that is picked up and goes up through the wind, like fine dust that is carried away.

notes.1708: (tn): The words “for a sacrifice” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.1709: (sn): The point is that not even the Lebanon forest could supply enough wood and animals for an adequate sacrifice to the Lord.

rashi.heb:
*אין די בער.* 
על מזבחו:
rashi.eng: *there is not enough to burn.* on His altar.

rashi.heb:
*וחיתו.* 
של לבנון, אין די עולה, ד"א:
rashi.eng: *and its beasts.* (the beasts] of the Lebanon-there is not enough for burnt offerings. Another explanation is:

rashi.heb: *ולבנון אין די בער וגו'.*  לכפר על עון האומות:
rashi.eng: *And the Lebanon etc..* to expiate the iniquity of the heathens.

notes.1710: (tn, Heb): “[as derived] from nothing and unformed.”

rashi.heb:
*כאין נגדו.* 
כאין הם בעיניו ואין חשובין לפניו:
rashi.eng: *All the nations are as naught before Him.* In His eyes they are as naught, and are not regarded by Him.

rashi.heb:
*נסך.* 
לו מסכה:
rashi.eng: *melted.* Heb. נָסַךְ, an expression of melting (מַסֵּכָה).

rashi.heb:
*נסך חרש.* 
חרש של ברזל נוסכו מברזל או מנחושת ואח"כ הצורף מרקעו בטסי זהב ומצפהו מלמעלה:
rashi.eng: *the craftsman has melted.* The ironsmith has cast it from iron or from copper, and then the goldsmith plates it with plates of gold and covers it from above.

rashi.heb:
*ורתקות.* 
שלשלאות:
rashi.eng: *and chains.* Heb. וּרְתֻקוֹת, and chains.

notes.1712: (tn): The first two words of the verse (הַמְסֻכָּן תְּרוּמָה, hamsukan t�rumah) are problematic. Some take מְסֻכָּן as an otherwise unattested Pual participle from סָכַן (sakhan, “be poor”) and translate “the one who is impoverished.” תְּרוּמָה (t�rumah, “contribution”) can then be taken as an adverbial accusative, “with respect to a contribution,” and the entire line translated, “the one who is too impoverished for such a contribution [i.e., the metal idol of v. 19?] selects wood that will not rot.” However, מְסֻכָּן is probably the name of a tree used in idol manufacturing (cognate with Akkadian musukkanu, cf. H. R. Cohen, Biblical Hapax Legomena [SBLDS], 133). מְסֻכָּן may be a scribal interpretive addition attempting to specify עֵץ (’ets) or עֵץ may be a scribal attempt to categorize מְסֻכָּן. How an idol constitutes a תְּרוּמָה (“contribution”) is not entirely clear.
notes.1713: (tn): Or “set up” (ASV, NAB, NIV, NRSV); KJV, NASB “to prepare.”

rashi.heb:
*המסכן תרומה.* 
או אם בא לעשותו של עץ המלומד להבחין בין עץ המתקיים לשאר עצים שלא ירקב מהר יבחר:
rashi.eng: *He who is accustomed to select.* הַמְסֻכָּן תְּרוּמָה. Or, if he comes to make it of wood, one who is accustomed to discern between a durable tree and other trees, chooses a tree that does not decay quickly.

rashi.heb:
*המסכן.* 
המלומד כמו (במדבר כ״ב:ל׳) ההסכן הסכנתי:
rashi.eng: *He who is accustomed.* Heb. הַמְסֻכָּן. Comp. (Num. 22:30) “Have I been accustomed (הַהַסְכֵּן הִסְכַּנְתִּי)?”

rashi.heb:
*תרומה.* 
הפרשה ברירת העצים:
rashi.eng: *to select.* Heb. תְּרוּמָה, separation, selection of the trees.

rashi.heb:
*הלא תדעו.* 
מוסדות הארץ מי יסדה ואותו היה לכם לעבוד:
rashi.eng: *Do you not know… the foundations of the earth.* Who founded it, and you should have worshipped Him.

notes.1714: (tn, Heb): “the circle of the earth” (so KJV, NIV, NRSV, NLT).
notes.1715: (tn): The words “before him” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.1716: (tn): The otherwise unattested noun דֹּק (doq), translated here “thin curtain,” is apparently derived from the verbal root דקק (“crush”) from which is derived the adjective דַּק (daq, “thin”; see HALOT 229 s.v. דקק). The nuance “curtain” is implied from the parallelism (see “tent” in the next line).
notes.1717: (tn): The meaning of the otherwise unattested verb מָתַח (matakh, “spread out”) is determined from the parallelism (note the corresponding verb “stretch out” in the previous line) and supported by later Hebrew and Aramaic cognates. See HALOT 654 s.v. *מתה.
notes.1718: (tn, Heb): “like a tent [in which] to live”; NAB, NASB “like a tent to dwell (live NIV, NRSV) in.”

rashi.heb:
*חוג.* 
ל' מחוגה (לקמן מד) עוגל קומפ"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *the circle.* Heb. חוּג, an expression similar to (infra 44:13) “And with a compass (וּבַמְּחוּגָה),” a circle (compas in O.F.).

rashi.heb:
*ויושביה.* 
לפניו כחגבים:
rashi.eng: *and whose inhabitants.* are to Him [lit. before Him] like grasshoppers.

rashi.heb:
*כדוק.* 
כיריעה טייל"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *like a curtain.* Heb. כַדֹּק, a curtain, toile in French.

rashi.heb:
*אף בל נטעו.* 
אף הרי הם כמי שלא נטעו:
rashi.eng: *Even [as though] they were not planted.* They are even as though they were not planted.

rashi.heb:
*אף בל זרעו.* 
ועוד יתר מכאן שישורשו ויעקרו כאלו לא זורעו, זריע' פחותה מנטיעה:
rashi.eng: *even [as though] they were not sown.* And still more than this, that they shall be uprooted and plucked out, as if they were not sown. Sowing is less than planting.

rashi.heb:
*בל שורש בארץ גזעם.* 
לכשיעקרו לא ישריש הגזע בארץ שיהא מחליף כל שורש שבמקרא טעמו באות ראשונה ונקודה הרי"ש פתח וזה טעמו למטה ונקוד קמץ לפי שהוא לשון פועל אינרצינ"י בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *their trunk is not rooted in the earth.* When they will be plucked out, the trunk will not take root in the ground that it will grow up anew. Every שֹׁרֶשׁ, root, in Scripture is accented on the first letter, and the ‘reish’ is vowelized with a ‘pattah’ [segol]. This one, however, is accented on the latter syllable and it is vowelized with a ‘kamatz katan’ [tzeireh] because it is a verb, present tense, [enracinant in French] being rooted.

notes.1719: (sn): See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

notes.1720: (tn, Heb): “Lift on high your eyes and see.”
notes.1721: (tn): The words “heavenly lights” are supplied in the translation for clarification. See the following lines.
notes.1722: (tn, Heb): “the one who brings out by number their host.” The stars are here likened to a huge army that the Lord leads out. Perhaps the next line pictures God calling roll. If so, the final line may be indicating that none of them dares “go AWOL.” (“AWOL” is a military acronym for “absent without leave.”)

rashi.heb:
*מי ברא אלה.* 
כל הצבא אשר תראו במרום:
rashi.eng: *who created these.* All the host that you will see on high.

rashi.heb:
*מרוב אונים.* 
שיש לו ושהוא אמיץ כח איש מהצבא לא נעדר שלא יקרא בשם:
rashi.eng: *because of His great might.* that He has, and that He is strong in power, no one of His host is missing, that He does not call by name.

notes.1723: (tn, Heb): “my way is hidden from the Lord” (so NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).
notes.1724: (tn, Heb): “and from my God my justice passes away”; NRSV “my right is disregarded by my God.”

rashi.heb:
*למה תאמר.* 
עמי יעקב ותדבר בגלות:
rashi.eng: *Why should you say.* My people ([K’li Paz, mss.:] the people of) Jacob, and speak in exile.

rashi.heb:
*נסתרה דרכי מה'.* 
העלים מנגד עיניו כל מה שעבדנוהו והמשיל עלינו אות' שלא ידעוהו:
rashi.eng: *My way has been hidden from the Lord.* He hid from before His eyes all that we served Him, and gave those who did not know Him, dominion over us.

rashi.heb:
*ומאלהי משפטי יעבור.* 
העביר מלפניו משפט הגמול הטוב שהי' לו לשלם לאבותינו ולנו:
rashi.eng: *and from my God, my judgment passes?.* He ignores the judgment of the good reward He should have paid our forefathers and us.

notes.1725: (tn, Heb): “the ends of the earth,” but this is a merism, where the earth’s extremities stand for its entirety, i.e., the extremities and everything in between them.
notes.1726: (sn): Exiled Israel’s complaint (v. 27) implies that God might be limited in some way. Perhaps he, like so many of the pagan gods, has died. Or perhaps his jurisdiction is limited to Judah and does not include Babylon. Maybe he is unable to devise an adequate plan to rescue his people, or is unable to execute it. But v. 28 affirms that he is not limited temporally or spatially nor is his power and wisdom restricted in any way. He can and will deliver his people, if they respond in hopeful faith (v. 31a).

rashi.heb:
*בורא קצות הארץ וגו'.* 
אין חקר לתבונתו ומי שיש לו כח כזה וחכמה כזו הוא יודע את המחשבות למה הוא מאחר טובתכם אלא כדי לכלות את הפשע ולהתם את החטאת ע"י היסורין:
rashi.eng: *the Creator of the ends of the earth… there is no fathoming His understanding.* And One who has such strength and such wisdom. He knows the thoughts. Why does He delay your benefit, only to terminate the transgression and to expiate the sin through afflictions.

rashi.heb:
*נותן ליעף כח.* 
וסופו להחליף כח לעייפותכם:
rashi.eng: *Who gives the tired strength.* And who will eventually renew strength for your tiredness.

notes.1727: (tn, Heb): “stumbling they stumble.” The verbal idea is emphasized by the infinitive absolute.

rashi.heb:
*ויעפו נערים.* 
גבורת הכשדי' המנוערים מן המצות תיעף:
rashi.eng: *Now youths shall become tired.* Heb. נְעָרִים. The might of your enemies who are devoid (מְנֹעָרִים) of commandments, shall become faint.

rashi.heb:
*ובחורים כשול יכשלו.* 
אותם שהם עכשיו גבורים וחזקים יכשלו ואתם קוי ה' תחליפו כח חדש וחזק:
rashi.eng: *and young men shall stumble.* Those who are now mighty and strong, shall stumble, but you, who put your hope in the Lord shall gain new strength and power.

notes.1728: (tn): The words “for the Lord’s help” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.1729: (tn, Heb): “they rise up [on] wings like eagles” (TEV similar).

rashi.heb:
*אבר.* 
כנף:
rashi.eng: *wings.* [The Hebrew אבר means] a wing.

notes.1730: (tn): Or “islands” (KJV, NIV, CEV); TEV “distant lands”; NLT “lands beyond the sea.”
notes.1731: (tn): The Hebrew term מִשְׁפָּט (mishpat) could be translated “judgment,” but here it seems to refer to the dispute or debate between the Lord and the nations.

rashi.heb:
*החרישו אלי.* 
כדי לשמוע דבר:
rashi.eng: *Be silent to Me.* in order to hear My words.

rashi.heb:
*איים.* 
אומות של עכו"ם:
rashi.eng: *islands.* Heathens ([mss. Kli Paz:] nations).

rashi.heb:
*יחליפו כח.* 
יתקשטו ויתחזקו בכל גבורתם אולי יעמדו בדין בכח:
rashi.eng: *shall renew [their] strength.* They shall adorn themselves and strengthen themselves with all their might perhaps they will succeed in their judgment by force.

rashi.heb:
*יגשו.* 
הלום ואז משיגשו ידברו:
rashi.eng: *they shall approach.* here, and then, when they approach, they shall speak.

rashi.heb:
*למשפט נקרבה.* 
להוכיח' על פניהם:
rashi.eng: *to judgment let us draw near.* to reprove them to their faces.

notes.1732: (sn): The expression this one from the east refers to the Persian conqueror Cyrus, as later texts indicate (see 44:28-45:6; 46:11; 48:14-16).
notes.1733: (tn): The interrogative particle is understood by ellipsis.
notes.1734: (tn, Heb): “[in] righteousness called him to his foot.”
notes.1735: (tn, Heb): “he [the Lord] places before him [Cyrus] nations.”
notes.1736: (tn): The verb יַרְדְּ (yard�) is an otherwise unattested Hiphil form from רָדָה (radah, “rule”). But the Hiphil makes no sense with “kings” as object; one must understand an ellipsis and supply “him” (Cyrus) as the object. The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa has יוֹרִד (yorid), which appears to be a Hiphil form from יָרַד (yarad, “go down”). Others suggest reading יָרֹד (yarod), a Qal form from רָדַד (radad, “beat down”).
notes.1737: (sn): The point is that they are powerless before Cyrus’ military power and scatter before him.

rashi.heb:
*מי העיר ממזרח.* 
אותו שצדק יקראהו לרגלו מי העיר את אברה' להביאו מארם שהוא במזרח וצדק שהיה עושה היא היתה לקראת רגליו בכל אשר הלך:
rashi.eng: *Who aroused from the East.* one whom righteousness accompanied? Who aroused Abraham to bring him from Aram which is in the East and the righteousness that he would perform that was opposite his feet wherever he went.

rashi.heb:
*יתן לפניו גוים.* 
מי שהעירו ממקומו להסיע הוא נתן לפניו ארבעה מלכים וחיילותיהם:
rashi.eng: *He placed nations before him.* He, Who aroused him to leave his place to cause him to move, He placed before him four kings and their hosts.

rashi.heb:
*ירד.* 
ירדה:
rashi.eng: *He gave him dominion.* Heb. יַרְדְּ, like יַרָדֶּה.

rashi.heb:
*יתן כעפר חרבו.* 
רמא כעפרא קטולין קדם חרביה, נתן את חרבו ועושה חללים רבים כעפר ואת קשתו נתן מרבה הרוגים ונופלים כקש נדף:
rashi.eng: *He made his sword like dust.* [Jonathan paraphrases:] He cast slain ones before his sword like dust. He suffered his sword to take its toll of casualties as [numerous as] grains of dust, and his bow He suffered to take its toll of casualties who would fall like wind blown stubble.

notes.1738: (tn, Heb): “[in] peace”; KJV, ASV “safely”; NASB “in safety”; NIV “unscathed.”
notes.1739: (tn, Heb): “a way with his feet he does not come [or “enter”].” One could translate, “by a way he was not [previously] entering with his feet.” This would mean that he is advancing into new territory and expanding his conquests. The present translation assumes this is a hyperbolic description to his speedy advance. He moves so quickly he does not enter the way with his feet, i.e., his feet don’t even touch the ground. See C. R. North, Second Isaiah, 94.

rashi.heb:
*ירדפם יעבור שלום.* 
הלך על מעברותיו בשלום לא נכשל ברדפו אותם:
rashi.eng: *He pursued them and passed on safely.* He traversed all his fords safely; he did not stumble when he pursued them.

rashi.heb:
*אורח ברגליו לא יבא.* 
דרך אשר לא בא קודם לכן ברגליו, לא יבא לא היה רגיל לבא:
rashi.eng: *a path upon which he had not come with his feet.* A road upon which he had not come previously with his feet. [The future tense of] יָבוֹא means that he was not accustomed to come.

notes.1740: (tn, Heb): “Who acts and accomplishes?”; NASB “Who has performed and accomplished it.”
notes.1741: (tn): The interrogative particle is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
notes.1742: (tn, Heb): “I, the Lord, [am with] the first, and with the last ones I [am] he.”

rashi.heb:
*מי פעל ועשה.* 
לו את זאת מי שהוא קורא הדורות מראש לאדם הראשון הוא עשה לאברהם גם את זאת:
rashi.eng: *Who worked and did.* for him all this? He Who called the generations from the beginning, to Adam, He did this also for Abraham.

rashi.heb:
*אני ה' ראשון.* 
להפליא פלא ולעזור:
rashi.eng: *I, the Lord, am first.* to perform wonders and to aid.

rashi.heb:
*ואת אחרונים אני הוא.* 
אף עמכם בנים אחרונים אהיה ואעזור אתכם:
rashi.eng: *and with the last ones I am He.* Also with you, the last sons, I will be, and I will aid you.

notes.1743: (tn): Or “islands” (NIV, CEV); NCV “faraway places”; NLT “lands beyond the sea.”
notes.1744: (tn, Heb): “the ends of the earth,” but this is a merism, where the earth’s extremities stand for its entirety, i.e., the extremities and everything in between them.

rashi.heb:
*ראו איים.* 
עובדי עכו"ם הגבורות שאעשה וייראו:
rashi.eng: *The islands shall see.* [lit. saw.] The heathens shall see the mighty deeds that I will perform, and they shall fear.

rashi.heb:
*קרבו ויאתיון.* 
זה אצל זה נאספים להלחם כשיראו הגאולה:
rashi.eng: *they have approached and come.* One to another they will gather to war when they see the redemption.

notes.1745: (tn, Heb): “each his neighbor helps”; NCV “The workers help each other.”

rashi.heb:
*איש את רעהו וגו'.* 
יאמר חזק למלחמה אולי יעמדו להם אלהיהם:
rashi.eng: *Each one… his fellow etc..* He shall say, “Strengthen yourself” for war, perhaps their gods will protect them [lit. stand up for them].

notes.1746: (tn): The verb “encourages” is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
notes.1747: (tn, Heb): “saying of the welding, ‘It is good.’”

rashi.heb:
*ויחזק חרש.* 
נוסך הפסל:
rashi.eng: *And the craftsman strengthened.* [i.e.,] the one who molds the idol.

rashi.heb:
*את צורף.* 
המרקעו בזהב:
rashi.eng: *the smith.* who plates it with gold.

rashi.heb:
*מחליק פטיש.* 
באחרונה כשהוא מכה בנחת להחליק את המלאכה:
rashi.eng: *the one who smoothes with the hammer.* The final stage, when he taps lightly to flatten out the work.

rashi.heb:
*את הולם פעם.* 
הוא המתחיל בה כשהיא עשת ומכה בכל כחו:
rashi.eng: *the one who wields the sledge hammer.* He is the one who commences on it when it is a block, and beats it with all his might.

rashi.heb:
*אומר לדבק טוב הוא.* 
על אותן שהיו מחזירין אחר קרקע טובה לדבק בה עששיות ברזל:
rashi.eng: *he says of the cement, “It is good,”.* Heb. דֶּבֶק. He alludes to those who seek suitable ground upon which to adhere iron plates.

rashi.heb:
*דבק.* 
שולדור"א:
rashi.eng: *of the cement.*  דֶּבֶק is soudure in French, weld.

rashi.heb:
*ויחזקהו.* 
לצלם:
rashi.eng: *and he strengthened it.* The idol.

rashi.heb:
*במסמרים לא ימוט.* 
כולם יחזקו זה את זה:
rashi.eng: *with nails that it should not move.* All of them will strengthen each other.

notes.1748: (tn): Or perhaps, “covenantal partner” (see 1 Kgs 5:15 HT [5:1 ET]; 2 Chr 20:7).

rashi.heb:
*ואתה ישראל עבדי.* 
ועלי יש לעזור לך סוף המקרא אל תירא כי אתך אני כך נראה לי חבור הענין לפי פשוטו ומ"א בבראשית רבה דורש כל הענין במלכי צדק ואברה'
rashi.eng: *But you, Israel My servant.* and I am obliged to help you. The end of this sentence is (infra 10): “Do not fear.” This appears to me to be the sequence of the section according to its simple meaning. But the Midrash Aggadah in Gen. Rabbah 44:7 expounds the entire section as alluding to Malchizedek and Abraham.

rashi.heb:
*ראו איים.* 
אותה מלחמ' וייראו שם נתיירא מאברהם פן יאמר לו העמדת רשעים אלו בעולם ואברהם נתיירא משם לפי שהרג את בני עילם שהם משם:
rashi.eng: *[5] Islands saw.* the war and feared. Shem [Malchizedek] feared Abraham, lest he say to him, You begot these wicked men in the world. And Abraham feared Shem, since he slew his sons, the people of Elam, who was descended from Shem.

rashi.heb:
*איים.* 
כשם שאיי הים מסויימין בעולם כך אברהם ושם היו מסויימין בעולם:
rashi.eng: *islands.* Just as the islands of the sea are distinguished and recognized in the sea, so were Abraham and Shem distinguished in the world.

rashi.heb:
*איש את רעהו יעזורו.* 
זה עוזר את זה בברכו' ברוך אברם (בראשית י״ד:כ׳) וזה עוזר את זה במתנות (שם) ויתן לו מעשר מכל:
rashi.eng: *[6] Each one aided his fellow.* This one [Shem] aided this one [Abraham] with blessings, “Blessed be Abram” (Gen. 14:19), and this one [Abraham] aided this one [Shem] with gifts, “And he gave him tithe from everything” (ibid. verse 20).

rashi.heb:
*ויחזק חרש.* 
זה שם שהיה נפח לעשות מסמרות ובריחים לתבה:
rashi.eng: *[7] And the craftsman strengthened.* This is Shem, who was a blacksmith, to make nails and bars for the ark.

rashi.heb:
*את צורף.* 
זה אברהם שהוא צורף את הבריות לקרבן אל השכינה:
rashi.eng: *the smith.* This is Abraham, who purified (צוֹרֵף) the people, to bring them near to God [lit. to Heaven].

rashi.heb:
*את הולם פעם.* 
זה אברהם שהלם כל המלכים האלה פעם אחת:
rashi.eng: *the sledge hammer.* This is Abraham, who smote (הָלַם) all these kings at one time.

rashi.heb:
*אומר לדבק טוב הוא.* 
טוב לידבק באלוה של זה:
rashi.eng: *He says of the cement.* Heb. דֶּבֶק. The nations said, It is good to cleave to this one’s God [rather than to Nimrod’s idols].

rashi.heb:
*ויחזקהו.* 
שם לאברה' להיו' דבק בהקב"ה ולא ימוט:
rashi.eng: *And he strengthened him.* Shem strengthened Abraham to cleave to the Holy One, blessed be He, and not to move.

rashi.heb:
*ואתה ישראל עבדי.* 
אברהם שלא היה מזרע צדיקים עשיתי לו כל זאת ואתה ישראל עבדי. הקנוי לי משני אבות:
rashi.eng: *[8] And you, Israel My servant.* Abraham, who was not descended from righteous men, I did all this for him, and you, Israel My servant, who belong to Me by dint of two forefathers.

rashi.heb:
*זרע אברהם אוהבי.* 
שלא הכירני מתוך תוכחה ולימוד אבותיו אלא מתוך אהבה:
rashi.eng: *the seed of Abraham, who loved Me.* who did not recognize Me because of the admonition and the teaching of his fathers, but out of love.

notes.1749: (tn, Heb): “whom I have taken hold of [i.e., to lead back].”

rashi.heb:
*אשר החזקתיך.* 
לקחתיך לחלקי כמו (שמות ד׳:ד׳) וישלח ידו ויחזק בו:
rashi.eng: *whom I grasped.* Heb. הֶחֱזַקְתִּי. I took you for My share. Comp. (Ex. 4:4) “And he stretched out his hand and grasped (וַיְּחֲזֵק) it.”

rashi.heb:
*מקצות הארץ.* 
משאר העכו"ם:
rashi.eng: *from the ends of the earth.* from the other nations.

rashi.heb:
*ומאציליה.* 
מן הגדולים שבהן:
rashi.eng: *and from its nobles.* from the greatest of them.

rashi.heb:
*קראתיך.* 
בשם לחלקי בני בכורי ישראל:
rashi.eng: *I called you.* by name for My share, “My firstborn son, Israel” (ibid. v. 22).

rashi.heb:
*ולא מאסתיך.* 
כזה שנאמר בו (מלאכי א) שנאתי:
rashi.eng: *and I did not despise you.* like Esau, as it is said (Malachi 1:3), “And Esau I hated.”

notes.1750: (tn): According to BDB (1043 s.v. שָׁעָה), the verb תִּשְׁתָּע (tishta’) in the second line of the poetic couplet is a Hitpael form from the root שָׁעָה (sha’ah, “gaze,” with metathesis of the stem prefix and the first root letter). Taking the Hitpael as iterative, one may then translate “do not anxiously look about.” However, the alleged Hitpael form of שָׁעָה (sha’ah) only occurs here and in verse 23. HALOT 1671 s.v. שׁתע proposes that the verb is instead a Qal form from the root שׁתע (“fear”) which is attested in cognate Semitic languages, including Ugaritic (discovered after the publishing of BDB), suggests the existence of this root. The poetic structure of v. 10 also supports the proposal, for the form in question is in synonymous parallelism to יָרֵא (yare’, “fear”).
notes.1751: (tn): The “right hand” is a symbol of the Lord’s power to deliver (Exod 15:6, 12) and protect (Ps 63:9 HT [63:8 ET]). Here צֶדֶק (tsedeq) has its well-attested nuance of “vindicated righteousness,” i.e., “victory, deliverance” (see 45:8; 51:5, and BDB 841-42 s.v.).

rashi.heb:
*אל תשתע.* 
אל ימס לבך להיות כשעוה זו וזה הכלל כל תיבה שתחל' יסודה שי"ן כשבא לדבר בל' מתפעל התפעל או יתפעל התי"ו חולקת ונכנסת בין שתי אותיות שרשי התיבה כמו (ישעיה כט) וישתומם (מיכה ז) וישתמר חוקות עמרי (ש"א א) תשתכרין (איוב ל) תשתפך נפשי:
rashi.eng: *be not discouraged.* Heb. אַל תִּשְׁתָּע. Let your heart not melt like wax (שַׁעֲוָה). This is the rule: Every word whose first radical is ‘shin,’ when it is used in the reflexive present, past, or future, the ‘tav’ separates it and enters between the first two radicals. Comp. (infra 49:16) “And He was astounded (וַיַּשְׁתּוֹמֵם);” (Micah 6:16) “For the statutes of Omri shall be observed (וְיִשְׁתַּמֵּר);” (I Sam. 1:14) “will you be drunk (תִּשְׁתַּכָּרִין)?;” (Job 30:16) “My soul is poured out (תִּשְׁתַּפֵּךְ).”

notes.1752: (tn, Heb): “the men of your strife”; NASB “those who contend with you.”

notes.1754: (tn, Heb): “the men of your struggle”; NASB “those who quarrel with you.”
notes.1755: (tn, Heb): “the men of your battle”; NAB “who do battle with you.”

notes.1756: (tn, Heb): “O worm Jacob” (NAB, NIV). The worm metaphor suggests that Jacob is insignificant and despised.
notes.1757: (tn): On the basis of the parallelism (note “worm”) and an alleged Akkadian cognate, some read “louse” or “weevil.” Cf. NAB “O maggot Israel”; NRSV “you insect Israel.”
notes.1758: (tn, Heb): “your kinsman redeemer.” A גָּאַל (ga’al, “kinsman redeemer”) was a protector of the extended family’s interests.
notes.1759: (sn): See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

rashi.heb:
*תולעת יעקב.* 
משפחת יעקב החלשה כתולעת שאין לה גבורה אלא בפיה, תולעת וירמונ"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *O worm of Jacob.* Heb. תּוֹלַעַת. The family of Jacob, which is weak like a worm, which has no strength except in its mouth. תּוֹלַעַת is vermener in O.F., [vermisseau in Modern French, a worm].

rashi.heb:
*מתי ישראל.* 
מספר ישראל:
rashi.eng: *the number of Israel.* Heb. מְתֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, the number of Israel.

notes.1760: (tn, Heb): “into” (so NIV); ASV “have made thee to be.”
notes.1762: (sn): The mountains and hills symbolize hostile nations that are obstacles to Israel’s restoration.

rashi.heb:
*למורג חרוץ.* 
כלי הוא של עץ וכבד ועשוי חריצים חריצים כעין כלי נפחים של ברזל שקורין לימ"א בלע"ז וגוררין על הקשין של שבלין ומחתכן עד שנעשו תבן דק:
rashi.eng: *a… grooved threshing sledge.* It is a heavy wooden implement made with many grooves, similar to the ironsmiths’ tool known as ‘lime’ in French, a file, and they drag it over the straw of the ears of grain and it cuts them until they become fine straw.

rashi.heb:
*חדש.* 
כשהוא חדש עד שלא הוחלקו פיות חריציו הוא חותך הרבה אבל משנתישן הוחלקו פיות חריציו:
rashi.eng: *new.* When it is new, before the points of its grooves are smoothed off, it cuts very much, but when it becomes old, the points of the grooves are smoothed off.

rashi.heb:
*בעל פיפיות.* 
הם חידודי החריצין:
rashi.eng: *with sharp points.* Heb. פִּיפִיוֹת. Those are the points of the grooves.

rashi.heb:
*תדוש הרים.* 
מלכים ושרים:
rashi.eng: *you shall thresh the mountains.* kings and princes.

rashi.heb:
*תזרם.* 
תזרה אותם כבמזרה לרוח:
rashi.eng: *You shall winnow them.* You shall scatter them, as with a pitchfork, to the wind.

rashi.heb:
*ורוח תשאם.* 
מאליהם לגיהנם:
rashi.eng: *and a wind shall carry them off.* by themselves to Gehinnom.

notes.1763: (tn, Heb): “will answer them” (so ASV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT).

rashi.heb:
*מבקשים מים.* 
נתנבא הנביא על אחרית הימים (עמוס ח׳:י״א) לא רעב ללחם ולא צמא למים כי אם לשמוע את דבר ה' ישוטטו לבקש את דבר ה' ולא ימצאו וכשישוב אפו יכין להם לחם ומים וישכון שכינתו ורוח בפי נביאיהם:
rashi.eng: *seek water.* The prophet prophesied concerning the end of days (Amos 8:11), “Not a famine for bread nor a thirst for water, but to hear the words of the Lord… They shall wander to seek the word of the Lord, but they shall not find it.” And when His wrath subsides, He shall prepare for them bread and water and cause His Shechinah and His spirit to rest in the mouth of their prophets.

rashi.heb:
*נשתה.* 
ל' ונשתו מים מהים (לעיל יט) לשון השאת והשבר (איכה ג׳:מ״ז) וכולן ל' חורבה ויובש ולכך התי"ו מודגשת שהרי באה במקום שתים שאין שאת בלא תי"ו והיה לו לומר לנקבה נשתתה שהרי לזכר יחיד יאמר נשתה ולרבי' ונשתו:
rashi.eng: *is parched.* Heb. נָשָׁתָּה. An expression similar to (supra 19:5) “And water from the sea shall dry up (וְנִשְּׁתּוּ).” An expression similar to (Lam. 3:45) “The destruction (הַשֵּׁאת) and the breach.” And all of them are an expression of destruction and dryness. Therefore, a ‘dagesh’ appears in the ‘tav,’ since it comes instead of two, for there is no שֵׁאת without a ‘tav,’ and he should have said for the feminine וְנָשָׁתְתָה, since for the masculine singular he says נשתה and for the plural ונשתו.

rashi.heb:
*נהרות.* 
לב מבין לתורה ולנבואה:
rashi.eng: *rivers.* an understanding heart for Torah and prophecy.

rashi.heb:
*מדבר.* 
מקום שלא היתה חכמת התורה:
rashi.eng: *a desert.* A place where there was no Torah wisdom.

rashi.heb:
*אתן במדבר ארז שטה.* 
כל מיני ישוב אף בם אתן כל מיני חכמה וטובה ושלום:
rashi.eng: *I will give in the desert cedars, acacia trees.* all kinds of civilization. Even in them will I give all kinds of wisdom, goodness, and peace.

rashi.heb:
*תדהר ותאשור.* 
שמות אילני סרק העשויין לבנין:
rashi.eng: *firs and cypresses.* Names of trees that do not produce fruit, used for building.

notes.1764: (tn): The words “I will do this” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The Hebrew text has here simply, “in order that.”
notes.1765: (tn, Heb): “they”; NAB, NRSV “that all may see”; CEV, NLT “Everyone will see.”
notes.1767: (tn): Or “created it” (KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV); TEV “has made it happen.”

notes.1769: (sn): Apparently this challenge is addressed to the pagan idol gods, see vv. 23-24.

rashi.heb:
*קרבו ריבכם.* 
כל העכו"ם בואו וריבו והתוכחו עם בני:
rashi.eng: *Present your plea.* All the heathens ([mss. K’li Paz:] nations), come and contend and debate with My children.

rashi.heb:
*עצומותיכם.* 
טענות בריאות וחזקות שלכם ול' ריב הוא זה בל' משנה שנים שהיו מתעצמין בדין במסכת סנהדרין:
rashi.eng: *your strong points.* Heb. עַצֻּמוֹתֵיכֶם, Your sturdy and strong arguments. This is an expression of a dispute in Mishnaic Hebrew: “Two who were engaged in a legal dispute (מִתְעַצְּמִין),” in Tractate Sanhedrin (31b).

notes.1770: (tn, Heb): “As for the former things, tell us what they are!”
notes.1771: (tn, Heb): “so we might set [them to] our heart.”

rashi.heb:
*יגישו.* 
העכו"ם את נביאיהם וקוסמיהם:
rashi.eng: *Let them present.* Let those who deny the Torah ([mss., K’li Paz:] the nations) present their prophets and their soothsayers.

rashi.heb:
*ויגידו לנו.* 
את אשר תקרינה לעתיד:
rashi.eng: *and tell us what will happen.* in the future.

rashi.heb:
*הראשונות.* 
שהיו קודם בריאת עולם ועל מה נברא מה הנה (ס"א מאורעות שהתחילו כבר מה יהא בסופן):
rashi.eng: *the first things.* that were before the Creation of the world, and concerning what was created and what they are. (Other editions: The incidents that have already begun, what will be their end.)

rashi.heb:
*או הבאות.* 
לעתיד ישמיענו ונראה אם יש בהם ממש שיתקיימו דבריהם:
rashi.eng: *or the coming events.* in the future, let us hear, and we will see if there is any substance to them, that their words will come true.

notes.1773: (tn, Heb): “Declare the coming things, with respect to the end.”
notes.1774: (tc, Heb): The translation assumes the Qere (וְנִרְאֶה [v�nir’eh], from יָרֵא [yare’], “be afraid”). “so we might be frightened and afraid together.” On the meaning of the verb שָׁתָע (shata’), see the note at v. 10.

rashi.heb:
*הגידו האותיות לאחור.* 
המופתים הבאים באחרונה:
rashi.eng: *Tell the signs coming later.* Heb. הָאוֹתִיוֹתלְאָחוֹר, the wonders coming at the end.

rashi.heb:
*ונשתעה.* 
ונספר דבריה' ויספר מתרגמינן ואישתעי:
rashi.eng: *let us talk.* Heb. וְנִשְׁתָּעָה. Let us tell your words. (Gen. 24:66) “And he told (וַיְּסַפֵּר),” the Targum renders וְאִשְׁתָּעֵי.

notes.1775: (tn, Heb): “an object of disgust [is he who] chooses you.”

rashi.heb:
*הן אתם מאין.* 
ודבריכם איך יתקיימו:
rashi.eng: *Behold you are of naught.* and how will your words be fulfilled.

rashi.heb:
*ופעלכם מאפע.* 
אינכם אלא פועים ומרימים קול להטעו' בדברי כזב:
rashi.eng: *and your deed is one of shouting.* Heb. מֵאָפַע. You shout and raise your voice only to mislead the people with lies.

rashi.heb:
*תועבה.* 
הנתעבים הם יבחרו בכם ולא הקב"ה ולא עבדיו ולא משרתיו:
rashi.eng: *the abominable one.* Heb. תּוֹעֵבָה [lit. an abomination.] The abominable ones select you, and not the Holy One, blessed be He, or His servants or His ministers.

notes.1776: (sn): That is, Cyrus the Persian. See the note at v. 2.
notes.1777: (tn, Heb): “[one] from the rising of the sun [who] calls in my name.”
notes.1778: (tn): The Hebrew text has וְיָבֹא (v�yavo’, “and he comes”), but this is likely a corruption of an original וַיָּבָס (vayyavas), from בּוּס (bus, “step on”).

rashi.heb:
*העירותי מצפון ויאת.* 
אני מגיד העתידות הנני מעיר לבנות חרבות ירושלם את כורש מצפון ויאת את בבל להחריבה:
rashi.eng: *I have aroused from the north and he came.* I tell the future events. Behold I arouse Cyrus from the north to build the ruins of Jerusalem, and he came upon Babylon to destroy it.

rashi.heb:
*ממזרח שמש, יקרא בשמי.* 
כל ממלכות הארץ נתן לי ה' אלהי השמים (עזרא א׳:ב׳) ונראה שארץ פרס במזרחית צפונית היא לארץ ישראל, ד"א העירותי מצפון את נבוכדנצר להחריב את עירי ויאת, וכורש העירותי ממזרח שיקרא בשמי לבנות את עירי שמלכות פרס ממזרח ארץ ישראל היא שנא' ראיתי את האיל וגו' וי"ת אייתיתי בגלאי מלך דתקוף מרוח צפונא וייתי כמפק שמשא בגבורתיה ממדינתא אגבריני' בשמי:
rashi.eng: *from the rising of the sun he shall call in My name.* (Ezra 1:2) “All the kingdoms of the earth has the Lord God of the heavens given me.” And it appears that Persia is northeast of Eretz Israel. Another explanation is: I aroused Nebuchadnezzar from the north to destroy My city, and he came, and I aroused Cyrus from the east, that he call in My name to build My city, for the kingdom of Persia is east of Eretz Israel, as it is stated (Dan. 8:4): “I saw the ram butting etc.” [This verse in Daniel proves it. “I saw the ram butting to the west and to the north and to the south.” We deduce that he came from the east.] Jonathan paraphrases: I brought speedily a king, strong as the north wind, and he will come as the sun comes out with its might from the east; I will strengthen him with My name.

rashi.heb:
*ויבא סגנים.* 
ויבא על מלך בבל ועל שריו כאשר בא לרמוס על חומר וכמו יוצר חרשים ירמוס טיט לכלי חרס כן ירמוס הוא סגנים:
rashi.eng: *and he shall come [upon] princes.* And he shall come upon the king of Babylon and upon his princes as he would come to trample upon mire, and as a potter tramples clay for earthenware vessels, so will he trample the princes.

notes.1779: (tn): The words “who announced it” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The interrogative particle and verb are understood by ellipsis (see the preceding line).

rashi.heb:
*מי.* 
מנביאי הבעל הגיד כמוני דבר העתיד לבוא, ומי מלפנים הגידה ולכשתבא נאמר שהיא צדיק שנבואתו צדק:
rashi.eng: *Who.* of the prophets of Baal told, like me, a thing destined to come, and who told it from before, that when it comes we will say that he is just, that his prophecy is just?

rashi.heb:
*אף אין מגיד.* 
אבל אין בכם שיגיד עתידות ותתקיים:
rashi.eng: *Not one told.* But there is none among you who will foretell the future and that it will come true.

rashi.heb:
*אף אין שומע אמריכם.* 
שיעיד בבא עתידה פלוני נביא הבעל נבא אותה מלפנים:
rashi.eng: *not one hears your statements.* Who will testify when the future comes, that so and so the prophet of the Baal prophesied this from before.

notes.1780: (tn): The Hebrew text reads simply, “First to Zion, ‘Look here they are!’” The words “I decreed” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.1781: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*ראשון לציון הנה הנם.* 
מלך ראשון שיתן לב לציון הנה זה הוא שאמרתי ואע"פ שלא תגמר הגאולה על ידו הוא יהיה המתחיל מי בכם מכל עמו (עזרא א׳:ג׳):
rashi.eng: *The first to Zion, behold, behold them.* The first king who will give heart to Zion, behold he is the one I mentioned, and even though the redemption will not be completed through him, he will be the one to initiate it. (Ezra 1:3) “Whoever of you from all His people…”

rashi.heb:
*הנם.* 
זקני ישראל יהיו נכונים על פי דברו לעלות מן הגולה ולהתחיל:
rashi.eng: *behold them.* The elders of Israel will be ready, according to his statement, to go up from the exile and to begin.

rashi.heb:
*ולירושלים מבשר אתן.* 
באותן הימים חגי זכריה אשר יזרזום לבנות בימי דריוש השלישי לפרס:
rashi.eng: *and for Jerusalem I will give a herald.* in those days, [viz.] Haggai and Zechariah, who will encourage them to build it in the days of Darius III of Persia.

rashi.heb:
*וארא ואין איש.* 
תמיד אני מביט בנביאי הבעל ואין איש מגיד דבר עתיד:
rashi.eng: *And I look and there is no man.* [lit. and I will see, in the future tense.] I always look at the prophets of Baal, and there is no man who tells of a future event.

rashi.heb:
*ומאלה.* 
מכל אלה העתידות לבא ואין מהם יועץ שעמד בסוף ה' וידע אותם:
rashi.eng: *and of these.* of all these destined to come, and none of them is a counselor who stood in God’s counsel and will know them.

rashi.heb:
*ואשאלם וישיבו דבר.* 
אשר ישיבו דבר אם אשאלם:
rashi.eng: *and I ask them that they reply with a word.* That they should reply with a word if I should ask them.

notes.1782: (tc): The Hebrew text has אָוֶן (’aven, “deception,” i.e., “false”), but the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa has אין (“nothing”), which forms a better parallel with אֶפֶס (’efes, “nothing”) in the next line. See also 40:17 and 41:12.
notes.1783: (tn, Heb): “their statues are wind and nothing”; NASB “wind and emptiness”; NIV “wind and confusion.”

rashi.heb:
*הן כולם און.* 
יש לכם לדעת שכל נביאי מכחישי תורה און ואפס כל מעשיהם נסכיהם.
rashi.eng: *Behold them all,… naught.* You should know that, as for the prophets of those who deny the Torah ([mss.:] pagan prophets;) ([other mss.:] prophets of Baal), all their deeds are naught and of no substance.

rashi.heb:
*דמות מסכותם.* 
כמו הפסל נסך חרש וי"ת בענין אחר. ראשון לציון וגו'. פתגמי נחמתא דאתנביאו נבייא מלקדמין על ציון הא אתו ולפי התרגום כל העניין מדבר ממלך המשיח ובגאולה אחרונה אבל אני רואה נבואה שנתנבא ישעיה על כורש כולם בל' הסיגנון של פרשה זו אני ה' העירותיהו בצדק קורא ממזרח עיט האותיות שאלוני מגיד מראשית אחרית כולה נוטה אחר ענין פרשה זו:
rashi.eng: *their molten images.* Heb. נִסְכֵּיהֶם. Comp. (supra 40:19) “The graven image the craftsman melted (נָסַךְ).” Jonathan renders this section differently: [27] The first one to Zion etc. The words of consolation that the prophets prophesied concerning Zion, from before, behold they have come. And according to the Targum, the entire section speaks of the King Messiah and of the last redemption, but I see that the prophecy that Isaiah prophesied concerning Cyrus is all in the same language as this section. Comp. (infra 45:13) “I aroused him with righteousness;” (Infra 46:11) “Calling from the east a bird of prey;” (infra 45:11) “The signs ask Me;” (infra 46:10) “Who tells from the beginning the end.” All of this resembles the topic of this section.

notes.1784: (sn): Verses 1-7 contain the first of Isaiah’s “servant songs,” which describe the ministry of a special, ideal servant who accomplishes God’s purposes for Israel and the nations. This song depicts the servant as a just king who brings justice to the earth and relief for the oppressed. The other songs appear in 49:1-13; 50:4-11; and 52:13-53:12.
notes.1785: (tn, Heb): “he will bring out justice” (cf. ASV, NASB, NRSV).
notes.1786: (sn): Like the ideal king portrayed in Isa 11:1-9, the servant is energized by the divine spirit and establishes justice on the earth.

rashi.heb:
*הן עבדי אתמך בו.* 
הן עבדי יעקב אינו כמותכם כי אתמוך בו:
rashi.eng: *Behold My servant, I will support him.* Behold My servant Jacob is not like you, for I will support him.

rashi.heb:
*בחירי.* 
ישראל קרוי בחירי (תהילים קל״ה:ד׳) כי יעקב בחר לו יה ואומר (לקמן מה) למען עבדי יעקב ישראל בחירי:
rashi.eng: *My chosen one.* Israel is called ‘My chosen one’ ([mss.:] His chosen one) (Ps. 135:4) “For the Eternal chose Jacob for Himself.” Scripture states also (infra 45:4): “For the sake of My servant Jacob and Israel My chosen one.”

rashi.heb:
*רצתה נפשי.* 
עליו נתתי רוחי להודיע נביאיו את סודו וסופו משפט לגוים יוציא שנאמר (לעיל ב) והלכו גוים רבים וגו' ויורנו מדרכיו וגו':
rashi.eng: *whom My soul desires; I have placed My spirit upon him.* to let his prophets know My secret, and his end will be that ‘he shall promulgate justice to the nations,’ as it is stated (supra 2:3): “And let Him teach us of His ways etc.”

notes.1787: (tn, Heb): “he will not cause his voice to be heard in the street.”

rashi.heb:
*ולא ישא.* 
לא יגביה קול לא יצטרך להוכיח ולהתנבאות אל הגוים שהם מעצמם יבואו ללמוד מהם כענין שנאמר (זכריה ח׳:כ״ג) נלכה עמכם כי שמענו אלהים עמכם:
rashi.eng: *nor shall he raise [his voice].* He shall not raise his voice. It will not be necessary to admonish and to prophesy to the nations, for they will come by themselves to learn from them [i.e., from Israel], as the matter is stated (Zech. 8:23): “Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.”

notes.1788: (sn): The “crushed reed” and “dim wick” symbolize the weak and oppressed who are on the verge of extinction.
notes.1789: (tn, Heb): “faithfully he will bring out justice” (cf. NASB, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*קנה רצוץ לא ישבור.* 
ת"י עינותניא דאינון כקניא רעיע לא יתברון וחשיכיא דאינין כבוצין עמי (פיי כנר כבה) לא יטפון:
rashi.eng: *A breaking reed he shall not break.* Jonathan paraphrases: The meek, who are like a breaking reed, shall not break, and the poor, who are like a flickering candle, shall not be quenched.

rashi.heb:
*ופשתה כהה.* 
פתילת פשתה לחה שקרובה ליכבות מלך שלהם לא יגזול את הדלים ולא ירצץ את העניים ואת החלשים:
rashi.eng: *and a flickering flaxen wick.* A wet flaxen wick, that is nearly extinguished. Their king will not rob the poor and will not break the poor and the weak.

notes.1790: (tn): For rhetorical effect the terms used to describe the “crushed (רָצַץ, ratsats) reed” and “dim (כָּהָה, kahah) wick” in v. 3 are repeated here.
notes.1791: (tn): Or “islands” (NIV); NLT “distant lands beyond the sea.”
notes.1792: (tn): Or “his law” (KJV, ASV, NASB, NIV) or “his instruction” (NLT).

rashi.heb:
*ולא ירוץ.* 
כמו לא ירצץ כי מלאה הארץ דעה (לעיל יא) וישמעו להן כענין שנא' (צפניה ג׳:ט׳) כי אז אהפוך אל עמים וגו' וזהו לתורתו איים ייחלו כולם ישמעו לתורתו:
rashi.eng: *Neither shall he weaken nor shall he be broken.* Heb. וְלֹא יָרוּץ, like לֹא יֵרָצֵץ, he shall not be broken, “for the earth shall be full of knowledge of the Lord as water covers the seabed” (supra 11:9). And they shall obey them, as the matter is stated (Zeph. 3:9): “For then I will make the nations pure of speech etc.” That is what follows: And for his instruction islands shall long. They shall all obey his instruction.

notes.1793: (tn, Heb): “the God.” The definite article here indicates distinctiveness or uniqueness.
notes.1794: (tn, Heb): “and its offspring” (so NASB); NIV “all that comes out of it.”
notes.1795: (tn, Heb): “and spirit [i.e., “breath”] to the ones walking in it” (NAB, NASB, and NRSV all similar).

rashi.heb:
*האל ה'.* 
בעל הדין ובעל הרחמי':
rashi.eng: *God the Lord.* The Master of justice and the Master of clemency.

rashi.heb:
*בורא השמים.* 
תחילה כמין פקיע של שתי ואח"כ נטה אותם כדאיתא במס' חגיגה:
rashi.eng: *the Creator of the heavens.* First like a sort of ball of warp thread, and afterward He stretched it out as it is stated in Tractate Hagigah (12a).

rashi.heb:
*וצאצאיה.* 
בורא את היוצא ממנה:
rashi.eng: *and what springs forth from it.* And He creates what springs forth from it.

rashi.heb:
*נותן נשמה.* 
נשמת חיים:
rashi.eng: *Who gave a soul.* A soul of life.

rashi.heb:
*לעם עליה.* 
לכולם בשוה:
rashi.eng: *to the people upon it.* To all of them equally.

rashi.heb:
*ורוח.* 
קדושה:
rashi.eng: *and a spirit.* of sanctity.

rashi.heb:
*להולכים בה.* 
למתהלכים לפניו:
rashi.eng: *to those who walk thereon.* To those who walk before Him.

notes.1796: (tn, Heb): “call you in righteousness.” The pronoun “you” is masculine singular, referring to the servant. See the note at 41:2.
notes.1797: (tn): The translation assumes the verb is derived from the root נָצַר (natsar, “protect”). Some prefer to derive it from the root יָצַר (yatsar, “form”).
notes.1798: (tn, Heb): “a covenant of people.” A person cannot literally be a covenant; בְּרִית (b�rit) is probably metonymic here, indicating a covenant mediator. The precise identity of עָם (’am, “people”) is uncertain. In v. 5 עָם refers to mankind, and the following reference to “nations” also favors this. But in 49:8, where the phrase בְּרִית עָם occurs again, Israel seems to be in view.
notes.1799: (sn): Light here symbolizes deliverance from bondage and oppression; note the parallelism in 49:6b and in 51:4-6.
notes.1800: (tn): Or “the Gentiles” (so KJV, ASV, NIV); the same Hebrew word can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context.

rashi.heb:
*קראתיך.* 
לישעיה הוא אומר:
rashi.eng: *I called you.* To Isaiah He says.

rashi.heb:
*ואצרך.* 
כשיצרתיך זאת היתה מחשבתי שתשי' את עמי לבריתי ולהאיר להם:
rashi.eng: *and I formed you.* Heb. וְאֶצָּרְךָ. When I formed you (כְּשֶׁיְצַרְתִּיךָ) , this was My thought, that you return My people to My covenant and to enlighten them.

rashi.heb:
*לאור גוים.* 
כל שבט קרוי גוי לעצמו כענין שנא' גוי וקהל גוים:
rashi.eng: *for a light to nations.* Every tribe is called a nation by itself, as the matter is stated (Gen. 35:11): “A nation and a congregation of nations.”

notes.1801: (sn): This does not refer to literal physical healing of the blind. As the next two lines suggest, this refers metonymically to freeing captives from their dark prisons where their eyes have grown unaccustomed to light.
notes.1802: (sn): This does not refer to hardened, dangerous criminals, who would have been executed for their crimes in ancient Near Eastern society. This verse refers to political prisoners or victims of social injustice.

rashi.heb:
*לפקוח עינים עורות.* 
שאינ' רואין את גבורתו לתת לב לשוב אלי:
rashi.eng: *To open blind eyes.* who do not see My might, to take heart to return to Me.

rashi.heb:
*להוציא ממסגר אסיר.* 
וע"י שיתפקחו עיניהם יצאו אסירים ממסגר ד"א לבשרם על גלות בבל העתיד' לבא עליהן שסופן לצאת ממנה:
rashi.eng: *to bring prisoners out of a dungeon.* And because their eyes will be opened, the prisoners will come out of the dungeon. Another explanation: To inform them of the exile destined to befall them, out of which they will eventually come.

rashi.heb:
*הוא שמי.* 
הוא מפור' בל' אדנות וכח ועלי להראות שאדון אני לפיכך כבודי לאחר לא אתן:
rashi.eng: *that is My Name.* This is explained as an expression of Lordship and power. I must show that I am the Master. Therefore, My glory I will not give to another, that the heathens shall rule over My people forever and say that the hand of their God is powerful.

notes.1803: (tn, Heb): “the former things, look, they have come.”
notes.1804: (tn, Heb): “before they sprout up, I cause you to hear.” The pronoun “you” is plural, referring to the people of Israel. In this verse “the former things” are the Lord’s earlier predictive oracles which have come to pass, while “the new things” are predicted events that have not yet begun to take place. “The former things” are earlier events in Israel’s history which God announced beforehand, such as the Exodus (see 43:16-18). “The new things” are the predictions about the servant (42:1-7). and may also include Cyrus’ conquests (41:25-27).

rashi.heb:
*הראשונות.* 
שהבטחתי לאברהם על גלות מצרים (בראש' טו) וגם את הגוי וגו':
rashi.eng: *The former things.* that I promised Abraham concerning the exile of Egypt (Gen. 15:14), “And also the nation etc.”

rashi.heb:
*הנה באו.* 
שמרתי הבטחתי ועת' חדשות אני מגיד לעמי להבטיח על גלות שנייה:
rashi.eng: *behold they have come to pass.* I kept My promise, and now new things I tell My people, to promise them concerning a second exile.

notes.1805: (tn, Heb): “his praise.” The phrase stands parallel to “new song” in the previous line.
notes.1806: (tn, Heb): “and its fullness”; NASB, NIV “and all that is in it.”

rashi.heb:
*תהלתו מקצה הארץ.* 
על כרחם כשיראו את גבורתי לישראל יודו כל העכו"ם כי אלהים אני:
rashi.eng: *His praise from the end of the earth.* Perforce, when they see My mighty deeds for Israel, all the heathens (nations [Parshandatha, K’li Paz]) will admit that I am God.

rashi.heb:
*יורדי הים.* 
פורשי בספינות:
rashi.eng: *those who go down to the sea.* Those who embark in ships.

rashi.heb:
*ומלואו.* 
הקבועים בים ולא באיים אלא בתוך המים שופכים עפר כל אחד ואחד כדי בית והולכים מבית לבית בספינה כגון עיר ווניציי"א:
rashi.eng: *and those therein.* Those whose permanent residence is in the sea and not in the islands, but in the midst of the water, they spill earth, each one of them, enough for a house, and go from house to house by boat, like the city of Venice. [As in Warsaw ed. and Parshandatha.]

rashi.heb:
*ישאו מדבר.* 
קול בשיר:
rashi.eng: *The desert and its cities shall raise [their voice].* their voice in song.

rashi.heb:
*חצרים תשב קדר.* 
(מוסב על ישאו) מדבר קדר שהם דרים עתה באוהלים ישאו קול וירונו (כמו והחצרים אשר תשב קדר), במדבר קדר שהם דרים עתה באהליהם יהיו ערים וחצרים קבועים:
rashi.eng: *Kedar shall be inhabited with villages.* (Connected to “The desert… shall raise.” The desert of Kedar, where they now dwell in tents, shall raise their voice and sing. It is like: And the villages with which Kedar is settled.) The desert of Kedar, where they now dwell in tents, will be permanent cities and villages.

rashi.heb:
*יושבי סלע.* 
המתים שיחיו כן ת"י:
rashi.eng: *rock dwellers.* The dead who will be resurrected. So did Jonathan render this.

rashi.heb:
*מראש הרים יצווחו.* 
מריש טוריא ירימון קליהון:
rashi.eng: *from the mountain peaks they shall shout.* From the mountain peaks they shall raise their voices [from Jonathan].

notes.1808: (tn, Heb): “Let them ascribe to the Lord glory.”
notes.1809: (tn, Heb): “and his praise in the coastlands [or “islands”] let them declare.”

notes.1810: (tn, Heb): “like a man of war he stirs up zeal” (NIV similar).
notes.1811: (tn): Or perhaps, “he triumphs over his enemies” (cf. NIV); NLT “will crush all his enemies.”

notes.1812: (tn, Heb): “silent” (so NASB, NIV, TEV, NLT); CEV “have held my temper.”
notes.1813: (sn): The imagery depicts the Lord as a warrior who is eager to fight and can no longer hold himself back from the attack.

rashi.heb:
*החשיתי מעולם.* 
זה ימים רבים החשיתי על חרבן ביתי ותמיד אחריש:
rashi.eng: *I was silent from time immemorial.* Already for a long time I have been silent about the destruction of My Temple, and always…

rashi.heb:
*אתאפק.* 
לשון הווה עד עתה הציקתני רוחי ומעתה כיולדה אפעה:
rashi.eng: *I am still; I restrain Myself.* This is present tense. Until now My spirit has constrained Me, and from now, like a travailing woman will I cry.

rashi.heb:
*אשום.* 
אתבהל:
rashi.eng: *I will be terrified.* Heb. אֶשֹּׁם, I will be terrified.

rashi.heb:
*ואשאף.* 
ואתאוה להשמיד הכל יחד כל אויבי:
rashi.eng: *and destroy [them] together.* And I will long to destroy everyone together, all My adversaries.

notes.1814: (tn, Heb): “I will dry up the mountains and hills.” The “mountains and hills” stand by synecdoche for the trees that grow on them. Some prefer to derive the verb from a homonymic root and translate, “I will lay waste.”
notes.1815: (tc): The Hebrew text reads, “I will turn streams into coastlands [or “islands”].” Scholars who believe that this reading makes little sense have proposed an emendation of אִיִּים (’iyyim, “islands”) to צִיּוֹת (tsiyyot, “dry places”; cf. NCV, NLT, TEV). However, since all the versions support the MT reading, there is insufficient grounds for an emendation here. Although the imagery of changing rivers into islands is somewhat strange, J. N. Oswalt describes this imagery against the backdrop of rivers of the Near East. The receding of these rivers at times occasioned the appearance of previously submerged islands (Isaiah [NICOT], 2:126).
notes.1816: (sn): The imagery of this verse, which depicts the Lord bringing a curse of infertility to the earth, metaphorically describes how the Lord will destroy his enemies.

rashi.heb:
*אחריב הרים וגבעות.* 
אהרוג מלכים ושלטונים של עכו"ם:
rashi.eng: *I will destroy mountains and hills.* I will slay kings and rulers.

rashi.heb:
*וכל עשבם.* 
כל הנלוים עליהם:
rashi.eng: *and all their grass.* All their followers.

rashi.heb:
*אוביש.* 
ל' יובש הוא לענין דבר לח כגון עשב ונהרות:
rashi.eng: *I will dry out.* Heb. אוֹבִישׁ. This is an expression of drying, used in reference to wet things, e.g., grass and rivers.

notes.1817: (tn, Heb): “a way they do not know” (so NASB); NRSV “a road they do not know.”
notes.1818: (tn, Heb): “in paths they do not know I will make them walk.”
notes.1819: (tn, Heb): “and the rough ground into a level place.”

rashi.heb:
*והולכתי.* 
ישראל שהיו עורים עד הנה מהביט אלי בדרך הטוב אשר לא ידעו להלוך בה:
rashi.eng: *And I will lead the blind.* Israel, who were heretofore blind from looking to Me, I will lead in the good way, upon which they did not know to walk.

rashi.heb:
*עשיתים.* 
אעשה כן ל' נבואה לדבר על העתיד כאילו עשוי:
rashi.eng: *I will do them.* Heb. עֲשִׂיתִם [lit. I did them], I will do. So is the language of prophecy, to speak of the future as if it was already done.

notes.1820: (tn, Heb): “be ashamed with shame”; ASV, NASB “be utterly put to shame.”

notes.1821: (tn, Heb): “look to see”; NAB, NCV “look and see”; NRSV “look up and see.”

rashi.heb:
*החרשים.* 
והעורים על ישראל הוא אומר:
rashi.eng: *You deaf ones… and you blind ones.* He is referring to Israel.

notes.1822: (tc): The precise meaning of מְשֻׁלָּם (m�shullam) in this context is uncertain. In later biblical Hebrew the form (which appears to be a Pual participle from the root שָׁלַם, shalam) occurs as a proper name, Meshullam. The Pual of שָׁלַם (“be complete”) is attested with the meaning “repaid, requited,” but that makes little sense here. BDB 1023 s.v. שָׁלַם relates the form to the denominative verb שָׁלַם (“be at peace”) and paraphrases “one in a covenant of peace” (J. N. Oswalt suggests “the covenanted one”; Isaiah [NICOT], 2:128, n. 59) Some emend the form to מֹשְׁלָם (mosh�lam, “their ruler”) or to מְשֻׁלָּחִי (m�shullakhi, “my sent [or “commissioned”] one”), which fits nicely in the parallelism (note “my messenger” in the previous line). The translation above assumes an emendation to כְּמוֹ שֹׁלְמִי (k�mo shol�mi, “like my ally”). Isaiah uses כְּמוֹ in 30:22 and perhaps 51:5; for שֹׁלְמי (“my ally”) see Ps 7:5 HT (7:4 ET).
notes.1823: (tn, Heb): “Who is blind but my servant, and deaf like my messenger I send? Who is blind like my commissioned one, blind like the servant of the Lord?” The point of the rhetorical questions is that no one is as blind/deaf as this servant. In this context the Lord’s “servant” is exiled Israel (cf. 41:8-9), which is spiritually blind and deaf and has failed to fulfill God’s purpose for it. This servant stands in contrast to the ideal “Israel” of the servant songs.

rashi.heb:
*מי עור.* 
בכם אין אחד כי אם עבדי הוא העור שבכלכם, וחרש שבכם הרי הוא כמלאכי אשר אני שולח להנבא נבואות:
rashi.eng: *Who is blind.* among you? There is no one but My servant; he is the most blind of all of you. And the most deaf among you is like My messenger whom I send to prophesy prophecies.

rashi.heb:
*מי עור כמשולם.* 
מי היה עור בכם כבר קבל יסוריו והרי הוא כמשולם כל תגמוליו ויוצא נקי:
rashi.eng: *He who was blind is as the one who received his payment.* He who was blind among you has already received his chastisements, and he is as one who was paid all payments due him and has emerged cleansed.

notes.1824: (tn): The consonantal text (Kethib) has a perfect, 2nd person masculine singular; the marginal reading (Qere) has an infinitive absolute, which functions here as a finite verb.
notes.1825: (tn, Heb): “but you do not guard [i.e., retain in your memory]”; NIV “but have paid no attention.”

rashi.heb:
*ראות רבות.* 
ראיות הרבה לפניכם ואינכם שומרים להביט במעשי ולשוב אלי:
rashi.eng: *There is much to see.* There are many sights before you, and you do not observe to look at My deeds and to return to Me.

rashi.heb:
*פקוח אזנים.* 
אני עסוק לפקוח אזניכם ע"י נביאי ולא ישמע איש מכם את דברי ולשון הוה הוא:
rashi.eng: *to open the ears.* I am busy opening your ears through My prophets, but none of you listens to My words. This is a present tense.

notes.1826: (tn, Heb): “The Lord was pleased for the sake of his righteousness [or “justice”], he was magnifying [the] law and was making [it] glorious.” The Lord contrasts his good intentions for the people with their present crisis (v. 22). To demonstrate his just character and attract the nations, the Lord wanted to showcase his law among and through Israel (Deut 4:5-8). But Israel disobeyed (v. 24) and failed to carry out their commission.

rashi.heb:
*ה' חפץ.* 
להראותכם ולפקוח אזניכם למען צדק ולכך הוא מגדיל ומאדיר לכם תורה:
rashi.eng: *The Lord desires.* to show you and to open your ears for His righteousness’ sake; therefore, he magnifies and strengthens the Torah for you.

notes.1827: (tc): The Hebrew text has בַּחוּרִים (bakhurim, “young men”), but the text should be emended to בְּהוֹרִים (b�horim, “in holes”).
notes.1828: (tn, Heb): “and made to be hidden”; NAB, NASB, NIV, TEV “hidden away in prisons.”
notes.1829: (tn, Heb): “they became loot and there was no one rescuing, plunder and there was no one saying, ‘Bring back’.”

rashi.heb:
*והוא.* 
העם הזה בזוי ושסוי וסוף הענין ולא ישים על לב כל זה לומר למה קראתנו זאת מי נתן למשיסה יעקב:
rashi.eng: *And it.* This people is despised and pillaged, and the end of the section is (infra v. 25) “And they laid not to heart” all of this to say, “Why did this befall me?” (v. 24) “Who subjected Jacob to plunder?”

rashi.heb:
*הפח בחורים כולם.* 
בחוריהם פחי נפש כולם, תו' ד"א הפח בחורים כולם ישימו את עצמם בפחי האדמה ובחורים ובבתי כלאים החבאו יוכיח שכן הוא:
rashi.eng: *all their youths are grieved.* Heb. הָפֵח ַבַּחוּרִים, all their youths are grieved. [Addendum: Another explanation of הָפֵח בַּחוּרִים כֻּלָם They will put themselves into snares (פַּחֵי) of the earth and into pits. [The clause,] “And they are hidden in dungeons,” proves that this is so.]

rashi.heb:
*ואין אומר השב.* 
כמו השב לפיכך הוא רפי אבל השב באמתחתינו הוא דגש:
rashi.eng: *and no one says, “Return.”.* Heb. הָשַׁב, like הָשֵׁב [the imperative]. Therefore, it is not punctuated with a dagesh, but (Gen. 43:17) “That returned (הַשָּׁב) in our sacks,” is punctuated with a ‘dagesh.’

notes.1830: (tn): The interrogative particle is understood in the second line by ellipsis (note the preceding line).

rashi.heb:
*יאזין.* 
לתת לב לזאת מי נתן למשיסה יעקב:
rashi.eng: *will hearken.* to pay attention to this, “Who subjected Jacob to plunder?”

rashi.heb:
*לאחור.* 
יקשיב וישמע דבר שיעמוד לו באחרונה וכן ת"י לאחור לסופ' וכן כל לאחור שבמקררא עתיד להיות הוא:
rashi.eng: *for the future.* Who will hearken and hear something that will stand him in good stead at the end? Jonathan, too, renders: לְסוֹפָא, at the end, and likewise, every לְאָחוֹר in Scripture refers to something that is destined to be.

notes.1831: (tn, Heb): “Who gave to the robber Jacob, and Israel to the looters?” In the first line the consonantal text (Kethib) has מְשׁוֹסֶה (m�shoseh), a Polel participle from שָׁסָה (shasah, “plunder”). The marginal reading (Qere) is מְשִׁיסָּה (m�shissah), a noun meaning “plunder.” In this case one could translate “Who handed Jacob over as plunder?”
notes.1832: (tn, Heb): “they were not willing in his ways to walk, and they did not listen to his law.”

rashi.heb:
*זו חטאנו לו.* 
זו היא שגרמה את המשיסה והבז את אשר חטאנו לו:
rashi.eng: *This, that we sinned against Him.* This is what caused the plunder and the spoiling, what we sinned against Him.

rashi.heb:
*ולא אבו.* 
אבותינו בדרכיו הלוך:
rashi.eng: *and they did not want.* Our forefathers did not want to go in His ways.

notes.1833: (tn, Heb): “strength” (so KJV, NASB); NAB “fury”; NASB “fierceness”; NIV “violence.”
notes.1834: (tn, Heb): “and it blazed against him all around, but he did not know.” The subject of the third feminine singular verb “blazed” is the divine חֵמָה (khemah, “anger”) mentioned in the previous line.
notes.1835: (tn, Heb): “and it burned against him, but he did not set [it] upon [the] heart.”

rashi.heb:
*ותלהטהו מסביב.* 
כדי שיראו ויקחו מוסר כענין שנאמ' (צפניה ג ו) הכרתי גוים נשמו פנותם אמרתי אך תיראי וגו':
rashi.eng: *and it blazed upon them all around.* I brought retribution upon the heathens ([Ms.] nations) all around so that they see and learn their lesson, like the matter stated (Zeph. 3:6f.): “I cut off nations, their towers were desolate… I said, You shall but fear Me, you shall learn a lesson…” ([This appears in certain manuscripts and in printed editions. In Nach Lublin, the reading is:] So that Israel see and learn a lesson.)

rashi.heb:
*ולא ידע.* 
יודע הוא אלא שדש בעקב לא חש להבין זאת ולשוב מרשעו:
rashi.eng: *and they did not know.* They actually did know, but they trod with their heels. They did not care to understand this and to repent of their wickedness.

rashi.heb:
*ותבער בו.* 
אחר פורענו' העכו"ם שמסביב בערה בעצמו:
rashi.eng: *and it burned among them.* After the retribution of the heathens ([ms.] nations) around, it burned upon them themselves.

notes.1836: (tn): Or “redeem.” See the note at 41:14. Cf. NCV “saved you”; CEV “rescued you”; NLT “ransomed you.”

rashi.heb:
*ועתה.* 
אף כל זאת כה אמר ה' אל תירא:
rashi.eng: *And now.* despite all this, so said the Lord, “… do not fear.”

notes.1837: (tn): The verb is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
notes.1838: (tn, Heb): “burn” (so NASB); NAB, NRSV, NLT “consume”; NIV “set you ablaze.”

rashi.heb:
*כי תעבר במים.* 
כשעברת בים סוף אתך הייתי:
rashi.eng: *When you pass through water.* When you passed through the Reed Sea, I was with you.

rashi.heb:
*ובנהרות לא ישטפוך.* 
גרתה בין המצרים והאומות המרובין כמי נהר ולא יכלו לך לכלות:
rashi.eng: *and in rivers, they shall not overflow you.* You dwelt among the Egyptians and the heathens (peoples [: mss.]) numerous as the waters of a river, and they could not prevail against you to destroy you.

rashi.heb:
*כי תלך במו אש.* 
לעתיד לבא כי הנה היום בא בוער כתנור (מלאכי ג׳:י״ט) שאקדיר חמה על הרשעים וליהט אותם היום הבא (שם) גם שם לא תכוה:
rashi.eng: *when you go amidst fire.* In the future, “For behold, a sun is coming, burning like an oven” (Malachi 3:19), for I will cause the sun to burn upon the wicked, “and the coming sun shall burn them.” There, too, you shall not be burnt.

rashi.heb:
*ולהבה.* 
שתשרוף האומות כמו שנאמר והיו עמים משרפות סיר גם היא לא תבער בך:
rashi.eng: *a flame.* which shall burn the heathens ([mss.:] the nations), as it is said (supra 33:12): “And the peoples shall be as the burnings of lime.” That too shall not burn amidst you.

notes.1839: (sn): See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.
notes.1840: (sn): Seba is not the same as Sheba in southern Arabia; cf. Gen 1:10; 1 Chr 1:9.

rashi.heb:
*נתתי כפרך מצרים.* 
והם היו לך לפדיון שבכוריהם מתו ואתה בני בכורי נצלת והייתם חייבים כליה כמו שנאמר (ביחזקאל כ׳:ח׳) ואומר לשפוך חמתי עליהם בארץ מצרים:
rashi.eng: *I have given Egypt as your ransom.* And they were your ransom, for their firstborn died, and you, My firstborn son, although you were deserving of destruction, as it is said in Ezekiel (20:8): “And I thought to pour out My fury upon them… in the land of Egypt.”

notes.1841: (tn, Heb): “Since you are precious in my eyes and you are honored.”

rashi.heb:
*ואתן אדם תחתיך.* 
תמיד אני רגיל בכך:
rashi.eng: *and I give.* I am always accustomed to this.

rashi.heb:
*אומר.* 
לרוח צפון תני הגליות שבצפון:
rashi.eng: *I will say.* to the north wind, “Give the exiles who are in the north.”

rashi.heb:
*ולתימן.* 
שהיא רוח חזקה אל תכלאי מלנשב בחזקה להביא גליותי וכן (שיר השירים ד׳:ט״ז) עורי צפון ובאי תימן מתוך שהרוח צפונית חלשה צריכה חיזוק לכך כתוב עורי תני. אבל דרומית שאינה צריכה חיזוק כתוב בואי כמות שהיא וכן ואל תכלאי:
rashi.eng: *and to the south.* which is a strong wind, “Do not refrain from blowing strongly to bring My exiles.” Similarly (Song 4:16), “Awaken, O north wind, and come, O south wind.” Since the north wind is weak, it needs strengthening. Therefore, it is written, “Awaken”, “Give.” But concerning the south wind which does not need straightening, it is written, “Come,” as it is, and so, “Do not refrain.”

notes.1842: (tn, Heb): “everyone who is called by my name” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*כל הנקרא בשמי ולכבודי בראתיו.* 
כל הצדיקים הנקראים בשמי וכל העשוי לכבודי יצרתיו אף עשיתיו תכנתיו בכל הצריך לו והכנתי הכל כלומר אע"פ שעברו בגולה ובצרה כבר הכנתי להם כל צרכי גאולתם:
rashi.eng: *Everyone that is called by My name, and whom I created for My glory.* All the righteous, who are called by My name and everyone who was made for My glory, I formed him, yea, I made him. fixed him with all that is necessary for him, and I prepared everything. That is to say, that although they experienced exile and trouble, I prepared for them all the necessities of their redemption.

rashi.heb:
*הוציא עם עור.* 
הוציא כמו להוציא מן הגולה אותם שגלו על שנעשו כעורים ועינים להם ולא ראו:
rashi.eng: *To bring out a blind people.* Heb. הוֹצִיא, like לְהוֹצִיא to bring out of the exile those who were exiled because they became like blind; although they had eyes, they did not see.

notes.1843: (tn, Heb): “and the former things was causing us to hear?”

rashi.heb:
*כל הגוים נקבצו.* 
אם כל הגוים מעכו"ם נתקבצו יחדיו מי בהם ובנביאיהם יגיד עתידות וכיוצא בה מפי טעותם או הראשונות שכבר עברו ישמיעונו לאמר אנחנו הגדנו אותם קודם שבאו:
rashi.eng: *Were all the nations gathered.* If all the nations (of the peoples [Lublin;]) (of the heathens [Warsaw]; absent in all mss. and in K’li Paz) would gather together, who of them and of their prophets would tell the future, or the like, quoting their pagan Gods, or the first events, that have already passed, would they let us know, saying “We foretold them before they came about” ?

rashi.heb:
*יתנו עדיהם.* 
ששמעו שנבאו עליהם קודם לכן ויצדקו אבל אני יש לי עדים שאתם עדי שהגדתי לאברהם אביכם הגליות ובאו:
rashi.eng: *Let them present their witnesses.* who heard that they prophesied concerning them prior to their occurrence, and they shall be deemed just. But I have witnesses, for you are My witnesses that I told Abraham your forefather about the exiles, and they came about.

notes.1845: (tn, Heb): “and after me, there will not be”; NASB “there will be none after Me.”

rashi.heb:
*ועבדי.* 
יעקב:
rashi.eng: *and My servant.* Jacob.

rashi.heb:
*אשר בחרתי.* 
הוא יעיד שהבטחתיו בלכתו לארם נהרים ושמרתי הבטחתי:
rashi.eng: *whom I chose..* He, too, shall testify that I promised him when he went to Mesopotamia, and I kept My promise.

rashi.heb:
*למען תדעו וגו'.* 
כל זה עשיתי למען תתנו לב לדעת אותי:
rashi.eng: *in order that you know.* I did all this in order that you put your heart to know Me.

rashi.heb:
*אנכי הגדתי.* 
הגליות לאברהם:
rashi.eng: *I told.* of the exiles to Abraham.

rashi.heb:
*והושעתי.* 
לקיים דברי בעת רץ:
rashi.eng: *and I saved.* to fulfill the word at the time [designated for its] end.

rashi.heb:
*והשמעתי.* 
לכם הראשונו':
rashi.eng: *and I made heard.* to you the first events.

rashi.heb:
*ואין בכם זר.* 
באותן הימים שעשיתי כל אלה לא נראה בכולכם ביני העכו"ם אל זר להראות גדולתו ואלהותו בפני:
rashi.eng: *and there was no stranger among you.* In those days, when I did all these, there did not appear among all of you, among the heathens (the children of the nations [mss., K’li Paz]) a strange God, to show his greatness and his Godliness. ([Other manuscripts read:] And I made My Torah heard to you, and none among you estranged himself from accepting.)

rashi.heb:
*ואתם עדי.* 
שפתחתי לכם שבעה רקיעי' ולא ראיתם כל תמונה:
rashi.eng: *and you are My witnesses.* that I opened seven heavens for you, and you saw no image.

notes.1846: (tn, Heb): “hand” (so KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NLT “No one can oppose what I do.”

rashi.heb:
*גם מיום אני הוא.* 
לא אותו היום לבדו הייתי לבדי כי גם מאז היות יום אני הוא לבדי:
rashi.eng: *Even before the day I am He.* Not only that day was I alone, but even before it became day I am He alone.

rashi.heb:
*אפעל.* 
אם באתי לפעול אין משיב:
rashi.eng: *I do.* If I came to do, no one can retract.

notes.1847: (tn): Or “kinsman redeemer.” See the note at 41:14.
notes.1848: (sn): See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.
notes.1849: (tn, Heb): “and I bring down [as] fugitives all of them.”
notes.1850: (tn): The Hebrew text reads literally, “as for the Babylonians, in ships their joyful shout.” This might be paraphrased, “even the Babylonians in the ships [over which] they joyfully shouted.” The point would be that the Lord caused the Babylonians to flee for safety in the ships in which they took such great pride. A slight change in vocalization yields the reading “into mourning songs,” which provides a good contrast with “joyful shout.” The prefixed bet (בְּ) would indicate identity.

rashi.heb:
*למענכם שלחתי בבלה.* 
י"ת בדיל חוביכון אגליתי יתכון לבבל:
rashi.eng: *Because of you, I sent [you] to Babylon.* Jonathan paraphrases: Because of your sins I exiled you to Babylon.

rashi.heb:
*והורדתי בריחים כולם.* 
ואחתית במשוטין כולהון משוטין הוא עץ שמנהיג את הספינה ומיישרה:
rashi.eng: *and I lowered them all with oars.* Heb. בָרִיחִים וְהוֹרַדְתִּי. Jonathan renders: And I lowered with oars (בִּמְשׁוֹטִין), all of them. מְשׁוֹטִין denotes the wood that guides the ship and straightens it out.

rashi.heb:
*וכשדים.* 
הוליכו אתכם באניות רנתם וגם יש לפרשו על בשורת הגאולה:
rashi.eng: *and Chaldees.* led you in the ships of their rejoicing. This may also be explained as regards the news of the redemption, as follows:

rashi.heb: *למענכם שלחתי.* אשלח מלכי מדי לבבל ואוריד הכשדים בספינות ומשוטין לגולה לארץ מדי, וכשדים אוריד באניות שהיתה רינתם בהם:
rashi.eng: *Because of you, I sent.* I will send the kings of Media to Babylon, and I will lower the Chaldees in ships and oars into exile to the land of Media. And the Chaldees I will lower in ships which their rejoicing was [i.e., the Chaldees would be taken into captivity with the very boats in which they had previously rejoiced].

notes.1851: (sn): See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

rashi.heb:
*הנותן בים דרך.* 
בים סוף ושם הוצאתי מצרים לרדוף אחריכם רכב וסוס וחיל ועיזוז וכולם יחדיו ישכבו מתים על שפת הים בל יקומו:
rashi.eng: *Who made a way in the sea.* in the Sea of Reeds, and there I drew the Egyptians out to pursue you, with chariots and horses, and an army and power, and all of them lay together dead on the seashore, not to rise.

notes.1852: (tn, Heb): “led out chariots and horses.” The words “to destruction” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The verse refers to the destruction of the Egyptians at the Red Sea.
notes.1853: (tn, Heb): “lay down”; NAB “lie prostrate together”; CEV “lie dead”; NRSV “they lie down.”

rashi.heb:
*כפשתה כבו.* 
תירגם יונתן כבוצא עמי טפו:
rashi.eng: *they were quenched.* Jonathan renders: Like flax they dimmed, they were quenched.

notes.1854: (tn, Heb): “the former things” (so KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NLT “forget all that.”

rashi.heb:
*אל תזכרו ראשונות.* 
הניסים הללו שאני מזכיר לכם שעשיתי במצרים אל תזכרו אותם מעתה כי בגאולה זו תעסקו להודות ולהלל:
rashi.eng: *Remember not the first events.* These miracles that I mention to you, that I performed in Egypt do not remember them from now on, for you shall be engaged in this redemption, to thank and to praise.

rashi.heb:
*אל תתבוננו.* 
אל תסתכלו בהן אל תתנו להם לב:
rashi.eng: *do not meditate.* Do not ponder about them; do not pay attention to them.

notes.1856: (tn): Or “know” (KJV, ASV); NASB “be aware of”; NAB, NIV, NRSV “perceive.”
notes.1857: (tn): The Hebrew texts has “streams,” probably under the influence of v. 20. The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa has נתיבות (“paths”).

rashi.heb:
*תכבדני חית השדה.* 
מקום שהוא חרב ומרבץ לחיות השדה לתנים ולבנות יענה:
rashi.eng: *The beasts of the field shall honor Me.* The place that is desolate and a habitat of the beasts of the field, for the jackals and for the ostriches.

rashi.heb:
*כי נתתי במדבר מים.* 
כלומר בארץ חריבה אתן ישוב:
rashi.eng: *for I gave water in the desert.* i.e., in a desolate land I will place a settlement.

notes.1858: (tn, Heb): “[so] they might declare my praise.”

rashi.heb:
*עם זו יצרתי לי.* 
למען תהלתי יספרו:
rashi.eng: *This people I formed for Myself.* so that they recite My praise.

notes.1859: (tn): Or “strive”; KJV, ASV, NRSV “been weary of me.”

rashi.heb:
*ולא אותי קראת.* 
ואתה לא אותי קראת בפנותך אחרי עכו"ם:
rashi.eng: *But you did not call Me.* But you did not call Me in your turning after idolatry.

rashi.heb:
*כי יגעת בי.* 
נלאיתם מהר בעבודתי:
rashi.eng: *for you wearied of Me.* You quickly wearied of My worship.

notes.1860: (tn, Heb): “with.” The words “by demanding” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*לא הבאת לי שה עולותיך.* 
כ"א לעכו"ם:
rashi.eng: *You did not bring Me the lambs of your burnt offerings.* but to idolatry.

rashi.heb:
*לא העבדתיך.* 
עבודה רבה במנחה קומץ מעט עולה לגבוה וגם הוא לא אמרתי לך להקריב לך חובה אלא נדבה:
rashi.eng: *neither did I overwork you.* Cause you to do much work with the meal offering; merely a handful would be offered to the Most High, and even that I did not ordain upon you to sacrifice as an obligation but as a free-will offering.

notes.1861: (tn): That is, “calamus” (so NIV); NCV, TEV, NLT “incense”; CEV “spices.”
notes.1862: (tn, Heb): “you did not saturate me”; NASB “Neither have you filled Me.”
notes.1863: (sn): In vv. 22-24 the Lord appears to be condemning his people for failure to bring the proper sacrifices. However, this is problematic. If this refers to the nation’s behavior while in exile, such cultic service was impossible and could hardly be expected by the Lord. If this refers to the nation’s conduct before the exile, it contradicts other passages that depict Israel as bringing excessive sacrifices (see, e.g., Isa 1:11-14; Jer 6:20; Amos 4:4-5, 5:21-23). Rather than being a condemnation of Israel’s failure to bring sacrifices, these verses are better taken as a highly rhetorical comment on the worthlessness of Israel’s religious ritual. They may have brought sacrifices, but not to the Lord, for he did not accept them or even want them. See C. R. North, Second Isaiah, 127, and R. Whybray, Isaiah 40-66 (NCBC), 91.

rashi.heb:
*לא קנית לי בכסף קנה.* 
לקטרת לא הוצרכת לקנותה בכסף לפי שהיתה מצויה בארצכם הרבה אמר רבי אבא קינמני' היתה גדילה בארץ ישראל והיו אוכלין אותה עזים וצביים במדרש איכה:
rashi.eng: *Neither did you purchase cane for Me with money.* for incense. You did not have to purchase it with money, for it was very common in your land. Said Rabbi Abba: Cinnamon grew in the Land of Israel, and goats and deer would eat of it. In Midrash Eichah (Proem X). ([Some manuscripts read:]

rashi.heb: *לא קנית לי בכסף קנה.*
rashi.eng: *Neither did you purchase cane for Me with money.* for incense, for you failed to offer to Me what you should have, and you were attracted to idolatry.)

rashi.heb:
*העבדתני בחטאותיך.* 
אתם גרמתם לי להיות שמש לעובדי פסילים כמו שראה יחזקאל והנה רוח סערה באה מן הצפון שהיתה חוזרת מרכבת השכינה מבבל שהלכה לכבוש את כל העולם תחת ידו של נבוכדנצר שלא יאמרו ביד אומה שפלה מסר את בניו כדאיתא בחגיגה:
