rashi.eng: *But you have burdened Me.* [lit. you have overworked Me.] You have caused Me to be an attendant to pagans, as Ezekiel envisioned (1:4): “And behold a tempest was coming from the north.” For the chariot of the Shechinah was returning from Babylon, where it had gone to conquer the whole world under the domination of Nebuchadnezzar, lest they say that He delivered His children into the hands of an inferior nation, as is found in Hagigah (13b).

rashi.heb:
*אנכי אנכי.* 
אני הוא שמחיתים מאז ואני מוחה אותם גם עתה:
rashi.eng: *I, yea I.* I am He Who erased them from time immemorial [lit. from then], and I erase them even now.

rashi.heb:
*למעני.* 
לא בזכותך ולא בצדקת אבותיך:
rashi.eng: *for My sake.* Neither in your merit nor in the merit of your forefathers.

notes.1864: (tn, Heb): “you, tell in order that you may be right”; NAB “prove your innocence.”

rashi.heb:
*הזכירני.* 
כל תגמול שיש לך ולאבותיך עלי:
rashi.eng: *Remind Me.* all the reward I owe you and your forefathers.

rashi.heb:
*נשפטה יחד.* 
נבא למשפט:
rashi.eng: *let us stand in judgment.* [lit. let us be judged together.] Let us come to judgment.

notes.1865: (tn, Heb): “your first father.” This could refer to Abraham (see 51:2), but elsewhere in Isaiah he does not appear in a negative light (see 29:22; 41:8; 63:16). A more likely candidate is Jacob/Israel, also referred to as the nation’s “father” elsewhere (see 58:14; 63:16).
notes.1866: (tn): On the meaning of the term לִיץ (lits), see HALOT 590 s.v. מֵלִיץ. This may refer to the nation’s prophets, priests, and/or kings.

rashi.heb:
*אביך הראשון חטא.* 
באומרו במה אדע (בראשית טו):
rashi.eng: *Your first father sinned.* by saying (Gen. 15:8), “How will I know…?”

rashi.heb:
*ומליציך פשעו בי.* 
אין לך בכל מליצי' שאתה סומך על זכותם שלא מצאתי בו פשע יצחק אהב את שונאי:
rashi.eng: *and your intercessors transgressed against Me.* You have none among all the intercessors upon whose merit you rely, in whom I have not found transgression. Isaac loved My enemy [Esau].

notes.1867: (tn): The word “subjected” is supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*ואחלל שרי קדש.* 
בשביל עונותיכם:
rashi.eng: *And I profane the holy princes.* because of your iniquities.

rashi.heb:
*ועתה שמע.* 
לשוב לתורתי יעקב עבדי:
rashi.eng: *And now, hearken.* to return to My Torah, Jacob My servant.

notes.1868: (sn): Jeshurun is a poetic name for Israel; it occurs here and in Deut 32:15; 33:5, 26.

notes.1869: (tn, Heb): “the thirsty.” Parallelism suggests that dry ground is in view (see “dry land” in the next line.)
notes.1870: (tn, Heb): “and streams”; KJV “floods.” The verb “cause…to flow” is supplied in the second line for clarity and for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*כי אצק מים על צמא.* 
כמו שאני יוצק מים על צמא כן אצק רוחי על זרעך:
rashi.eng: *As I will pour water on the thirsty.* Just as I pour water on the thirsty, so will I pour My spirit on your seed.

notes.1871: (tn): The Hebrew term בֵין (ven) is usually taken as a preposition, in which case one might translate, “among the grass.” But בֵין is probably the name of a tree (cf. C. R. North, Second Isaiah, 133). If one alters the preposition bet (בְּ) to kaf (כְּ), one can then read, “like a binu-tree.” (The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa supports this reading.) This forms a nice parallel to “like poplars” in the next line. חָצִיר (khatsir) is functioning as an adverbial accusative of location.

rashi.heb:
*וצמחו בבין חציר.* 
בתוך עמלק על ידי גרים שיתוספו עליהם, בין חציר הוא עמלק שנאמר עליו והיתה נוה תנים חציר לבנות יענה (לעיל ד):
rashi.eng: *And they shall sprout among the grass.* among Esau (mss. and K’li Paz). [The Jewish nation will grow] through the proselytes who will join them. [The expression,] “among the grass” refers to Esau, for it is stated concerning Edom (supra 34:13): “And it shall be the habitat of jackals, an abode (חָצִיר) for ostriches.” (Editions reading, “Amalek,” are erroneous cf. reference.)

notes.1872: (tn): The Hebrew text has a Qal verb form, “and another will call by the name of Jacob.” With support from Symmachus (an ancient Greek textual witness), some read the Niphal, “and another will be called by the name of Jacob.”
notes.1873: (tn, Heb): “and by the name of Israel he will title.” Some, with support from several ancient versions, prefer to change the Piel (active) verb form to a Pual (passive), “and he will be titled by the name of Israel.”

rashi.heb:
*זה יאמר לה' אני.* 
אלו צדיקים גמורים:
rashi.eng: *This one shall say, “I am the Lord’s.”.* These are the perfectly righteous.

rashi.heb:
*וזה יקרא בשם יעקב.* 
אלו קטנים בני רשעים:
rashi.eng: *and this one shall call himself by the name of Jacob..* These are the children, the sons of the wicked.

rashi.heb:
*זה יכתוב ידו לה'.* 
אלו בעלי תשובה:
rashi.eng: *and this one shall write [with] his hand, “To the Lord,”.* These are the repentant.

rashi.heb:
*ובשם ישראל יכנה.* 
אלו הגרים מעכו"ם כך שנויה באבות דרבי נתן:
rashi.eng: *and adopt the name Israel.* These are the proselytes. So it was taught in Avoth d’Rabbi Nathan (36:1).

notes.1874: (tn, Heb): “his kinsman redeemer.” See the note at 41:14.

notes.1875: (tn, Heb): “let him call” or “let him proclaim” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV); NAB “Let him stand up and speak.”
notes.1876: (tc): The Hebrew text reads, “from (the time) I established an ancient people, and the coming things.” Various emendations have been proposed. One of the options assumes the reading מַשְׁמִיעִים מֵעוֹלָם אוֹתִיּוֹת (mashmi’im me’olam ’otiyyot); This literally reads “the ones causing to hear from antiquity coming things,” but more idiomatically would read “as for those who predict from antiquity what will happen” (cf. NAB, NEB, REB). The emendation directs the attention of the reader to those who claim to be able to predict the future, challenging them to actually do what they claim they can do. The MT presents Yahweh as an example to whom these alleged “predictors of the future” can compare themselves. Since the ancient versions are unanimous in their support of the MT, the emendations should be set aside.
notes.1877: (tn, Heb): and those things which are coming let them declare for themselves.”

rashi.heb:
*ומי כמוני יקרא.* 
ומי יקרא שהוא כמוני ויגיד ויערוך לי את כל מה שהיה משומי עם עולם ועד עתה:
rashi.eng: *And who will call [that he is] like Me.* And who will call that he is like Me and tell and arrange for me all that transpired since I placed the ancient people and until now?

rashi.heb:
*עם עולם.* 
כל בריות:
rashi.eng: *the ancient people.* All the creatures.

rashi.heb:
*ואותיות.* 
דברי מופת:
rashi.eng: *and the signs.* Marvelous things.

rashi.heb:
*ואשר תבאנה.* 
ואת העתידות לבא יגידו כמו שאני עושה עתה שעדיין לא חרב הבית ולא גליתם ולא נולד כורש ואני מבשר אתכם עליו:
rashi.eng: *and those that will come.* And those destined to come, let them tell, as I do now, for the Temple has not yet been destroyed, and you have not been exiled, and neither has Cyrus been born, but I am reporting it to you.

notes.1878: (tn): BDB 923 s.v. רָהָה derives this verb from an otherwise unattested root, while HALOT 403 s.v. יָרָה defines it as “be stupefied” on the basis of an Arabic cognate. The form is likely a corruption of תיראו, the reading attested in the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa.
notes.1879: (tn, Heb): “rock” or “rocky cliff,” a title that depicts God as a protective refuge in his role as sovereign king; thus the translation “sheltering rock.”

rashi.heb:
*ואל תרהו.* 
אין לו דמיון ופתרונו לפי הענין כמו אל תחתו מלהודיע את שמי לבין העכו"ם:
rashi.eng: *and be not dismayed.* Heb. תִּרְהוּ. There is no similar word, and its interpretation according to its context is like תֵּחַתּוּ, be not dismayed from making My name known among the heathens (nations [K’li Paz and mss.]).

rashi.heb:
*הלא מאז השמעתיך.* 
מהר סיני והגדתי לכם שם שאין אלוהי מבלעדי:
rashi.eng: *let you hear.* from Mount Sinai, and I told you there that there is no god besides Me.

rashi.heb:
*ואתם עדי.* 
שפתחתי לכם שבעה רקיעים והראיתי אתכם שאין אחר ואתם עדי בדבר הזה שאין אלוה מבלעדי:
rashi.eng: *and you are My witnesses.* that I opened for you seven heavens and showed you that there is no other, and you are My witnesses to this thing that there is no god besides Me.

rashi.heb:
*ואין צור בל ידעתי.* 
ת"י ולית דתקיף אלהן דמן קדמי מתיהב ליה תקיף:
rashi.eng: *and there is no rock I did not know.* Jonathan renders: And there is no strong one unless he is given strength by Me.

rashi.heb:
*בל ידעתי.* 
לשון ואדעך בשם (שמות ל״ג:י״ז) ידע לכתך (דברים ב׳:ז׳) אני ידעתיך במדבר (הושע י״ג:ה׳):
rashi.eng: *I did not know.* Heb. יָדַעְתִּי. An expression similar to (Exodus 33:17) “And I knew you by name (וָאֵדָעֲךָ);” (Deut. 2:7) “He knew (יָדַע) your going;” (Hosea 13:5) “I knew you (יְדַעְתִּיךָ) in the desert.”

rashi.heb:
*ועדיהם המה.* 
הפסילי' הם עדים על בושת עובדיהם שהרי אנו רואין שאינן לא רואין ולא יודעין והיו עובדין להם:
rashi.eng: *and they are their witnesses.* The idols are witnesses of the shame of their worshipers, for we see that they neither see nor know, yet they were worshiping them.

rashi.heb:
*למען יבושו.* 
העובדים להם:
rashi.eng: *so that they be ashamed.* Those who worship them.

notes.1880: (tn): The rhetorical question is sarcastic. The sense is, “Who is foolish enough…?”

rashi.heb:
*נסך.* 
לשון יציקה ומסכה והנו"ן בתיבה יסוד הנופל ממנו כגון נו"ן של נשך ושל נגף:
rashi.eng: *molded.* Heb. נָסָךְ, an expression of pouring and a molten image (מַסֵּכָה). The ‘nun’ in the word is a radical sometimes omitted, e.g., the ‘nun’ of נשך, biting, and of נגף, plaguing.

notes.1881: (tn): The pronoun “his” probably refers to the one who forms/casts an idol (v. 10), in which case it refers to the craftsman’s associates in the idol-manufacturing guild.
notes.1882: (sn): The point seems to be this: If the idols are the mere products of human hands, then those who trust in them will be disappointed, for man-made gods are incapable of helping their “creators.”

rashi.heb:
*הן כל חביריו.* 
של אותו יוצר ונוסך פסילים המתחברים אליו לעבוד את יצירתו ונסכו יבושו:
rashi.eng: *Behold, all his colleagues.* of that fashioner and molder of graven images, who join him to worship his creation and his molten image, shall be ashamed.

rashi.heb:
*וחרשים המה.* 
אותם יוצרים ונוסכים מבני אדם הם קל וחומר ליצירתם שהיא הבל:
rashi.eng: *and they are smiths.* those fashioners and molders, and they are of men, surely their creation is vanity.

notes.1883: (tn): The noun מַעֲצָד (ma’atsad), which refers to some type of tool used for cutting, occurs only here and in Jer 10:3. See HALOT 615 s.v. מַעֲצָד.
notes.1884: (tn): Some English versions take the pronoun “it” to refer to an idol being fashioned by the blacksmith (cf. NIV, NCV, CEV). NLT understands the referent to be “a sharp tool,” which is then used by the carpenter in the following verse to carve an idol from wood.
notes.1885: (tn, Heb): “and there is no strength”; NASB “his strength fails.”

rashi.heb:
*חרש ברזל.* 
חרש של ברזל:
rashi.eng: *The ironsmith.* a smith of iron.

rashi.heb:
*מעצד.* 
הוא אחד מכלי הנפחים:
rashi.eng: *an axe.* Heb. מַעֲצָד. That is one of the tools of the blacksmiths.

rashi.heb:
*ופעל.* 
הפסל:
rashi.eng: *and he works.* the image.

rashi.heb:
*בפחם.* 
קרבו"ן בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *with coal.* Heb. פֶּחָם, charbon in French.

rashi.heb:
*ובמקבות.* 
מרטי"ל בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and with sledge hammers.* Heb. מַקָּבוֹת, marteau in French.

rashi.heb:
*יצרהו.* 
ל' ציור:
rashi.eng: *he fashions it.* Heb. יִצְּרֵהוּ, an expression of fashioning.

rashi.heb:
*ויפעלהו בזרוע כחו גם רעב וגו'.* 
גם הוא היוצר חסר כח וחלש הוא שאם ירעב אין בו כח או אם לא שתה מים ויעף לאלתר קל וחומר שפעולתו אין בה תועלת לעזור:
rashi.eng: *and he made it with his strong arm; yea he is hungry etc..* Even he, the fashioner, lacks strength and is weak, for if he becomes hungry he has no strength, or if he does not drink water, he becomes faint immediately. Surely his product has no power to help.

notes.1886: (tn, Heb): “stretches out a line” (ASV similar); NIV “measures with a line.”
notes.1887: (tn, Heb): “he makes an outline with the [?].” The noun שֶׂרֶד (shered) occurs only here; it apparently refers to some type of tool or marker. Cf. KJV “with a line”; ASV “with a pencil”; NAB, NRSV “with a stylus”; NASB “with red chalk”; NIV “with a marker.”
notes.1888: (tn, Heb): “works” (so NASB) or “fashions” (so NRSV); NIV “he roughs it out.”
notes.1889: (tn, Heb): “he makes it like the pattern of a man”; NAB “like a man in appearance.”
notes.1890: (tn, Heb): “like the glory of man to sit [in] a house”; NIV “that it may dwell in a shrine.”

rashi.heb:
*חרש עצים.* 
ואם בא לעשותו של עץ וחרש עצים הוא כך דרכו:
rashi.eng: *The carpenter.* And if he comes to make it of wood, and he is a carpenter, the following is his method.

rashi.heb:
*נטה קו.* 
כדרך הנגרים ועל פי הקו יתארהו בשרד מיישר אותו במסור שקורין דאלאור"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *stretched out a line.* as is the custom of the carpenters, and according to the line, יְתָאֲרֵהוּ בַשֶּׂרֶד, he straightens it with a saw, which they call doloire in French.

rashi.heb: *יתארהו.*  ייפהו:
rashi.eng: *he beautifies it.* Heb. יְתָאֲרֵהוּ, he beautifies it.

rashi.heb:
*יעשהו במקצועות.* 
ומחליקו ברהיטני ואיזמל, מקצועות ת"י אזמליא:
rashi.eng: *he fixes it with planes.* Heb. מַקְצֻעוֹת. He smoothes it with a plane and a blade. Jonathan renders מַקְצֻעוֹת as אִיזְמֵלַיָּא, knives or blades.

rashi.heb:
*ובמחוגה יתארהו.* 
לשון ותאר הגבול (יהושע ט״ו:ט׳) אם בא לעשו' בו ציורים עגולים מסבב אותו במחוגה קונפ"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and with a compass he rounds it.* Heb. יְתָאֳרֵהוּ, an expression similar to (Josh. 15:9): “And the border circled (וְתָאַר).” If he comes to make circular drawings, he draws around it with a compass, compas in French.

rashi.heb:
*כתפארת אדם.* 
היא האשה שהיא תפארת בעלה:
rashi.eng: *like the beauty of a man.* That is a woman, who is the beauty of her husband.

notes.1891: (tn): It is not certain what type of tree this otherwise unattested noun refers to. Cf. ASV “a holm-tree” (NRSV similar).
notes.1892: (tn, Heb): “strengthens for himself,” i.e., “secures for himself” (see BDB 55 s.v. אָמֵץ Pi.2).
notes.1893: (tn): Some prefer to emend אֹרֶן (’oren) to אֶרֶז (’erez, “cedar”), but the otherwise unattested noun appears to have an Akkadian cognate, meaning “cedar.” See H. R. Cohen, Biblical Hapax Legomena (SBLDS), 44-45. HALOT 90 s.v. I אֹרֶן offers the meaning “laurel.”

rashi.heb:
*תרזה ואלון.* 
מיני אילני סרק:
rashi.eng: *ilex and an oak.* kinds of non-fruit-producing trees.

rashi.heb:
*ויאמץ לו בעצי יער.* 
עושה לו חיזוקי' בין לחיזוק בין לנוי במיני עצי' המשונים זה מזה במראיהן:
rashi.eng: *and he reinforced it with forest trees.* He makes for it types of reinforcements, either for strength or for beauty, with types of trees, one different from the other in their appearance.

rashi.heb:
*נטע אורן.* 
כשמוצא ייחור ונטע הראוי לכך נוטעו לכך והגשם מגדלו:
rashi.eng: *he planted a sapling.* When he finds a branch or a sapling that is fit for that, he plants it for that and the rain makes it grow.

rashi.heb:
*אורן.* 
ל' נטע יונק פלנצו"ן בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *a sapling.* Heb. אֹרֶן, a young sapling, ploncon in O.F.

notes.1894: (tn, Heb): “and it becomes burning [i.e., firewood] for a man”; NAB “to serve man for fuel.”

rashi.heb:
*והיה לאדם לבער.* 
והיה אותו עץ מקצתו לצרכי אדם לבער:
rashi.eng: *And it was for man to ignite.* And part of that very tree was for man’s necessities, [viz.] to ignite.

rashi.heb:
*ויקח.* 
מן העצים:
rashi.eng: *and he took.* from the trees.

rashi.heb: *ויחם.*  גופו לנגדם:
rashi.eng: *and he warmed.* his body opposite them.

rashi.heb:
*אף ישיק.* 
מהם תנור ואופה לחם:
rashi.eng: *he even heated.* an oven with them and baked bread.

rashi.heb:
*אף יפעל אל.* 
מן הנותר:
rashi.eng: *he even made a god.* from what was left over.

notes.1897: (tn, Heb): “for their eyes are smeared over so they cannot see, so their heart cannot be wise.”

notes.1898: (tn): There is no formal interrogative sign here, but the context seems to indicate these are rhetorical questions. See GKC 473 �150.a.

rashi.heb:
*ולא ישיב אל לבו.* 
חציו שרפתי במו אש:
rashi.eng: *And he does not give it thought.* [lit. and he does not return to his heart.] Half of it I burnt with fire.

rashi.heb:
*ולא דעת ולא תבונה.* 
בו לאמר זאת:
rashi.eng: *and he has neither knowledge nor understanding.* [lit. and there is neither knowledge nor understanding] in him to say this.

rashi.heb:
*לבול עץ.* 
לרקבון עץ:
rashi.eng: *to rotten wood.* Heb. לְבוּל עֵץ, to decay of wood.

notes.1899: (tn): Or perhaps, “he eats on an ash heap.”
notes.1900: (tn, Heb): “Is it not a lie in my right hand?”

rashi.heb:
*רועה אפר לב הותל הטהו.* 
לבו אשר הותל הטהו לעשות לו רועה של אפר הדמות שנשרף חציו ונעשה אפר השוטה הזה היה אומר שהוא לו לרועה ולמפרנס, דבר אחר רועה אפר ל' ריעות עובד עבודת אחרים ומחבר אליו עבודת אחרים שהיא אפר:
rashi.eng: *[To] a provider [made] of ashes, a deceived heart has perverted him.* His heart, which was deceived, turned him aside to make for himself a provider of ashes. The image, half of which was burned and made into ashes, this fool says that it is his provider and patron. Another explanation: אֵפֶר רוֹעֶה is an expression of companionship. One who worships idols associates himself with the idol, which is ash.

rashi.heb:
*ולא יציל.* 
הנתעה את נפשו לאמר הלא שקר בימיני ויפרד מעליו:
rashi.eng: *and he shall not save.* [i.e.,] the misled one shall not save his soul, saying, “Is there not falsehood in my right hand?” and separate from it.

notes.1901: (tc): The verb in the Hebrew text is a Niphal imperfect with a pronominal suffix. Although the Niphal ordinarily has the passive sense, it can have a reflexive nuance as well (see above translation). Some have suggested an emendation to a Qal form: “Do not forget me” (all the ancient versions, NEB, REB; see GKC 369 �117.x). “Do not forget me” would make a good parallel with “remember these things” in the first line. Since the MT is the harder reading and fits with Israel’s complaint that God had forgotten her (Isa 40:27), the MT reading should be retained (NASB, NKJV, NRSV, ESV). The passive has been rendered as an active in the translation in keeping with contemporary English style (so also NIV, NCV, TEV, NLT).

rashi.heb:
*לא תנשני.* 
לא תהיה שכוח מיראתי:
rashi.eng: *do not forget Me.* Do not forget My fear.

notes.1902: (tn, Heb): “I blot out like a cloud your rebellious deeds, and like a cloud your sins.” “Rebellious deeds” and “sins” stand by metonymy for the guilt they produce. Both עָב (’av) and עָנָן (’anan) refer to the clouds in the sky. It is tempting for stylistic purposes to translate the second with “fog” or “mist” (cf. NAB, NRSV “cloud…mist”; NIV “cloud…morning mist”; NLT “morning mists…clouds”), but this distinction between the synonyms is unwarranted here. The point of the simile seems to be this: The Lord forgives their sins, causing them to vanish just as clouds disappear from the sky (see Job 7:9; 30:15).

rashi.heb:
*מחיתי כעב פשעיך.* 
במצרים ובמדבר גם עתה שובה אלי:
rashi.eng: *I erased your transgressions like a thick cloud.* in Egypt and in the desert. Now too, return to Me.

notes.1904: (tn, Heb): “acts”; NASB, NRSV “has done it”; NLT “has done this wondrous thing.”
notes.1905: (tn, Heb): “lower regions.” This refers to Sheol and forms a merism with “sky” in the previous line. See Pss 63:9; 71:20.
notes.1906: (tn, Heb): “O forest and all the trees in it”; NASB, NRSV “and every tree in it.”
notes.1908: (tn): That is, by delivering Israel. Cf. NCV “showed his glory when he saved Israel”; TEV “has shown his greatness by saving his people Israel.”

rashi.heb:
*פצחו.* 
ל' פתחון פה:
rashi.eng: *burst out.* An expression of opening the mouth.

notes.1909: (tn, Heb): “your redeemer.” See the note at 41:14.
notes.1910: (tn): The consonantal text (Kethib) has “Who [was] with me?” The marginal reading (Qere) is “from with me,” i.e., “by myself.” See BDB 87 s.v. II אֵת 4.c.

rashi.heb:
*ויוצרך מבטן.* 
מאז ויתרוצצו הבנים בקרבה (בראשית כ״ה:כ״ב) הייתי לך לעזרה ובחרתיך:
rashi.eng: *and the One Who formed you from the womb.* From the time that (Gen. 25:22) “the children struggled within her,” I was your help and I chose you.

rashi.heb:
*נוטה.* 
שמים לבדי:
rashi.eng: *stretched forth.*

notes.1911: (tc): The Hebrew text has בַּדִּים (baddim), perhaps meaning “empty talkers” (BDB 95 s.v. III בַּד). In the four other occurrences of this word (Job 11:3; Isa 16:6; Jer 48:30; 50:36) the context does not make the meaning of the term very clear. Its primary point appears to be that the words spoken are meaningless or false. In light of its parallelism with “omen readers,” some have proposed an emendation to בָּרִים (barim, “seers”). The Mesopotamian baru-priests were divination specialists who played an important role in court life. See R. Wilson, Prophecy and Society in Ancient Israel, 93-98. Rather than supporting an emendation, J. N. Oswalt (Isaiah [NICOT], 2:189, n. 79) suggests that Isaiah used בַּדִּים purposively as a derisive wordplay on the Akkadian word baru (in light of the close similarity of the d and r consonants).
notes.1912: (tn): Or “makes fools of” (NIV, NRSV); NAB and NASB both similar.
notes.1913: (tn, Heb): “who turns back the wise” (so NRSV); NIV “overthrows the learning of the wise”; TEV “The words of the wise I refute.”
notes.1914: (tn, Heb): “their knowledge” (so KJV, NAB, NASB, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*מפר אותות בדים.* 
לפי שאני נטיתי שמים לפיכך אני יכול להפר אותם:
rashi.eng: *Who stretched forth the heavens alone… Who frustrates the signs of imposters.* Since I stretched forth the heavens, I can, therefore, frustrate their signs.

rashi.heb:
*בדים.* 
הם החוזים בכוכבי' ע"י אותות השמים ועל שם שפעמים הרבה שהם מכזבים קורין אותם בדים, שאני מחליף השרים שלמעלה וטועין אלו הנשאלין בהם ולפי שאיצטגניני בבל היו חוזים בכוכבים כמו שהוא אומר (לקמן מז) יעמדו נא ויושיעוך הוברי שמים לכך הוא אומר שיפר אותות בדיהם כי אני הוא שהפרתי אותות בדי מצרים:
rashi.eng: *imposters.* Heb. בַּדִּים. They are stargazers, who predict the future through signs of the heavens, and since many times they lie, they are called בַּדִּים, imposters, for I change the heavenly princes, and these who ask of them err, and since the astrologers of Babylon were stargazers, as Scripture states (infra 47:13), “Let them stand now, and let the gazers into the heavens save you.” He, therefore, states that He will frustrate the signs of their imposters, for I am He Who frustrated the signs of the imposters of Egypt.

notes.1915: (tn, Heb): “the word of his servant.” The following context indicates that the Lord’s prophets are in view.
notes.1916: (tn, Heb): “counsel.” The Hebrew term עֵצָה (’etsah) probably refers here to the divine plan as announced by the prophets. See HALOT 867 s.v. I עֵצָה.
notes.1917: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*מקים דבר עבדו.* 
משה:
rashi.eng: *He fulfills the word of His servant.* Moses.

rashi.heb:
*ועצת מלאכיו.* 
מלאך אחד אמר ליעקב ישראל יהיה שמך (בראשית לב) וקיימתי דבריו אף כאן אקיים עצת נביאי האומר על ירושלים תושב:
rashi.eng: *and the counsel of His messengers.* One angel said to Jacob (Gen. 32:27), “Israel shall be your name,” and I fulfilled his words. Here too, I will fulfill the counsel of My prophets who say concerning Jerusalem, “It shall be settled.”

rashi.heb:
*האומר לצולה חרבי.* 
האומר לבבל התיבשי:
rashi.eng: *Who says to the deep, “Be dry”.* Who says to Babylon, “Be dry.”

rashi.heb:
*ונהרותיך אוביש.* 
לפי שהיא יושבת על נהרות מדמה הריגת אוכלוסיה ליובש נהרות:
rashi.eng: *and I will dry up your rivers.* Since it is situated on rivers, he compares the slaying of its population to the drying up of rivers.

notes.1918: (tn, Heb): “says to.” It is possible that the sentence is not completed, as the description of Cyrus and his God-given role is developed in the rest of the verse. 45:1 picks up where 44:28a leaves off with the Lord’s actual words to Cyrus finally being quoted in 45:2.
notes.1919: (tn, Heb): “my shepherd.” The shepherd motif is sometimes applied, as here, to a royal figure who is responsible for the well-being of the people whom he rules.
notes.1920: (tn, Heb): “that he might bring to completion all my desire.”
notes.1921: (tn, Heb): “and [concerning the] temple, you will be founded.” The preposition -לְ (l�) is understood by ellipsis at the beginning of the second line. The verb תִּוָּסֵד (tivvased, “you will be founded”) is second masculine singular and is probably addressed to the personified temple (הֵיכָל [hekhal, “temple”] is masculine).

rashi.heb:
*רועי.* 
מלך שלי:
rashi.eng: *My shepherd.* My king.

notes.1922: (tn, Heb): “anointed” (so KJV, NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT); NCV “his appointed king.”
notes.1923: (sn): The “right hand” is a symbol of activity and strength; the Lord directs Cyrus’ activities and assures his success.
notes.1924: (tn, Heb): “and the belts of kings I will loosen”; NRSV “strip kings of their robes”; NIV “strip kings of their armor.”

rashi.heb:
*למשיחו.* 
כל שם גדולה קרויה משיחה כמו לך נתתיה למשחה (במדבר י״ח:ח׳) ורבותינו אמרו למלך המשיח אומר הקב"ה קובל אני לך על כורש כדאיתא במסכת מגילה:
rashi.eng:
*to His anointed one.* 
Every title of greatness is called anointing. Comp. (Num. 18:8) “To you I have given them for greatness (לְמָשְׁחָה).” Our Sages, however, said: To the King Messiah, the Holy One, blessed be He, says, “I complain to you about Cyrus,” as it is stated in Tractate Megillah 12a.

rashi.heb:
*לרד לפניו גוים.* 
להרקיע ולרדד לפניו גוים, לרד לשטוח:
rashi.eng: *to flatten nations before him.* Heb. לְרַד, to spread out and to flatten nations before him. לְרַד is equivalent to לְרַדֵּד, to spread out.

rashi.heb:
*ומתני מלכים אפתח.* 
לשון חלשות הוא זה ושבר כח כי חגורת מתנים הוא זירוז כח כמו אזר נא כגבר חלציך (איוב מ׳:ז׳) ואתה תאזר מתניך (ירמיהו א׳:י״ז) ומזיח אפיקים ריפה (איוב י״ב:כ״א) ל' שברון כח:
rashi.eng: *and the loins of kings I will loosen.* This is an expression of weakness and breaking strength, for girding the loins constitutes arming with strength. Comp. (Job 38:3) “Gird up your loins like a mighty man;” (Jer. 1:17) “And you gird up your loins;” (Job 12:21) “And the belt of the mighty He loosens;” an expression of breaking strength.

rashi.heb:
*לפתוח לפניו.* 
דלתי שערי בבל, שערים הוא חלל פתח השער, דלתים הם הפותחים ונועלין בהן את השער:
rashi.eng: *to open… before him.* the portals of the gates of Babylon. Gates are the space of the opening of the gate; portals are those with which they open and lock the gate.

notes.1925: (tc): The form הֲדוּרִים (hadurim) makes little, if any, sense here. It is probably a corruption of an original הָרָרִים (hararim, “mountains”), the reduplicated form of הָר (har, “mountain”).
notes.1926: (tn): That is, on the gates. Cf. CEV “break the iron bars on bronze gates.”

rashi.heb:
*והדורים אישר.* 
ת"י ושורייא אכבש כמו הדר הדרנה על שם שסובבת החומה את העיר ויש לפרש הדורים אורחות מקלקלות איישר לפניו:
rashi.eng: *and I will straighten out crooked paths.* Heb. וַהֲדוּרִים אֲיַשֵּׁר. Jonathan renders: I will level the walls. Comp. (Shab. 77b) “the surrounding area (הדר הדרנא),” since the wall surrounds the city. The word may also be explained as: I will straighten out crooked paths before him.

notes.1927: (tn, Heb): “treasures of darkness” (KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); TEV “treasures from dark, secret places.”

rashi.heb:
*הקורא בשמך.* 
עדיין לא נולדת ואני קורא לך שם כורש:
rashi.eng: *Who calls [you] by your name.* You are not yet born, and I call you by the name Cyrus.

rashi.heb:
*למען עבדי יעקב.* 
שתוציאהו מגלות בבל:
rashi.eng: *For the sake of My servant Jacob.* that you take him out of Babylonian exile.

rashi.heb:
*ולא ידעתני.* 
לא עשית רצוני כי אני אמרתי הוא יבנה עירי והוא כשעמד אמר מי בכם מכל עמו רשות נתן להם לילך וכל הטורח פורק מעל צוארו:
rashi.eng: *yet you have not known Me.* You did not do My will, for I said, (infra v. 13) “He shall build My city,” but he when he assumed the throne said, “Whoever among you is from all His people, may ascend.” He gave them permission to go, but he cast off all the trouble from upon his neck.

notes.1929: (tn, Heb): “and there is none besides.” On the use of עוֹד (’od) here, see BDB 729 s.v. 1.c.
notes.1930: (tn, Heb): “gird you” (so NASB) or “strengthen you” (so NIV).
notes.1931: (tn): Or “know” (NAB, NCV, NRSV, TEV, CEV, NLT); NIV “have not acknowledged.”

notes.1932: (tn): The words “I do this” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.1933: (tn, Heb): “they” (so KJV, ASV); TEV, CEV “everyone”; NLT “all the world.”

notes.1934: (tn): The words “I am” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons. In the Hebrew text the participle at the beginning of v. 7 stands in apposition to “the Lord” in v. 6.
notes.1935: (tn): On the surface v. 7a appears to describe God’s sovereign control over the cycle of day and night, but the following statement suggests that “light” and “darkness” symbolize “deliverance” and “judgment.”
notes.1936: (sn): This verses affirms that God is ultimately sovereign over his world, including mankind and nations. In accordance with his sovereign will, he can cause wars to cease and peace to predominate (as he was about to do for his exiled people through Cyrus), or he can bring disaster and judgment on nations (as he was about to do to Babylon through Cyrus).

rashi.heb:
*יוצר אור.* 
לצדיקים:
rashi.eng: *Who forms light.* for the righteous.

rashi.heb:
*ובורא חושך.* 
לבבל וכן עושה שלום ובורא רע:
rashi.eng: *and creates darkness.* for Babylon, and the same applies to “Who makes peace and creates evil.”

notes.1937: (tn, Heb): “let the clouds drip with”; KJV “let the skies pour down.”
notes.1938: (tn, Heb): “open up” (so NASB); NIV, NLT “open wide.”
notes.1939: (tc): The plural verb should be emended to a singular form. The vav (ו) ending is probably virtually dittographic (note the yod at the beginning of the following word).
notes.1940: (tc): The Hiphil verb form (תַצְמִיחַ, tatsmiakh) should probably be emended to a Qal (תִצְמַח, titsmakh). The יח sequence at the end of the form is probably due to dittography (note the following יַחַד, yakhad).
notes.1941: (tn): The masculine singular pronominal suffix probably refers back to יָשַׁע (yasha’, “salvation”).

rashi.heb:
*הרעיפו שמים וגו'.* 
צדק האמור במקרא מוסב על הנזל ועל הרעיפה הרעיפו שמים צדק ושחקים יזלו צדק כלומר מאתי יבא הצדק להיטיב להם מן השמים:
rashi.eng: *Cause the heavens to drip.* Righteousness, mentioned in the verse, is the object of the dripping and the pouring. Make the heavens drip righteousness and the skies shall pour righteousness, i.e., from Me shall come the righteousness to benefit them from the heavens.

rashi.heb:
*בראתיו.* 
בראתי את הדבר הזה:
rashi.eng: *created it.* I created this thing.

notes.1942: (tn, Heb): “Woe [to] the one who argues with the one who formed him.”
notes.1943: (tn): The words “one who is like a mere” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons and clarification.
notes.1944: (tn, Heb): “Should the clay say to the one who forms it?” The rhetorical question anticipates a reply, “Of course not!”
notes.1945: (tn): The words “in the world” are supplied in the translation to approximate in English idiom the force of the sarcastic question.
notes.1946: (tn, Heb): “your work, there are no hands for it,” i.e., “your work looks like something made by a person who has no hands.”

rashi.heb:
*הוי רב את יצרו.* 
נתנבא ישעיה על חבקוק שעתיד לעמוד ולקרו' תגר על אורך הצלחתו של נבוכדנצר עד אנה ה' שועתי וגו' ותעשה אדם כדגי הים (חבקוק א׳:ב׳) והקב"ה אמר לישעיה למה זה בא לריב אתי סבור הוא שאיני שם על לב להושיע את עמי לעת מלאת אשר תרצה הארץ את שבתותיה (ויקרא כ״ו:ל״ד):
rashi.eng: *Woe to him who contends with his Creator.* Isaiah prophesied concerning Habakkuk, who was destined to stand and complain about the length of Nebuchadnezzar’s success (1:2): “How long, O Lord, have I entreated [You]?…” (v. 14) “And [why] have You made man like the fish of the sea?” And the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Isaiah, Why does this one come to contend with Me? Does he think that I do not give thought to save My people? When the time lapses, “that the land will appease its sabbaths” (Lev. 26:34).

rashi.heb:
*אין ידים לו.* 
אין מקום לו:
rashi.eng: *has no place.* [lit. has no hands,] has no place.

notes.1947: (tn, Heb): “Woe [to] one who says” (NASB and NIV both similar); NCV “How terrible it will be.”
notes.1948: (tn): See the note at v. 9. This phrase occurs a second time later in this verse.
notes.1949: (sn): Verses 9-10 may allude to the exiles’ criticism that the Lord does not appear to know what he is doing.

rashi.heb:
*הוי אומר לאב מה תוליד.* 
כסבור הוא להיות מרחם על הבן יותר מאביו, ד"א הוי בן האומר לאב למה הולדת דומה הוא לזה שהוא רב את יוצרו:
rashi.eng: *Woe to him who says to a father, “What do you beget?”.* He thinks that he has more pity on the son than his father. Another explanation is: Woe is the son who says to his father, “Why have you begotten?” He is analogous to the one who contends with his Creator.

notes.1950: (sn): See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.
notes.1951: (tc): The Hebrew text reads “the one who formed him, the coming things.” Among various suggestions, some have proposed an emendation of יֹצְרוֹ (yots�ro, “the one who formed him”) to יֹצֵר (yotser, “the one who forms”; the suffixed form in the Hebrew text may be influenced by vv. 9-10, where the same form appears twice) and takes “coming things” as the object of the participle (either objective genitive or accusative): “the one who brings the future into being.”
notes.1952: (tn, Heb): “Ask me” The rhetorical command sarcastically expresses the Lord’s disgust with those who question his ways.
notes.1953: (tn, Heb): “Do you command me about…?” The rhetorical question sarcastically expresses the Lord’s disgust with those who question his ways.

rashi.heb:
*האותיות שאלוני וגו'.* 
ה"א נקודה קמץ למדת שאינה תמיהה וכן פירשו אם באתם לשאול לי אתם הנביאים שאלוני על אותות שמי' ומופתי' אשר אתם רואים נולדים בארץ עליהם היו שואלים אותי מה הם אבל על בני ועל פועל ידי ישרים שבשבילם יצרתי את הכל אתם באים לצוותי ולקרוא לפני תגר:
rashi.eng: *Ask Me about the signs etc..* Heb. הָאוֹתִיוֹת. The ‘heh’ is voweled with a ‘kamatz.’ This indicates that it is not the interrogative, but this is its explanation: If you have come to ask Me, you and the prophets, ask Me about the signs of the heavens and the wonders that you see coming about on the earth; about them you may ask Me, what they are, but about My children and about the work of My hands, Israel, for whose sake I formed everything, shall you come to command Me and to complain before Me?

rashi.heb:
*תצוני.* 
תמוה הוא וכי עליכם לצוות על בני אני כבר בראתי להם הישועה במחשבה שעלתה לפני כיצד אנכי העירותיהו בצדק על כורש הוא אומר:
rashi.eng: *do you command Me?.* This is the interrogative. Must you command Me concerning My children? I have already created the salvation for them in the thought that has entered My mind [lit. has come before Me]. How so? I aroused him with righteousness. This is stated regarding Cyrus.

notes.1954: (tn): The words “who live” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.1955: (tn, Heb): “I, even my hands”; NASB “I stretched out…with My hands”; NRSV “it was my hands that stretched out.” The same construction occurs at the beginning of v. 13.
notes.1956: (tn): Or “the heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heavens” or “sky” depending on the context.
notes.1957: (tn, Heb): “and to all their host I commanded.” See the notes at 40:26.

rashi.heb:
*אנכי עשיתי ארץ.* 
ונתתיה לאשר ישר בעיני:
rashi.eng: *I made the earth.* and gave it to whoever pleased Me [lit. was straight in My eyes].

notes.1958: (tn, Heb): “I stir him up in righteousness”; NASB “I have aroused him.” See the note at 41:2. Cyrus (cf. 44:28) is in view here.

notes.1959: (tn, Heb): “labor,” which stands metonymically for the fruits of labor, either “monetary profit,” or “products.”
notes.1960: (tn): Or perhaps, “merchandise” (so KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NAB “the gain of Ethiopia”; CEV “the treasures of Ethiopia.”
notes.1961: (tn, Heb): “they will pass over to you”; NASB, NIV “will come over to you”; CEV “will belong to you.”
notes.1962: (sn): Restored Israel is depicted here in typical ancient Near Eastern fashion as an imperial power that receives riches and slaves as tribute.
notes.1963: (sn): Israel’s vassals are portrayed as so intimidated and awed that they treat Israel as an intermediary to God or sub-deity.
notes.1964: (tn): Or perhaps, “among.” Cf. KJV, ASV “Surely God is in thee.”
notes.1965: (tn, Heb): “there is no other” (so NIV, NRSV). The same phrase occurs at the end of v. 18, in v. 21, and at the end of v. 22.

rashi.heb:
*יגיע מצרים וגו'.* 
הרי הודעתי אתכם במה אושיע את בני מיד בבל כי כורש לכך העירותיהו בצדקי ועוד אני מודיעכם תשועת סנחריב בימי חזקיהו כאשר ישוב (לעיל לז) מעל תרהקה מלך כוש יבא לירושלים וחמדת כל אוצרות כוש ומצרים שילכו לעזור את כוש בידו ויבא עם אותו השלל ויפול בירושלים וחזקיהו ועמו יבזו את הכל כן מפורש בסדר עולם שעל סנחריב נאמר:
rashi.eng: *The toil of Egypt etc..* I have informed how I will save My children from the hand of Babylon, for I have aroused Cyrus for that purpose with My righteousness. I further inform you of the salvation from Sennacherib that will take place in the days of Hezekiah. When he returns (supra 36:36) from marching upon Tirhaka, king of Cush, he will return to Jerusalem with all the valuable treasures of Cush, and Egypt, who will go to aid Cush, in his possession, and he will come with those spoils and fall in Jerusalem, and Hezekiah and his people will plunder everything. So is it delineated in Seder Olam (ch. 23) that it is stated concerning Sennacherib.

rashi.heb:
*אנשי מדה.* 
גובהי קומה
rashi.eng: *men of stature.* Tall people.

rashi.heb:
*עליך.* 
ירושלים:
rashi.eng: *over to you.* Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*בזקים יעבורו.* 
שהביאם שם סנחריב שלולים בקולרים ולאחר מפלתו עמד חזקיהו ופטר את כל השבוים ונתגיירו והכירו מלכות שמים:
rashi.eng: *they shall come over in chains.* For Sennacherib brought them there, with neck-irons fastened to them, and after his defeat, Hezekiah stood and released all those captives, who became converted to Judaism and recognized the kingdom of Heaven.

rashi.heb:
*אך בך אל.* 
יהו מודים שאין אלוה אלא ה' לבדו:
rashi.eng: *Only in you is God.* They will acknowledge that there is no God but the Lord alone. ([Mss. and K’li Paz read:] but to Israel.)

rashi.heb:
*אכן אתה אל מסתתר.* 
וכן יאמרו להקב"ה אכן הבנתנו כי לגבות חובותיהן של עמך אתה מסתתר מלהראות נצחונך כביכול אין בך יכולת ובהתעורר רחמיך אתה אלהי ישראל מושיע כך מפורש במכילתא:
rashi.eng: *Indeed, You are a God Who conceals Himself.* And so they shall say to the Holy One, blessed be He, “Indeed, You have given us to understand (we understand [Mss. and K’li Paz]) that to collect the debts of Your people, You conceal yourself from showing Your victory. So to speak, You have not the ability, and when Your mercy is aroused, You are the God of Israel, the Savior.” So it is explained in Mechilta (Ex. 14:4).

notes.1966: (tn): “together they will walk in humiliation, the makers of images.”

rashi.heb:
*חרשי צירים.* 
אומני ציורים של פסילים של עכו"ם ומזלות:
rashi.eng: *master painters.* Heb. צִירִים חָרָשֵׁי, the master painters of the idols, from among the pagans.

notes.1967: (tn, Heb): “Israel will be delivered by the Lord [with] a permanent deliverance.”
notes.1968: (tn, Heb): “you will not be ashamed and you will not be humiliated for ages of future time.”

notes.1969: (tn, Heb): “he [is] the God.” The article here indicates uniqueness.
notes.1970: (tn): Or “unformed.” Gen 1:2 describes the world as “unformed” (תֹהוּ, tohu) prior to God’s creative work, but God then formed the world and made it fit for habitation.

rashi.heb:
*לא תוהו בראה.* 
כי לשבת יצרה:
rashi.eng: *He did not create it for a waste.* but He formed it to be inhabited.

notes.1971: (tn, Heb): “in a place of a land of darkness” (ASV similar); NASB “in some dark land.”
notes.1972: (tn): “In vain” translates תֹהוּ (tohu), used here as an adverbial accusative: “for nothing.”
notes.1973: (tn): The translation above assumes that צֶדֶק (tsedeq) and מֵישָׁרִים (mesharim) are adverbial accusatives (see 33:15). If they are taken as direct objects, indicating the content of what is spoken, one might translate, “who proclaims deliverance, who announces justice.”

rashi.heb:
*לא בסתר דברתי.* 
כשנתתי את התורה ולא אמרתי על תהו על חנם: לזרע יעקב בקשוני כי אם לקבל שכר גדול:
rashi.eng: *Not in secret did I speak.* When I gave the Torah, and I did not say for naught and in vain to the seed of Jacob, Seek Me, but to receive great reward.

rashi.heb:
*אני ה' דובר צדק.* 
מאחר שפתחתי להם בדבר צדקי להודיעם מתן שכרן אחר כן הגדתי להם מישרים חוקי ותורתי שקודם מתן תורה נאמר להם (שמות יא) ועתה אם שמוע וגו' והייתם לי סגולה וממלכת כהנים וגו':
rashi.eng: *I am the Lord Who speaks righteousness.* Since I commenced to speak to them concerning My righteousness, to inform them of the giving of their reward, afterwards I told them things that are right, My statutes and My laws, for before the giving of the Torah it was said to them, “And now, if you heed, etc., you shall be for Me a treasure… a kingdom of priests, etc.” (Ex. 19:5).

rashi.heb:
*התנגשו.* 
לשון הגשה והנו"ן טפילה בו כאשר יאמר התנגפו:
rashi.eng: *approach.* Heb. הִתְנַגְּשׁוּ, an expression of approaching (הַגָּשָׁה) and the ‘nun’ is attached to it, as one says “they were struck (הִתְנַגְּפוּ);” “they will be struck (יִתְנַגְּפוּ).”

rashi.heb:
*פליטי הגוים.* 
אשר נשארו מחרבו של נבוכדנצר:
rashi.eng: *you survivors of the nations.* who survived the sword of Nebuchadnezzar.

rashi.heb:
*לא ידעו הנושאים את עץ פסלם.* 
להבין דעת:
rashi.eng: *who carry their graven wooden image… do not know.* to understand knowledge.

notes.1974: (tn, Heb): “Declare! Bring near!”; NASB “Declare and set forth your case.” See 41:21.
notes.1975: (tn): Or “a righteous God and deliverer”; NASB, NIV, NRSV “a righteous God and a Savior.”

rashi.heb:
*השמיע זאת מקדם.* 
מי בפסיליכם אשר השמיע מקדם להביא אלהיכם תשועה איש איש לעובדיו:
rashi.eng: *who announced this from before.* Who of your idols is it that announced from before that your God brought salvation, each one to its worshipers?

rashi.heb:
*הלא אני ה' ואין עוד.* 
שאני מודיע מה אני עתיד לעשות לעמי ואקיים דברי:
rashi.eng: *Is it not I, the Lord, and there are no other.* For I announce what I am destined to do for My people, and I fulfill My words.

notes.1976: (tn): The Niphal imperative with prefixed vav (ו) indicates purpose after the preceding imperative. The Niphal probably has a tolerative sense, “allow yourselves to be delivered, accept help.”

rashi.heb:
*פנו אלי.* 
והניחו פסילכם כל אפסי ארץ ובכך תושעו:
rashi.eng: *Turn to Me.* and abandon your graven images, all the ends of the earth, and, thereby, you shall be saved.

notes.1977: (tn, Heb): “I swear by myself”; KJV, NASB “have sworn.”
notes.1978: (tn, Heb): “a word goes out from my mouth [in] truth and will not return.”
notes.1979: (tn, Heb): “swear” (so KJV, NAB, NIV, NRSV); NLT “confess allegiance.”

rashi.heb:
*בי נשבעתי.* 
ויצא מפי צדקה לקבל כל השבים אלי דבר דברתי ולא ישוב מהו הצדקה אשר יצאת מפי כי לי תכרע כל ברך ואני אקבלם כענין שנאמר כי אז אהפוך אל עמים וגו' (צפניה ג׳:ט׳):
rashi.eng: *By Myself I swore.* and righteousness emanated from My mouth to accept all those who return to Me. I spoke a word, and it will not be retracted. What is the righteousness that emanated from My mouth? That to Me shall every knee kneel, and I will accept them, as the matter is stated (Zeph. 3:9): “For then will I change for the people a pure language, to call all of them in the name of the Lord…”

notes.1980: (tn, Heb): “‘Yes, in the Lord,’ one says about me, ‘is deliverance and strength.’”
notes.1981: (tn, Heb): “will come to him and be ashamed.”

rashi.heb:
*אך בה' לי אמר.* 
המקרא זה מסורס וכן פתרונו אך לי בה' אמר צדקות ועוז אע"פ שכל הגוים ישתחוו לפניו אך לי לבדי כנסת ישראל בה' הובטח לי צדקות ועוז ולא יבאו מכחישי תורה לחלל כבודי:
rashi.eng: *But to me did He say by the Lord.* Heb. אַךְ בַה׳ לִי אָמַר [lit. but by the Lord to me He said]. This verse is inverted, and thus is its interpretation: But to me did He say by the Lord righteousness and strength. Although all the nations shall prostrate themselves before Him [correct reading according to Warsaw edition, K’li Paz, and mss.], but to me alone, the congregation of Israel, has been promised by the Lord righteousness and strength, and other nations shall not be included in my glory.

rashi.heb:
*עדיו יבוא ויבשו וגו'.* 
כל הנחרים בהקב"ה יבואו עדיו להתחרט על מה שעשו בחייהם ויבושו:
rashi.eng: *to Him shall come and be ashamed etc..* All who were incensed against the Holy One, blessed be He, shall come to Him to regret what they did in their lifetimes and be ashamed.

rashi.heb:
*הנחרים.* 
המתגרים:
rashi.eng: *all who are incensed.* Heb. כֹּל הַנֶּחֱרִים בּוֹ, all who are incensed.

notes.1982: (tn, Heb): “In the Lord all the offspring of Israel will be vindicated and boast.”

rashi.heb:
*בה' יצדקו ויתהללו.* 
בהבטחת משען אהבתו ימצאו צדקה ויתפארו במעוז
rashi.eng: *Through the Lord… find righteousness and boast.* Through the promise of the support of His love they shall find righteousness and boast of His strength.

rashi.heb:
*ויתהללו.* 
פרוונטי"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *boast.* Heb. וְיִתְהַלְלוּ, porvantir in O.F.

notes.1983: (sn): Bel was the name of a Babylonian god. The name was originally associated with Enlil, but later was applied to Marduk. See HALOT 132 s.v. בֵּל.
notes.1984: (sn): Nebo is a variation of the name of the Babylonian god Nabu.
notes.1985: (tn, Heb): “their images belong to animals and beasts”; NIV “their idols are borne by beasts of burden”; NLT “are being hauled away.”
notes.1986: (tn, Heb): “your loads are carried [as] a burden by a weary [animal].”

rashi.heb:
*כרע בל קורס נבו.* 
אלהותיהם של בבל כרעו קרסו ל' שחוק של עכו"ם הוא כמי שיש לו חולי מעים ואינו מספיק לישב על מושב בה"כ עד שהוא נתרז:
rashi.eng: *Bel squats; Nebo soils himself.* The deities of Babylon squatted and soiled themselves. This is an expression of ridicule of the idols, like one who suffers from diarrhea and does not manage to sit down on the seat in the privy before he discharges with a splash.

rashi.heb:
*כרע בל קורס נבו.* 
אישקרופי"ר בל קונקיא"ה נבו כך שמעתי משמו של רבינו גרשום מאור הגולה:
rashi.eng: *Bel squats; Nebo soils himself.* Heb. כָּרַע בֵּל קֹרֵס נְבוֹ. Akropid sei Bel; konkiad sei Nebo. Bel squats; Nebo soils himself. So I heard in the name of Rabbenu Gershom, the Light of the Diaspora.

rashi.heb:
*היו עצביהם.* 
צלמי צורתם של בל ונבו היו לחיה ולבהמה נדמו להיות כחיה וכבהמה שמזהימין ומלכלכין עצמן ברעי שלהם:
rashi.eng: *their idols were.* The images of the forms of Bel and Nebo were to the beasts and the cattle, compared to the beasts and the cattle, which soil and dirty themselves with their droppings.

rashi.heb:
*נשואותיכם עמוסות משא.* 
רעי שבמעיהם כבדות הם לעמוס כמשא לאדם עיף לפיכך קרסו כרעו יחדיו הקריסה עם הכריעה:
rashi.eng: *what you carry is made a load, a burden.* The feces in their bowels are heavy to bear like a burden for a weary man. Therefore, they soiled themselves and squatted together, the soiling with the squatting.

notes.1987: (tn, Heb): “[the] burden,” i.e., their images, the heavy burden carried by the animals.
notes.1988: (tn): נַפְשָׁם (nafsham, “their souls/lives”) is equivalent here to a third masculine plural suffix, but the third feminine singular verb הָלָכָה (halakhah, “they go”) agrees with the feminine noun נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh, “soul, life”).
notes.1989: (sn): The downfall of Babylon is depicted here. The idols are carried off by the victorious enemy; the gods are likened to defeated captives who cower before the enemy and are taken into exile.

rashi.heb:
*לא יכלו מלט משא.* 
להפליט הצואה שבמעיהם כשאר המוציאין כהוגן:
rashi.eng: *they could not deliver the burden.* to discharge the feces in their bowels as others discharge, in the normal manner.

rashi.heb:
*מלט.* 
ל' הוצאה ממקום בלוע וכן (לעיל לד) שמה קננה קפוז ותמלט, הוציאה ביצתה וכן (לקמן סו) והמליטה זכר ויונתן לא תירגם כן המקראות הללו:
rashi.eng: *deliver.* Heb. מַלֵּט, an expression of discharging from an embedded place. Comp. (supra 34:15) “There, the owl has made its nest, and she has laid eggs (וַתְּמַלֵט),” he has discharged her egg. Comp. also (infra 66:7) “And she has been delivered (וְהִמְלִיטָה) of a male child.” Jonathan, however, did not render these verses in this manner.

notes.1990: (tn, Heb): “house of Jacob”; TEV “descendants of Jacob.”
notes.1991: (tn, Heb): “and all the remnant of the house of Israel.”
notes.1992: (tn, Heb): “from the womb” (so NRSV); KJV “from the belly”; NAB “from your infancy.”
notes.1993: (tn, Heb): “who have been lifted up from the womb.”

rashi.heb:
*העמוסים מני בטן.* 
מאז נולדתם בבית לבן הארמי עמסתי אתכם על זרועותי כי מאז עמדו עליכם עכו"ם בכל דור ודור ולא כעכו"ם שהיו עומסים ונושאים את אלהיהם כמו שאמור למעלה אבל אתם עמוסים ונשואים בזרועותי:
rashi.eng: *who are borne from birth.* Since you were born in the house of Laban the Aramean, I bore you on My arms, for since then, adversaries stand up against you in every generation and not like the idolaters (other nations [K’li Paz and mss.]) who are laden and carry their Gods, as is mentioned above, but you are laden and borne in My arms.

notes.1994: (tn, Heb): “until old age, I am he” (NRSV similar); NLT “I will be your God throughout your lifetime.”
notes.1995: (sn): Unlike the weary idol gods, whose images must be carried by animals, the Lord carries his weary people.

rashi.heb:
*ועד זקנה.* 
אשר זקנתם וכלה כחכם שאין לכם זכות אני הוא ברחמי ובמדת טובי להושיעכם ולעמוס ולשאת למלט לפי שאמר על יראתם שהיא נסבלת וגם משאה אינה יכולה למלט אמר אני הסובל אחרים ואת משאם אמלט:
rashi.eng: *And until old age.* that you have aged and your strength is depleted, that you have no merit, I am the same with My mercy and with My trait of goodness to save you and to bear you and to carry you and deliver you. Since he says regarding their deity, that it is carried and also that it cannot deliver its burden, he says, “But I bear others, and I will deliver My burden.”

rashi.heb:
*ותמשילוני.* 
כמו (איוב ל׳:י״ט) ואתמשל כעפר ואפר ל' דמיון:
rashi.eng: *and compare Me.* Heb. וְתַמְשִׁלֻנִי. Comp. (Job 30:19) “And I have become like (וָאֶתְמַשֵּׁל) dust and ashes.” An expression of comparison.

rashi.heb:
*ונדמה.* 
ונהיה אני והוא דומין זה לזה:
rashi.eng: *that we may be alike.* That I and he be alike, one to the other.

notes.1996: (tn, Heb): “the reed,” probably referring to the beam of a scales. See BDB 889 s.v. קָנֶה 4.c.

rashi.heb:
*הזלים זהב מכיס.* 
ל' יזלו מים (תהלים קמז):
rashi.eng: *Those who let gold run from the purse.* Heb. הַזָּלִים, an expression of (Ps. 146:18) “Water runs (יִזְּלוּ).”

rashi.heb:
*בקנה ישקולו.* 
הוא קנה המאזני' שקורין פליי"ל בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *with the balance.* Heb. קָנֶה, the bar of a scale, called flael in O.F.

notes.1997: (tn): Or perhaps, “cannot,” here and in the following two lines. The imperfect forms can indicate capability.

notes.1998: (tn): The meaning of the verb אָשַׁשׁ (’ashash, which appears here in the Hitpolel stem) is uncertain. BDB 84 s.v. אשׁשׁ relates it to a root meaning “found, establish” in Arabic; HALOT 100 s.v. II אשׁשׁ gives the meaning “pluck up courage.” The imperative with vav (ו) may indicate purpose following the preceding imperative.
notes.1999: (tn, Heb): “return [it], rebels, to heart”; NRSV “recall it to mind, you transgressors.”

rashi.heb:
*זכרו זאת.* 
אשר אני חפץ לומר:
rashi.eng: *Remember this.* what I wish to say.

rashi.heb:
*והתאוששו.* 
והתחזקו כמו לאשישי קיר חרשת (לעיל טז):
rashi.eng: *and strengthen yourselves.* Heb. וְהִתְאשָׁשׁוּ. Comp. (supra 16:7) “For the walls (לַאֲשִׁישֵׁי) of Kir-hareseth.”

rashi.heb:
*השיבו פושעים על לב.* 
ומה אני אומר לכם לזכור ולהשיב על לב:
rashi.eng: *take to heart, you transgressors.* And what do I say to you to remember and to take to heart?

notes.2000: (tn, Heb): “remember the former things, from antiquity”; KJV, ASV “the former things of old.”
notes.2001: (tn, Heb): “and there is no other” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*זכרו ראשונות מעולם.* 
אשר ראיתם כי אנכי אל ואין עוד, אנכי אלהים ואפס כמוני:
rashi.eng: *Remember the first things of old.* that you have seen that I am God and there is no other; I am God and there is none like Me.

notes.2002: (tn): Or “from long ago”; KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV “from ancient times.”

rashi.heb:
*מגיד מראשית אחרית.* 
גלות מצרים וגאולתה הודעתי בבין הבתרים לפני היותה:
rashi.eng: *[I] tell the end from the beginning.* The Egyptian exile and its redemption I announced in the Covenant between the Segments, before they came about.

notes.2003: (tn): Or, more generally, “a bird of prey” (so NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV; see 18:6).

rashi.heb:
*קורא ממזרח עיט.* 
מארץ ארם שהיא במזרח קראתי לי את אברה' להיות נמלך בעצתי: עיט כמו התיב עטה וטעם (דניאל ב) אתיעטו כל סרכי מלכותא (שם ו) וגם יש לפותרו בל' עוף קראתי למהר אחרי כעוף הפורח ונודד ממקומו:
rashi.eng: *[I] call from the east a swift bird.* Heb. עַיִט. From the land of Aram, which is in the east, I called Abraham to Me to take counsel with Me. עַיִט Comp. (Dan. 2:14) “Answered with counsel (עֵיטָא) and discretion;” (ibid. 6:8) “All the presidents of the kingdom have taken counsel (אִתְיָעֲטוּ).” Alternatively, it can be interpreted as an expression of a bird. I called him to hasten after Me like a bird that flies and wanders from its place.

rashi.heb:
*מרחק.* 
קראתי לאיש עצתי ועמו יעצתי בין הבתרים ד' גליות כמו שמפורש בבראשית רבה והנה אימה חשיכה גדולה וגו':
rashi.eng: *from a distant land.* I called My man of counsel, and with him I took counsel between the parts concerning the four exiles, as it is explained in Gen. Rabbah (44:17) “And behold, a fear, great darkness was falling upon him.” [“Fear” refers to Babylon… “Darkness” refers to Media, who darkened the eyes of Israel with fasting. “Great” refers to Greece…“Was falling upon him” refers to Edom…, etc.]

rashi.heb:
*אף דברתי.* 
עמו הגליות וגאולתן אף אביאנה:
rashi.eng: *yea I spoke.* with him concerning the exiles and their redemption; I will also bring it.

notes.2005: (tn, Heb): “strong of heart [or, mind]”; KJV “stouthearted”; NAB “fainthearted”; NIV “stubborn-hearted.”
notes.2006: (tn, Heb): “who are far from righteousness [or perhaps, “deliverance”].”

rashi.heb:
*אבירי לב.* 
אשר אמצתם לבנכם ונדבקתם בי:
rashi.eng: *stout-hearted.* You who have strengthened your heart among the heathens (the nations [Parshandatha, K’li Paz]) and have clung to Me.

rashi.heb:
*הרחוקים מצדקה.* 
אשר ארכו לכם הימים ולא הראיתי אתכם צדקתי לגאול:
rashi.eng: *that are far from righteousness.* For it has been a long time for you, and I have not demonstrated to you My righteousness to redeem you.

notes.2007: (tn, Heb): “my salvation.” The verb “I am bringing near” is understood by ellipsis (note the previous line).
notes.2008: (tn, Heb): “I will place in Zion salvation”; NASB “I will grant salvation in Zion.”
notes.2009: (tn, Heb): “to Israel my splendor”; KJV, ASV “for Israel my glory.”

rashi.heb:
*קרבתי צדקתי.* 
מעתה ולא תרחק:
rashi.eng: *I have brought near My righteousness.* from now on, and it will not be far off.

notes.2010: (tn): בְּתוּלַה (b�tulah) often refers to a virgin, but the phrase “virgin daughter” is apparently stylized (see also 23:12; 37:22). In the extended metaphor of this chapter, where Babylon is personified as a queen (vv. 5, 7), she is depicted as being both a wife and mother (vv. 8-9).

rashi.heb:
*אין כסא.* 
אין מלכות:
rashi.eng: *without a throne.* Without a kingdom.

rashi.heb:
*כי לא תוסיפי.* 
שיקראו לך עוד רכה וענוגה:
rashi.eng: *for no longer.* [lit. for you shall not continue,] that they call you tender and delicate.

rashi.heb:
*קחי רחיים.* 
היא עבודה קשה כלומר השתעבדי מעתה למלכי מדי ופרס, ד"א וטחני קמח לצדה לדרך גלותך:
rashi.eng: *Take millstones.* This is hard labor, i.e., subordinate yourself from now on, to the kings of Persia and Media. Alternatively: And grind flour for supplies on the road of your exile.

rashi.heb:
*גלי צמתך.* 
זרועיך ושוקיך דברים המצומת וקשור ומכוסה:
rashi.eng: *bare your covered parts.* Your arms and your legs, parts veiled, tied, and covered.

rashi.heb:
*חשפי שובל.* 
גלי השבילים מן המים שעליהם כי דרך שם תצאי בגולה או גלי שוקך ועברי נהרות:
rashi.eng: *uncover the paths.* Heb. חֶשְׂפִּי שֹׁבֶל. Uncover the paths of the water that is upon them, for that way you shall go out into exile, or bare your leg and cross rivers.

notes.2012: (tn, Heb): “Your shame will be seen.” In this context “shame” is a euphemism referring to the genitals.
notes.2013: (tn, Heb): “I will not meet a man.” The verb פָּגַע (pagah) apparently carries the nuance “meet with kindness” here (cf. 64:5, and see BDB 803 s.v. Qal.2).

rashi.heb:
*ולא אפגע אדם.* 
לא אבקש פני אדם לקחת נקמתי:
rashi.eng: *I will not entreat any man.* I will ask no man to take My revenge.

notes.2014: (tc): The Hebrew text reads, “Our redeemer – the Lord who commands armies [traditionally, the Lord of hosts] is his name, the Holy One of Israel.” The ancient Greek version adds “says” before “our redeemer.” אָמַר (’amar) may have accidentally dropped from the text by virtual haplography. Note that the preceding word אָדָם (’adam) is graphically similar. See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

rashi.heb:
*גואלנו ה' צבאות שמו.* 
הנביא אומר כל זה הקב"ה עושה לגאלנו משם:
rashi.eng: *Our redeemer, the Lord of Hosts is His name.* The prophet states: All this the Lord of Hosts does, to redeem us from there.

notes.2015: (tn, Heb): “darkness,” which may indicate a place of hiding where a fugitive would seek shelter and protection.

notes.2018: (tn, Heb): “on the old you made very heavy your yoke.”

rashi.heb:
*על זקן הכבדת עולך.* 
על הזקנים שלא היו יכולים לסבול טורח הכבדת עולך:
rashi.eng: *on the aged you made your yoke very heavy.* On the aged, who were unable to bear hard work, you made heavy your yoke.

notes.2019: (tn, Heb): “Forever I [will be] permanent queen”; NIV “the eternal queen”; CEV “queen forever.”
notes.2020: (tn, Heb): “you did not set these things upon your heart [or “mind”].”
notes.2021: (tn, Heb): “you did not remember its outcome”; NAB “you disregarded their outcome.”

rashi.heb:
*ותאמרי.* 
בלבבך לעולם אהיה גברת ואין פורענות בא עלי והדבר הזה השיאך עד לא שמת אלה המכות שיבואו עליך אל לבך ולא זכרת אחריתה של רעתך שעשית:
rashi.eng: *And you said.* to yourself, “I will forever be a mistress, and no retribution shall come upon me,” and this thing enticed you until you did not take to heart these blows that would come upon you, and you did not remember the end of your evil that you have done.

notes.2022: (tn): Or perhaps, “voluptuous one” (NAB); NAB “you sensual one”; NLT “You are a pleasure-crazy kingdom.”
notes.2023: (tn, Heb): “the one who says in her heart.”
notes.2024: (tn, Heb): “I [am], and besides me there is no other.” See Zeph 2:15.
notes.2025: (tn, Heb): “I will not live [as] a widow, and I will not know loss of children.”

rashi.heb:
*עדינה.* 
ת"י פנקתא:
rashi.eng: *delicate one.* Heb. עֲדִינָה. Jonathan renders: מְפַנֶּקְתָּא, delicate.

rashi.heb:
*ואפסי עוד.* 
ואפס מאותי כמו אין זולתי:
rashi.eng: *and there is none besides me.* Heb. וְאַפְסִי. And there is none outside of me. Like אֵין זוּלָתִי.

notes.2026: (tn, Heb): “loss of children and widowhood.” In the Hebrew text the phrase is in apposition to “both of these” in line 1.
notes.2027: (tn, Heb): “according to their fullness, they will come upon you.”
notes.2028: (tn): For other examples of the preposition bet (בְּ) having the sense of “although, despite,” see BDB 90 s.v. III.7.
notes.2029: (sn): Reference is made to incantations and amulets, both of which were important in Mesopotamian religion. They were used to ward off danger and demons.

rashi.heb:
*שתי אלה.* 
שאמרת שלא תשבי אלמנה ולא תדעי שכול תבאנה לך פתאום:
rashi.eng: *these two.* that you said that you would not sit as a widow and you would not know bereavement, shall suddenly come upon you.

rashi.heb:
*שכול.* 
מיושביך:
rashi.eng: *bereavement.* of your inhabitants.

rashi.heb:
*ואלמון.* 
ממלכך כל קבורת בנים וגלות בני הארץ קרוי שכול:
rashi.eng: *and widowhood.* of your king. Any burial of children or exile of the people of a land is called bereavement.

rashi.heb:
*כתומם.* 
כולם שלמי' בגזרת' השכול והאלמנו':
rashi.eng: *in their full measure.* All of them, complete in their decree, the bereavement and the widowhood.

rashi.heb:
*חבריך.* 
לשון כשפים כמו וחובר חבר (דברים יח):
rashi.eng: *your charms.* Heb. חֲבָרַיִךְ. An expression of sorcery. Comp. (Deut. 18:11) “And a charmer (וְחֹבֵר חָבֶר).”

notes.2030: (tn, Heb): “you trusted in your evil”; KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV “wickedness.”
notes.2031: (tn): Or “said”; NAB “said to yourself”’ NASB “said in your heart.”
notes.2032: (tn): The words “self-professed” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*חכמתך ודעתך.* 
חכמתך ורוע לבבך היא שובבתך הפכו לבך להיות שובבה אינווייז"א בלע"ז שבבך מדרך שאר הבריות:
rashi.eng: *your wisdom and your knowledge.* Your wisdom and the evil of your heart that perverted you. They turned your heart to be perverted, envesede in O.F. It perverted you from the way of other people (other daughters [mss. and K’li Paz]).

notes.2034: (tc): The Hebrew text has שַׁחְרָהּ (shakhrah), which is either a suffixed noun (“its dawning,” i.e., origin) or infinitive (“to look early for it”). Some have suggested an emendation to שַׁחֲדָהּ (shakhadah), a suffixed infinitive from שָׁחַד (shakhad, “[how] to buy it off”; see BDB 1005 s.v. שָׁחַד). This forms a nice parallel with the following couplet. The above translation is based on a different etymology of the verb in question. HALOT 1466 s.v. III שׁחר references a verbal root with these letters (שׁחד) that refers to magical activity.
notes.2035: (tn, Heb): “you will not know”; NIV “you cannot foresee.”

rashi.heb:
*לא תדעי שחרה.* 
לא תדעין למבעי עלה את פני מי תשחרי למלטך ממנה:
rashi.eng: *you shall not know how to remove it by prayer.* Heb. לֹא תֵדְעִי שַׁחְרָהּ. You shall not know to pray about it (Jonathan). Whom will you beseech to extricate you therefrom?

rashi.heb:
*כפרה.* 
לקנחה ולהעבירה וזהו כל ל' כפרה הוא ל' קינוח וסילוק:
rashi.eng: *to rid yourself of it.* Heb. כַּפְּרָהּ, to wipe it away and to remove it, and this is every expression of atonement (כַּפָּרָה). It is an expression of wiping and taking away.

notes.2036: (tn, Heb): “stand” (so KJV, ASV); NASB, NRSV “Stand fast.”
notes.2037: (tn): The word “trusting” is supplied in the translation for clarification. See v. 9.
notes.2038: (tn, Heb): “in that which you have toiled.”
notes.2039: (tn, Heb): “maybe you will be able to profit.”
notes.2040: (tn, Heb): “maybe you will cause to tremble.” The object “disaster” is supplied in the translation for clarification. See the note at v. 9.

rashi.heb:
*עמדי נא.* 
התחזקי נא:
rashi.eng: *Stand now.* Strengthen yourself now.

rashi.heb:
*אולי תערוצי.* 
מאים תכלין למיתקף:
rashi.eng: *perhaps you will gain strength.* Heb. תַּעֲרוֹצִי. Jonathan renders: Perhaps you will be able to become strong.

notes.2041: (tn, Heb): “you are tired because of the abundance of your advice.”
notes.2042: (tn, Heb): “let them stand and rescue you – the ones who see omens in the sky, who gaze at the stars, who make known by months – from those things which are coming upon you.”

rashi.heb:
*הוברי שמים.* 
י"ת כמו צופי שמים דמסכן למזלת שמיא דימהו לברה כחמה (שיר השירים ו׳:י׳) ולברור מללו (איוב לג) וכן חברו מנחם עמהם מבררי הליכת המזלות וכה פתרונו יען אשר לא יוכלון הקוסמים לעמוד על דעת רגעי היום ולילה עד ברור להם השמים לטוהר וגם מיכה אמר בנבואה (מיכה ג) חשכם להם מקסום לימד כי ביום מחשך יחתמו הכוכבים ולא יוכלו לקסום:
rashi.eng: *astrologers.* Heb. הֹבְרֵי שָׁמַיִם. Jonathan renders it like ‘the gazers of the heavens,’ who gaze at the constellations of the heavens. He compares it to (Song 6:10) “Clear (בָּרָה) as the sun,” and to (Job 33:3) “Spoke a clear (בָּרוּר) word.” And so did Menahem associate it with them (Machbereth Menahem p. 47f.); those who clarify the orbit of the constellations, and he interpreted it thus because the diviners are unable to determine the seconds of the day and the night until the heaven is perfectly clear to them. Micah, too, said in prophecy (3:6), “It has become too dark for you to divine.” This teaches us that on a dark day the stars are sealed, and they cannot divine (ibid. p. 13).

rashi.heb:
*מודיעים לחדשים מאשר יבאו עליך.* 
כי בהתחדש הלבנה רואים בשעת מולדתה מקצת ממה שעתיד לבא ואין יודעין כל הבירור לכך נאמר מאשר וכן הוא אומר במקום אחר (לעיל ח) המצפצפים והמהגים כעופות הללו שמצפצפין ומהגי' ואין יודעים על מה:
rashi.eng: *the monthly prognosticators of what will come upon you.* For when the moon is in its first phase [lit. renewed], they see at the time of its ‘birth’ part of what is destined to come, but they do not know it clearly. Therefore, it is stated, “of what.” Similarly, he says elsewhere (supra 8:19): “who chirp and mutter,” like these birds who chirp and mutter and do not know why.

notes.2043: (tn, Heb): “hand,” here a metaphor for the strength or power of the flames.
notes.2044: (tn): The Hebrew text reads literally, “there is no coal [for?] their food, light to sit before it.” Some emend לַחְמָם (lakhmam, “their food”) to לְחֻמָּם (l�khummam, “to warm them”; see HALOT 328 s.v. חמם). This statement may allude to Isa 44:16, where idolaters are depicted warming themselves over a fire made from wood, part of which was used to form idols. The fire of divine judgment will be no such campfire; its flames will devour and destroy.

rashi.heb:
*הנה היו.* 
חוזיך כקש:
rashi.eng: *Behold they were.* Your stargazers were like stubble.

rashi.heb:
*אין גחלת לחמם.* 
אין שארית להם כקש הזו שאין בדליקתו גחלים להתחמם לאורם:
rashi.eng: *there is no coal by which to warm oneself.* They have no remnant, like stubble, the fire of which does not leave over coals by whose fire one can warm himself.

notes.2045: (tn, Heb): “So they will be to you”; NIV “That is all they can do for you.”
notes.2046: (tn, Heb): “that for which you toiled, your traders from your youth.” The omen readers and star gazers are likened to merchants with whom Babylon has had an ongoing economic relationship.
notes.2047: (tn, Heb): “each to his own side, they err.”

rashi.heb:
*איש לעברו תעו.* 
איש לדרכו אל עבר פניו:
rashi.eng: *each one strayed to his side.* each one to his way, to the side of his face [i.e., each one wandered away in the direction he was facing].

notes.2048: (tn, Heb): “house of Jacob”; TEV, CEV “people of Israel.”
notes.2049: (tc): The Hebrew text reads literally “and from the waters of Judah came out.” מִמֵּי (mimme) could be a corruption of מִמְּעֵי (mimm�’e, “from the inner parts of”; cf. NASB, NIV, NLT, NRSV) as suggested in the above translation. Some translations (ESV, NKJV) retain the MT reading because the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa, which corrects a similar form to “from inner parts of” in 39:7, does not do it here.
notes.2050: (tn, Heb): “cause to remember”; KJV, ASV “make mention of.”
notes.2051: (tn, Heb): “not in truth and not in righteousness.”

rashi.heb:
*שמעו זאת.* 
שני שבטים העתידין ללכת בגולה לבבל:
rashi.eng: *Hearken to this.* The two tribes destined to go in exile to Babylon.

rashi.heb:
*בית יעקב הנקראים בשם ישראל.* 
הוא שבט בנימין שאינם נקראים על שבט יהודה אלא על שם סתם שבטי ישראל:
rashi.eng: *O house of Jacob, who are called by the name of Israel.* That is the tribe of Benjamin, who are not called by the tribe of Judah, but by the general name of the tribes of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*וממי יהודה יצאו.* 
ושבט יהודה שיצאו ונזלו מימי דליו של יהודה כמה דאת אמר יזל מים מדליו (במדבר כ״ד:ז׳):
rashi.eng: *and who emanated from the waters of Judah.* And the tribe of Judah who emanated and ran from the waters of Judah’s pail, as Scripture states (Num. 24:7): “Water shall run out of his pails.”

rashi.heb:
*לא באמת.* 
כמו שאמר (ירמיהו ה׳:ב׳) ואם חי ה' יאמרו לכן לשקר וגו' כלומר לא הייתם כדי ליגאל אלא על כי מעיר הקדש נקראו והיא גרמה להם שלא גלו עשרת השבטי' בימי סנחרב בחלח וחבור שאין להם גאולה:
rashi.eng: *neither in truth.* As Jeremiah said, (5:2) “And if they say, ‘As the Lord lives,’ surely they swear falsely,” i.e., you were unworthy of being redeemed, but since they were called [as being] from the Holy City, and that caused them not to be exiled with the ten tribes in the time of Sennacherib, to Halah and Habor, for they have no redemption.

notes.2052: (tn, Heb): “they call themselves [or “are called”] from the holy city.” The precise meaning of the statement is uncertain. The Niphal of קָרָא (qara’) is combined with the preposition מִן (min) only here. When the Qal of קָרָא is used with מִן, the preposition often indicates the place from which one is summoned (see 46:11). So one could translate, “from the holy city they are summoned,” meaning that they reside there.
notes.2053: (tn, Heb): “lean on” (so NASB, NRSV); NAB, NIV “rely on.”

rashi.heb:
*על אלהי ישראל נסמכו.* 
בימי חזקיהו שנאמר בו בה' אלהי ישראל בטח (מ"ב יח) היא גרמה להם שלא גלו אלא בימי נבוכדנצר שהגלם לבבל ותהי להם גאולה על ידי כורש:
rashi.eng: *and they leaned on the God of Israel.* in the days of Hezekiah, about whom it is written (2 Kings 18:5): “He trusted in the Lord God of Israel.” That caused them not to be exiled except in the days of Nebuchadnezzar, who exiled them to Babylon, and they had a redemption through Cyrus.

notes.2054: (tn, Heb): “the former things beforehand I declared.”
notes.2055: (tn, Heb): “and from my mouth they came forth and I caused them to be heard.”

rashi.heb:
*הראשונות.* 
שעברו גאולת מצרים ותשועת חזקיהו מיד סנחרב:
rashi.eng: *The first things.* that passed, [viz.] the redemption from Egypt and Hezekiah’s salvation from the hand of Sennacherib.

rashi.heb:
*מאז הגדתי.* 
מטרם היותם ופתאום עשיתים:
rashi.eng: *I told from then.* When they had not yet come about, and suddenly I did it.

rashi.heb:
*ותבאנה.* 
כמו שהגדתי תחלה על פי נביאי:
rashi.eng: *and they came to pass.* as I told before through My prophets.

notes.2056: (tn): The words “I did this” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons. In the Hebrew text v. 4 is subordinated to v. 3.
notes.2057: (sn): The image is that of a person who has tensed the muscles of the face and neck as a sign of resolute refusal.

rashi.heb:
*מדעתי כי קשה אתה.* 
מאשר ידעתי אותך כי קשה אתה ואם יבא הנס ולא הגדתיו תחלה תאמר עצבי עשאם ולא מאת הקב"ה הם לפיכך אגיד לך מאז בטר' תבא וגו', מדעתי מ"ם זו משמשת נתינת טעם כמו לפי שידעתי ודוגמתו כי מאהבת ה' אתכם ומשמרו את השבועה (דברים ז׳:ח׳):
rashi.eng: *Because of My knowledge that you are obstinate..* Heb. מִדַּעְתִּי. Because I knew you, that you are obstinate, and if the miracle would come and I had not told of it before, you would say, “My idol performed them, and they were not from the Holy One, blessed be He.” Therefore, I told you from then; when it had not yet come to pass etc. מִדַּעְתִּי [although usually translated ‘from My knowledge,’ in this case,]; the ‘mem’ denotes the giving of a reason, like ‘Because I knew.’ A similar form [is found in Deut. 7:8:], “For, because of the Lord’s love (מֵאַהֲבַת) for you, and because of His observing (וּמִשָּׁמְרוֹ) the oath.”

notes.2058: (tn, Heb): “gaze [at] all of it”; KJV “see all this.”
notes.2059: (tn, Heb): “[as for] you, will you not declare?”
notes.2060: (tn, Heb): “and hidden things, and you do not know them.”

rashi.heb:
*שמעת חזה כלה.* 
שמעת הראשונות שהגדתי ראה שבאו כולם:
rashi.eng: *You have heard, see all of it.* You have heard the first ones that I told; see that all of them have come about.

rashi.heb:
*ואתם הלוא תגידו.* 
ותעידוני אשר לא נפל דבר:
rashi.eng: *and you, will you not tell.* and testify for Me that nothing failed?

rashi.heb:
*השמעתיך חדשות מעתה.* 
עתה אני חוזר ומשמיעכם חדשות שהם חדשות לכם ולפני הם גלויות מעולם:
rashi.eng: *I let you hear new things from now.* Now I come back and let you hear new things that are new to you, but to Me they are revealed from time immemorial.

rashi.heb:
*ונצורות.* 
ושמורות באוצרותי ואתה לא ידעתם:
rashi.eng: *and hidden things.* and things guarded in My treasure houses, and you did not know them.

notes.2061: (tn, Heb): “are created” (so KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NLT “They are brand new.”

rashi.heb:
*עתה.* 
נבראו ולא מאז הם:
rashi.eng: *Now they have been created and not from then.* are they.

rashi.heb:
*ולפני יום.* 
היותם אני משמיעכם:
rashi.eng: *and before the day.* that they take place I let you hear of them.

rashi.heb:
*ולא שמעתם.* 
עד היום ולפני יום מוסב על השמעתיך האמור למעלה:
rashi.eng: *and you did not hear them.* until this day. The words, “and before the day,” refer back to “I let you hear,” as stated above.

notes.2063: (tn, Heb): “beforehand your ear did not open.”
notes.2064: (tn, Heb): “deceiving, you deceive.” The infinitive absolute precedes the finite verb for emphasis.

rashi.heb:
*גם לא שמעת וגו'.* 
ת"י אף לא שמעת למילי נבייא אף לא קבילתא אולפן אורייתא אף לפתגמי ברכן ולווטין קיימי דאקימית עמכון בחורב לא ארכינתא אודנך:
rashi.eng: *Neither did you hearken.* Jonathan renders: Neither did you hearken to the words of the prophets, neither did you accept the teaching of the Torah, nor did you bend your ear to the words of the blessings and the curses of My covenant that I established with you at Horeb.

rashi.heb:
*כי ידעתי בגוד תבגוד.* 
כשירדתי להצילך מיד מצרים גלוי היה לפני שסופך לבגוד ואעפ"כ שמרתי שבועות אבות וזהו שנא' ראה ראיתי את עני עמי (שמות ג׳:ז׳) שתי ראיות רואה אני שסופן לבגוד ומכל מקום ראיתי את עני עמי כך דרש ר' תנחומא:
rashi.eng: *for I knew that you would deal treacherously.* When I came down to save you from the hands of the Egyptians, it was revealed to Me that you would eventually deal treacherously. Nevertheless, I kept the oath of the Patriarchs. This is what is stated (Ex. 3:7): “I saw the affliction of My people.” [The Hebrew expression for “I saw,” is רָאֹה רָאִיתִי, a double verb form, which denotes] two seeings. I see that they will eventually deal treacherously, but, nevertheless, I saw the affliction of My people. Rabbi Tanhuma expounded it in this manner.

rashi.heb:
*ופושע מבטן.* 
משהיית' במצרים כמו שמפורש (ביחזקאל כ׳:ה׳) ואודע להם בארץ מצרים וגו' ואומר אליהם וגו':
rashi.eng: *and… transgressor from the womb.* Since you were in Egypt, as it is related in Ezekiel (20:5): “And I made Myself known in the land of Egypt, etc. (v. 7) and I said to them, [Cast away, each man the abominations of his eyes, and do not contaminate yourselves with the idols of Egypt].”

notes.2066: (tn, Heb): “for the sake of my name” (so NAB, NASB); NLT “for my own sake.”
notes.2067: (tn, Heb): “and my praise.” לְמַעַן (l�ma’an, “for the sake of”) is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
notes.2068: (tn, Heb): “I restrain [myself] concerning you not to cut you off.”

rashi.heb:
*אאריך אפי.* 
לשון הוה הוא:
rashi.eng: *I defer My anger.* Heb. (אַאֲרִיךְ אַפִּי). Despite the future form, it is an expression of the present.

rashi.heb:
*ותהלתי אחטם לך.* 
וזאת היא תהלתי אשר אחטם לך ל' חוטם אסתו' חוטמי מצאת עשן נחירי ומקצוף עליך שהכועס יוצא עשן מנחיריו כמה דאת אמר עלה עשן באפו (תהילים י״ח:ט׳) וכן כל חרון אף הוא לשון חימום החוטם חרה אפי וכן ועצמי חרה מני חורב (איוב ל׳:ל׳) נחר חוטמי מרוב חימום:
rashi.eng: *and My praise is that I restrain My wrath.* Heb. אֶחֱטָם. And this is My praise, that I restrain My wrath for you. אֶחֱטָם is an expression of חֹטֶם, a nose. I will close My nose not to allow the smoke of My nostrils to go out and not to be angry with you, for, when one is angry, smoke comes out of his nostrils, as Scripture states (Ps. 18:9): “Smoke rose in His nose.” Likewise, every expression of ‘kindling of anger’ אַף) (חֲרוֹן is an expression of the heating of the nose, (Job. 42:7) “My anger was kindled (חָרָה אַפִּי).” Comp. also (ibid. 30:30) “And my bones were burnt (חָרָה) from heat.” My nose was heated (נִחַר) from much heat."

notes.2069: (tc): The Hebrew text has בְּחַרְתִּיךָ (b�khartikha, “I have chosen you”), but the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa reads correctly בחנתיכה (“I have tested you”). The metallurgical background of the imagery suggests that purification through testing is the idea.

rashi.heb:
*ולא בכסף.* 
ולא ע"י אור של גיהנם כצורף הכסף באור:
rashi.eng: *but not as silver.* [lit. but not with silver.] Not with the fire of Gehinnom, as silver is refined through fire.

rashi.heb:
*בחרתיך.* 
בחרתי לך כור עוני כנגד אור כור הוא כלי שמתיכין בו כסף וזהב:
rashi.eng: *I have chosen for you.* Heb. בְּחַרְתִּיךָ. I have chosen for you the crucible of poverty as opposed to the crucible of fire. A crucible (כּוּר) is a vessel in which they melt silver and gold.

notes.2070: (tn): The Hebrew text repeats לְמַעֲנִי (l�ma’ani, “for my sake”) for emphasis.
notes.2071: (tn): The Hebrew text reads literally, “for how can it be defiled?” The subject of the verb is probably “name” (v. 9).

rashi.heb:
*למעני.* 
ולמען שמי הקדוש:
rashi.eng: *For My sake.* For the sake of My holy name.

rashi.heb:
*כי איך יחל.* 
איך יחולל שמי בהכריתו אתכם
rashi.eng: *for how shall it be profaned.* How shall My name be profaned when I utterly destroy you?

rashi.heb:
*וכבודי לאחר לא אתן.* 
שאויבי יאמרו יד גלוליהם רמה:
rashi.eng: *And My honor I will not give to another.* That your enemies shall say that their God is powerful.

notes.2073: (tn, Heb): “I [am] he, I [am the] first, also I [am the] last.”

rashi.heb:
*שמע אלי יעקב.* 
שם שקרא לך אביך:
rashi.eng: *Hearken to Me, O Jacob.* The name that your father called you.

rashi.heb:
*וישראל מקראי.* 
מאתי נקראת ישראל וי"ת וישראל מזומני:
rashi.eng: *and Israel, who was called by Me.* You were called Israel by Me (Gen. 32:29). Jonathan renders: Israel, My summoned one.

notes.2074: (sn): This probably refers to the idol gods (see v. 5).
notes.2075: (tn): Or “friend,” or “covenant partner.” The Lord’s ally is a reference to Cyrus.

rashi.heb:
*ה' אהבו.* 
לזה שיעשה חפצו של הקב"ה בבבל:
rashi.eng: *The Lord loves him.* He who will perform the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, upon Babylon.

rashi.heb:
*וזרועו.* 
יראה בארץ כשדים ועל כורש אמר כן:
rashi.eng: *and [show] His arm.* He will show in the land of the Chaldees, and concerning Cyrus he states this.

notes.2077: (tn, Heb): “and his way will be prosperous.”

rashi.heb:
*אני.* 
גאלתי ישראל ממצרים ואני אגאל כל ישראל מגלות אחרון ומארבע כנפות הארץ:
rashi.eng: *I.* redeemed Israel from Egypt, and I will redeem all Israel from the last exile and from the four corners of the earth.

rashi.heb:
*אף קראתיו.* 
לכורש, וי"ת ה' אהבו לישראל אף קראתיו לאברהם וקריאה זו ל' גידול להיות מקוראי כמו אלה קרואי העדה (במדבר א׳:ט״ז):
rashi.eng: *I even called him.* [i.e., I called] Cyrus. Others say: The Lord loves Israel. I even called him, [i.e.,] Abraham. This calling is an expression of exaltation, to be My called one. Comp. (Num. 1:16), “These are the called ones of the congregation.”

notes.2078: (tn, Heb): “from the time of its occurring.”
notes.2079: (sn): The speaker here is not identified specifically, but he is probably Cyrus, the Lord’s “ally” mentioned in vv. 14-15.

rashi.heb:
*מעת היותה שם אני.* 
מעידן דאיתפרשו עממיא מדחלתי תמן אנא קריבתיה לאברהם אבוכון לפולחני:
rashi.eng: *from the time it was, there was I.* [Jonathan paraphrases:] From the time the nations ceased fearing Me, there I brought Abraham your father near to My service.

rashi.heb:
*ועתה ה' אלהים שלחני ורוחו.*
