על עשותו זאת אחלק לו נחלה וגורל ברבים עם האבות הראשונים:
rashi.eng: *Therefore.* Because he did this, I will allot him an inheritance and a lot in public with the Patriarchs.

rashi.heb:
*הערה למות נפשו.* 
לשון ותער כדה (בראשית כד):
rashi.eng: *he poured out his soul to death.* Heb. הֶעֱרָה. An expression like (Gen. 24:20), “And she emptied (וַתְּעַר) her pitcher.”

rashi.heb:
*ואת פושעים נמנה.* 
סבל יסורין כאלו חטא ופשע והוא בשביל אחרים נשא חטא הרבים:
rashi.eng: *and with transgressors he was counted.* He suffered torments as if he had sinned and transgressed, and this is because of others; he bore the sin of the many.

rashi.heb:
*ולפושעים יפגיע.* 
על ידי יסורין שבאת על ידו טובה לעולם:
rashi.eng: *and interceded for the transgressors.* through his sufferings, for good came to the world through him.

rashi.heb:
*רני עקרה.* 
ירושלים אשר היתה כלא ילדה:
rashi.eng: *Sing, you barren woman.* Jerusalem, who was as though she had not borne.

rashi.heb:
*לא חלה.* 
ל' לידה הוא שהיולדת על ידי חיל וחבלי' יולדת:
rashi.eng: *you who have not experienced birth pangs.* Heb. חָלָה, an expression of childbirth, for the woman in confinement gives birth with pains and writhing.

rashi.heb:
*מבני בעולה.* 
בת אדום:
rashi.eng: *for the children of the desolate one.* The daughter of Edom.

notes.2290: (tn, Heb): “the curtains of our dwelling places let them stretch out.”

rashi.heb:
*יטו.* 
למרחוק:
rashi.eng: *and let them stretch forth.* far off.

rashi.heb:
*מיתריך.* 
הם חבלים דקים התלוים בשולי אהלים וקושרי' ביתדות שקורין קביל"ס בלע"ז ותוקעין בארץ:
rashi.eng: *lengthen your cords.* These are thin ropes that hang at the bottom of tents, and that are tied to stakes called ‘chevills’ in French, which are thrust into the ground.

rashi.heb:
*תפרוצי.* 
תגברו:
rashi.eng: *shall you prevail.* Heb. תִּפְרֹצִי, shall you prevail.

notes.2294: (tn): Another option is to translate, “the disgrace of our widowhood” (so NRSV). However, the following context (vv. 6-7) refers to Zion’s husband, the Lord, abandoning her, not dying. This suggests that an אַלְמָנָה (’almanah) was a woman who had lost her husband, whether by death or abandonment.

rashi.heb:
*עלומיך.* 
נעוריך:
rashi.eng: *your youth.* Heb. עֲלוּמַיִךְ, your youth.

notes.2296: (sn): See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

notes.2297: (tn, Heb): “like a woman abandoned and grieved in spirit.”

rashi.heb:
*כי תמאס.* 
כשתמאס פעמים שכועס עליה מעט:
rashi.eng: *who was rejected.* When she is rejected at times that her husband is a little wroth with her.

notes.2299: (tn): According to BDB 1009 s.v. שֶׁטֶף the noun שֶׁצֶף here is an alternate form of שֶׁטֶף (shetef, “flood”). Some relate the word to an alleged Akkadian cognate meaning “strength.”
notes.2300: (tn, Heb): “I hid my face from you.”

rashi.heb:
*בשצף קצף.* 
מנחם פתר חרי אף ודונש אמר במעט קצף כמו ברגע קטן עזבתיך וכן ת"י:
rashi.eng: *With a little wrath.* Heb. שֶׁצֶף. Menahem (Machbereth p. 179) interprets this as, “with kindling of wrath,” and Dunash (Teshuvoth p. 20) states, “with a little wrath,” paralleling “For a small moment have I forsaken you,” and so did Jonathan render.

rashi.heb:
*ובחסד עולם.* 
שיתקיים עד עולם:
rashi.eng: *and with everlasting kindness.* that will exist forever.

notes.2302: (tc): The Hebrew text reads literally, “For [or “indeed”] the waters of Noah [is] this to me.” כִּי־מֵי (ki-me, “for the waters of”) should be emended to כְּמֵי (k�mey, “like the days of”), which is supported by the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa and all the ancient versions except LXX.
notes.2303: (tn, Heb): “the waters of Noah” (so NAB, NIV, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*כי מי נח זאת לי.* 
שבועה בידי והולך ומפרש דברו כאשר נשבעתי מעבור מי נח וגו':
rashi.eng: *For this is to Me [as] the waters of Noah.* [i.e.,] it is an oath in My hand, and He proceeds to explain His words, “as I swore that the waters of Noah shall never again pass over the earth, etc.”

notes.2304: (tn, Heb): “peace” (so many English versions); NLT “of blessing.”

rashi.heb:
*כי ההרים ימושו.* 
אף אם תכלה זכות אבות ואמהות חסדי מאתך לא ימוש:
rashi.eng: *For the mountains shall depart.* Even if the merit of the Patriarchs and the Matriarchs is depleted, My kindness shall not depart from you.

rashi.heb:
*סוערה.* 
שלבה סוער ברובי צרות:
rashi.eng: *tempestuous one.* whose heart storms with many troubles.

rashi.heb:
*מרביץ בפוך.* 
רוצף רצפתך מאבני נופך:
rashi.eng: *I will set with carbuncle.* I pave your floor with carbuncle stones.

notes.2306: (tn): Perhaps, “rubies” (so ASV, NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT).
notes.2307: (tn): On the meaning of אֶקְדָּח (’eqdakh), which occurs only here, see HALOT 82 s.v.

rashi.heb:
*כדכד.* 
מין אבן טובה:
rashi.eng: *jasper.* Heb. כַּדְכֹד, a kind of precious stone.

rashi.heb:
*שמשותיך.* 
י"ת אמך ומנחם חברו עם ישמשוניה ויש פותרין ל' שמש חלונות שחמה זורחת בהן ועושין כנגדו מחיצה במיני זכוכית צבעים לנוי ומדרש תהלים פותר שמשותיך ושמש ומגן (תהילים פ״ד:י״ב) שיני החומה:
rashi.eng: *your windows.* Jonathan renders: your woodwork, and Menahem associated it with (Dan. 7:10): “ministered to Him (יְשַׁמְּשׁוּנֵהּ).” (Menahem, apparently renders: your utensils, i.e., the vessels that serve you.) And some interpret it as an expression of a sun (שֶׁמֶשׁ), windows through which the sun shines, and they make opposite it a barrier of kinds of colored glass for beauty, and Midrash Psalms interprets שִׁמְשׁוֹתַיִךְ as well as שֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן (Ps. 84:12) as “the pinnacles of the wall.”

rashi.heb:
*לאבני אקדח.* 
י"ת לאבני גמר גומרין תרגום גחלים פתר אקדח לשון קדחי אש והם מין אבנים טובות בוערות כלפידי' והוא קרבונקל"א לשון גחלת ויש פותרין ל' מקדח אבנים גדולות שכל חלל הפתח קדוח בתוכו והמזוזות והמפתן והסף כולן מתוך האבן הם:
rashi.eng: *of carbuncle stones.* Heb. אֶקְדָּח. Jonathan renders: of gomer stones. Gumrin is the Aramaic translation of גֶּחָלִים, coals. He interprets אֶקְדָּח as an expression similar to (supra 50:11) “who kindle (קֹדְחֵי) fire,” and they are a type of stones that burn like torches and that is the carbuncle (karbokle in O.F.), an expression of a coal. Others interpret it as an expression of a drill, i. e., huge stones of which the entire opening of the doorway is drilled, and the doorposts, the threshold, and the lintel are all hewn from the stone.

rashi.heb:
*לאבני חפץ.* 
לאבני צרוך:
rashi.eng: *of precious stones.* Desirable stones [from Jonathan].

notes.2310: (tn, Heb): “and great [will be] the peace of your sons.”

notes.2311: (tn, Heb): “in righteousness [or “vindication”] you will be established.” The precise meaning of צְדָקָה (ts�daqah) here is uncertain. It could mean “righteousness, justice,” indicating that the city will be a center for justice. But the context focuses on deliverance, suggesting that the term means “deliverance, vindication” here.
notes.2312: (tn, Heb): “Be far from oppression!” The imperative is used here in a rhetorical manner to express certainty and assurance. See GKC 324 �110.c.
notes.2313: (tn, Heb): “from terror.” The rhetorical command, “be far” is understood by ellipsis here. Note the preceding context.

rashi.heb:
*רחקי מעושק.* 
כמו (לעיל נב) התנערי מעפר תרחקי מן העושקי' אותך:
rashi.eng: *go far away from oppression.* [Although grammatically this is the imperative, here it is the future,] like (supra 52:2) “Shake yourself from the dust.” You will be far away from those who oppress you.

rashi.heb:
*רחקי מעושק.* 
תרחק מלעשוק בני אדם כדרך שעושים רשעים שאוספי' ממון מגזל אבל אתם לא תצרכו לגזול כי לא תיראו מדלות ועניות וממחתה כי לא תבא ולא תקר' אליך אברבנאל)
rashi.eng: *[go far away from oppression.* You will stay far from oppressing other peoples in the manner the wicked do, that they accumulate money through robbery, but you will not need to rob, for you will not fear poverty or straits, or ruin, for it shall neither come nor shall it approach you. [Abarbanel]]

rashi.heb:
*בצדקה.* 
שתעשה תהיה נכונה בגאולת עולם ותהיה רחוקה מעושק בני אדם כי לא תראי אפי' פחד ויראה לא יהיה לך מהם ותהיה רחוקה ממחתה שלא תקרב אליך, איל"ה שלוח'):
rashi.eng: *[With righteousness.* that you will perform, you will be established with an everlasting redemption, and you will be far from people’s oppression for you will not fear; you will not even have terror or fear of them, and you will be far from ruin, for it will not come near you. [Ayalah Sheluchah]]

notes.2315: (tn): The infinitive absolute precedes the finite verb here for emphasis.
notes.2316: (tn, Heb): “will fall over you.” The expression נָפַל עַל (nafal ’al) can mean “attack,” but here it means “fall over to,” i.e., “surrender to.”

rashi.heb:
*הן גור יגור אפס מאותי.* 
הן ירא יירא ויגור מגזרת רעו' אותו שאין אני עמו הוא שעיר:
rashi.eng: *Behold, the one with whom I am not, shall fear.* Heb. גּוֹר יָגוּר. Behold, he shall fear and dread evil decrees, he with whom I am not, i.e., Esau. ([Mss. read:] the wicked Esau and his ilk.)

rashi.heb:
*מי גר אתך.* 
מי אשר נאסף עליך למלחמה, או מי גר מי שנתגרה בך, ורבותינו פירשוהו בגרים לומ' שאין מקבלי' גרים לימות משיחנו ואף בפשוטו של מקרא יתכן מי שנעשו גרים אתך בעניותך עליך יפול בעשירותך כמו על פני כל אחיו נפל (בראשית כ״ה:י״ח):
rashi.eng: *whoever mobilizes against you.* Heb. גָר. Whoever mobilizes against you for war. Alternatively, מִי גָר [means:] whoever contends with you (וְנִתְגָּרֶה). And our Rabbis explained it as referring to the proselytes (גֵּרִים) , [i.e.,] to say that we will not accept proselytes in Messianic times. And even according to the simple meaning of the verse it is possible to explain: whoever became sojourners with you in your poverty, shall dwell with you in your wealth. Comp. (Gen. 25:18) “In the presence of all his brethren he dwelt (נָפָל).”

notes.2317: (tn, Heb): “who brings out an implement for his work.”

rashi.heb:
*הנה אנכי.* 
אשר בראתי חרש המתקן כלי ואני אשר בראתי משחית המחבלו כלו' אני הוא שגריתי בך את האוי' אני הוא שהתקנתי לו פורעניות:
rashi.eng: *Behold I.* am He Who created a smith who devises a weapon, and I am He Who has created a destroyer that destroys it. That is, to say: I am He Who incited the enemy against you; I am He Who has prepared retribution for him.

rashi.heb:
*ומוציא כלי למעשהו.* 
לצורך גומרו כל צורכו:
rashi.eng: *and produces a weapon for his work.* For necessity. He completes it according to all that is necessary.

notes.2318: (tn, Heb): “and every tongue that rises up for judgment with you will prove to be guilty.”
notes.2319: (tn, Heb): “this is the inheritance of the servants of the Lord, and their vindication from me.”

rashi.heb:
*כל כלי יוצר.* 
כל כלי זיין אשר ילטשוהו ויחדדהו בשבילך להלחם בך:
rashi.eng: *Any weapon whetted against you.* Any weapon that they will whet and sharpen for you, i.e., to battle with you.

rashi.heb:
*יוצר.* 
ל' חרבות צורים (יהושע ה׳:ב׳) אף תשיב צור חרבו (תהילים פ״ט:מ״ד):
rashi.eng: *whetted.* Heb. יוּצַר, an expression similar to (Jos. 5:2) “sharp knives (חַרְבוֹת צֻרִים),” also (Ps. 89:44) “You have also turned the edge of his sword (צוּר חַרְבּוֹ).”

notes.2320: (tn): The Hebrew term הוֹי (hoy, “woe, ah”) was used in funeral laments and is often prefixed to judgment oracles for rhetorical effect. But here it appears to be a simple interjection, designed to grab the audience’s attention. Perhaps there is a note of sorrow or pity. See BDB 223 s.v.
notes.2321: (sn): The statement is an oxymoron. Its ironic quality adds to its rhetorical impact. The statement reminds one of the norm (one must normally buy commodities) as it expresses the astounding offer. One might paraphrase the statement: “Come and take freely what you normally have to pay for.”

rashi.heb:
*הוי כל צמא.* 
הוי זה ל' קריאה וזימון וקיבוץ הוא ויש הרבה במקרא (זכריה ב) הוי הוי ונוסו מארץ צפון:
rashi.eng: *Ho! All who thirst.* Heb. הוֹי. This word הוֹי is an expression of calling, inviting, and gathering, and there are many in Scripture, [e. g.,] (Zech. 2:10) “Ho! Ho! and flee from the north land.”

rashi.heb:
*לכו למים.* 
לתורה:
rashi.eng: *go to water.* to Torah.

rashi.heb:
*שברו.* 
ל' לשבור בר (בראשית מב) קנו:
rashi.eng: *buy.* Heb. שִׁבְרוּ. Comp. (Gen. 42:3) “To buy (לִשְׁבֹּר) corn,” buy.

rashi.heb:
*יין וחלב.* 
לקח טוב מיין וחלב:
rashi.eng: *wine and milk.* Teaching better than wine and milk.

notes.2323: (tn): The interrogative particle and the verb “spend” are understood here by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
notes.2324: (tn, Heb): “your labor,” which stands by metonymy for that which one earns.
notes.2325: (tn): The infinitive absolute follows the imperative and lends emphasis to the exhortation.
notes.2327: (tn, Heb): “Let your appetite delight in fine food.” Nourishing, fine food here represents the blessings God freely offers. These include forgiveness, a new covenantal relationship with God, and national prominence (see vv. 3-6).

rashi.heb:
*למה תשקלו כסף.* 
למה תגרמו לכם לשקול כסף לאויביכם בלא לחם:
rashi.eng: *Why should you weigh out money.* Why should you cause yourselves to weigh out money to your enemies without bread?

notes.2328: (tn): The jussive with vav (ו) conjunctive following the imperative indicates purpose/result. To live here refers to covenantal blessing, primarily material prosperity and national security (see vv. 4-5, 13, and Deut 30:6, 15, 19-20).
notes.2330: (tn, Heb): “the reliable expressions of loyalty of David.” The syntactical relationship of חַסְדֵי (khasde, “expressions of loyalty”) to the preceding line is unclear. If the term is appositional to בְּרִית (b�rit, “covenant”), then the Lord here transfers the promises of the Davidic covenant to the entire nation. Another option is to take חַסְדֵי (khasde) as an adverbial accusative and to translate “according to the reliable covenantal promises.” In this case the new covenantal arrangement proposed here is viewed as an extension or perhaps fulfillment of the Davidic promises. A third option, the one reflected in the above translation, is to take the last line as comparative. In this case the new covenant being proposed is analogous to the Davidic covenant. Verses 4-5, which compare David’s international prominence to what Israel will experience, favors this view. In all three of these interpretations, “David” is an objective genitive; he is the recipient of covenantal promises. A fourth option would be to take David as a subjective genitive and understand the line as giving the basis for the preceding promise: “Then I will make an unconditional covenantal promise to you, because of David’s faithful acts of covenantal loyalty.”

rashi.heb:
*חסדי דוד.* 
שאגמול לדוד חסדיו:
rashi.eng: *the dependable mercies of David.* For I will repay David for his mercies.

notes.2331: (sn): Ideally the Davidic king was to testify to the nations of God’s greatness (cf. Pss 18:50 HT [18:49 ET]; 22:28 HT [22:27 ET]). See J. H. Eaton, Kingship in the Psalms (SBT), 182-84.

rashi.heb:
*לאומים.* 
שר וגדול עליהם ומוכיח ומעיד דרכיהם על פניהם:
rashi.eng: *a witness to nations.* A prince and a superior over them, and one who will reprove and testify of their ways to their faces. ([Mss., however, read:] One who reproaches them for their ways to their faces.)

notes.2332: (tn, Heb): “a nation,” but the singular is collective here, as the plural verbs in the next line indicate (note that both “know” and “run” are third plural forms).
notes.2333: (tn, Heb): “a nation,” but the singular is collective here, as the plural verbs that follow indicate.
notes.2334: (sn): See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

rashi.heb:
*הן גוי לא תדע תקרא.* 
לשמושך אם אלי תשמעו לשם ה' הנקרא עליך:
rashi.eng: *Behold, a nation you do not know you shall call.* to your service, if you hearken to Me, to the name of the Lord that is called upon you.

notes.2335: (tn, Heb): “while he allows himself to be found.” The Niphal form has a tolerative force here.

rashi.heb:
*בהמצאו.* 
קודם גזר דין בעוד שהוא אומר לכם דרשוני:
rashi.eng: *when He is found.* Before the verdict is promulgated, when He still says to you, “Seek Me.”

notes.2336: (tn, Heb): “Let the wicked one abandon his way.” The singular is collective.
notes.2337: (tn, Heb): “and the man of evil his thoughts.” The singular is collective.
notes.2338: (tn, Heb): “let him return.” The singular is collective, meaning “let them.”
notes.2339: (tn): The imperfect with vav (ו) conjunctive after the jussive indicates purpose/result.
notes.2340: (sn): The appeal and promise of vv. 6-7 echoes the language of Deut 4:25-31; 30:1-10; and 1 Kgs 8:46-53, all of which anticipate the exile and speak of the prerequisites for restoration.

notes.2343: (tn, Heb): “are not.” “Like” is interpretive, but v. 9 indicates that a comparison is in view.
notes.2345: (tn, Heb): “are not.” “Like” is interpretive, but v. 9 indicates that a comparison is in view.

rashi.heb:
*כי לא מחשבותי מחשבותיכם.* 
אין שלי ושלכם שוות לכך אני אומר לכם יעזוב רשע דרכו ויתפוש את דרכי:
rashi.eng: *For My thoughts are not your thoughts.* Mine and yours are not the same; therefore, I say to you, “The wicked shall give up his way,” and adopt My way…

rashi.heb:
*ואיש און מחשבותיו.* 
ויתפוש את מחשבותי לעשות הטוב בעיני, ומדרש אגדה:
rashi.eng: *“and a man of iniquity his thoughts”.* and adopt My thoughts, to do what is good in My eyes. And the Midrash Aggadah (Tanhuma Buber, Vayeshev 11 explains:)

rashi.heb:
*כי לא מחשבותי וגו'.* 
אין דיני כדיני בשר ודם אתם מי שמודה בדין מתחייב אבל אני מודה ועוזב ירוחם (משלי כה):
rashi.eng: *For My thoughts are not, etc..* My laws are not like the laws of man [lit. flesh and blood]. As for you, whoever confesses in judgment is found guilty, but, as for Me, whoever confesses and gives up his evil way, is granted clemency (Proverbs 28:13).

notes.2346: (tn): Or “the heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heavens” or “sky” depending on the context.

rashi.heb:
*כי גבהו שמים וגו'.* 
כלומר כי יש הבדל וחילוק מעלות ושבח בדרכי יותר מדרכיכ' ובמחשבותי יותר ממחשבותיכם כגבוה שמים על הארץ אתם נותנים לב למרוד בי ואני נותן לב להשיב אתכם:
rashi.eng: *As the heavens are higher, etc..* That is to say that there is a distinction and a difference, advantages and superiority in My ways more than your ways and in My thoughts more than your thoughts, as the heavens are higher than the earth; you are intent upon rebelling against Me, whereas I am intent upon bringing you back.

notes.2350: (tn): This verse begins in the Hebrew text with כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר (ki ka’asher, “for, just as”), which is completed by כֵּן (ken, “so, in the same way”) at the beginning of v. 11. For stylistic reasons, this lengthy sentence is divided up into separate sentences in the translation.

rashi.heb:
*כי כאשר ירד הגשם והשלג.* 
ולא ישוב ריקם אך ייטיב לעולם:
rashi.eng: *For, just as the rain and the snow fall.* and do not return empty, but do good for you.

notes.2351: (tn, Heb): “so is the word which goes out from my mouth, it does not return to empty.” “Word” refers here to divine promises, like the ones made just prior to and after this (see vv. 7b, 12-13).
notes.2352: (tn, Heb): “but it accomplishes what I desire, and succeeds [on the mission] which I send it.” Verses 8-11 focus on the reliability of the divine word and support the promises before (vv. 3-5, 7b) and after (vv. 12-13) this. Israel can be certain that repentance will bring forgiveness and a new covenantal relationship because God’s promises are reliable. In contrast to human plans (or “thoughts”), which are destined to fail (Ps 94:11) apart from divine approval (Prov 19:21), and human deeds (or “ways”), which are evil and lead to destruction (Prov 1:15-19; 3:31-33; 4:19), God’s plans are realized and his deeds accomplish something positive.

rashi.heb:
*כן יהיה דברי אשר יצא מפי.* 
להודיעכם ע"י הנביאים לא ישוב ריקם אך ייטיב לכם אם תשמעו להם:
rashi.eng: *so shall be My word that emanates from My mouth.* to inform you through the prophets, will not return empty, but will do good to you if you heed them.

rashi.heb:
*כי בשמחה תצאו.* 
מן הגלות:
rashi.eng: *For with joy shall you go forth.* from the exile.

rashi.heb:
*ההרים והגבעות יפצחו לפניכם רנה.* 
שיתנו לכם פריים וצמחם ויהנו (ירוננו) יושביהם:
rashi.eng: *the mountains and the hills shall burst into song before you.* for they will give you their fruit and their plants, and their inhabitants shall derive benefit. ([Some editions read:] And their inhabitants shall sing.)

notes.2353: (tn, Heb): “to the Lord for a name.” For שֵׁם (shem) used in the sense of “monument,” see also 56:5, where it stands parallel to יָד (yad).
notes.2354: (tn): Or, more literally, “a permanent sign that will not be cut off.”

rashi.heb:
*תחת הנעצוץ וגו'.* 
רבותינו דרשו תחת הרשעים יעלו צדיקים:
rashi.eng: *Instead of the briar, etc..* Our Rabbis expounded [Targum Jonathan]: Instead of the wicked, righteous people shall arise.

rashi.heb:
*נעצוץ.* 
וסרפד מיני קוצים הם כלומר הרשעים יאבדו והצדיקים יטלו ממשלתם:
rashi.eng: *briar… and… nettle.* They are species of thorns; i.e., to say that the wicked will be destroyed and the righteous will take their rule.

notes.2355: (tn, Heb): “guard”; KJV “Keep”; NAB “Observe”; NASB “Preserve”; NIV, NRSV “Maintain.”
notes.2356: (tn, Heb): “for near is my deliverance to enter, and my vindication [or “righteousness”] to be revealed.”

notes.2357: (tn, Heb): “blessed is the man who does this.”
notes.2358: (tn, Heb): “the son of mankind who takes hold of it.”
notes.2359: (tn, Heb): and who keeps his hand from doing any evil.”

rashi.heb:
*יעשה זאת.* 
שומר שבת וגו':
rashi.eng: *who will do this.* who observes the Sabbath, etc.

notes.2361: (tn): The infinitive absolute precedes the finite verb for emphasis.

rashi.heb:
*הבדל יבדילני ה' מעל עמו.* 
למה אתגייר הלא הקב"ה יבדילני מעל עמו כשישלם שכרם:
rashi.eng: *“The Lord will surely separate me from His people,”.* Why should I become converted? Will not the Holy One, blessed be He, separate me from His people when He pays their reward.

rashi.heb:
*ואל יאמר הסריס.* 
למה איטיב דרכי ומעללי הן אני כעץ יבש מאין זכרון:
rashi.eng: *Let not the eunnuch say.* Why should I better my ways and my deeds? I am like a withered tree, for lack of remembrance.

notes.2362: (tn, Heb): “and take hold of” (so KJV); NASB “hold fast.”

rashi.heb:
*ומחזיקים.* 
אוחזים:
rashi.eng: *and hold fast.* Heb. וּמַחֲזִיקִים, and hold fast.

notes.2363: (tn, Heb): “a hand and a name.” For other examples where יָד (yad) refers to a monument, see HALOT 388 s.v.

notes.2366: (tn, Heb): “and take hold of”; NAB “hold to”; NIV, NRSV “hold fast.”

notes.2367: (tn, Heb): “in the house of my prayer.”
notes.2368: (tn, Heb): “for my house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations.”

rashi.heb:
*לכל העמים.* 
ולא לישראל לבדם כי אף לגרים:
rashi.eng: *for all peoples.* Not only for Israel, but also for the proselytes.

notes.2369: (tn): The meaning of the statement is unclear. The text reads literally, “Still I will gather upon him to his gathered ones.” Perhaps the preposition -לְ (lamed) before “gathered ones” introduces the object of the verb, as in Jer 49:5. The third masculine singular suffix on both עָלָיו (’alayv) and נִקְבָּצָיו (niqbatsayv) probably refers to “Israel.” In this case one can translate literally, “Still I will gather to him his gathered ones.”

rashi.heb:
*עוד אקבץ עליו.* 
מן האומות שיתגיירו ונלוו עליהם:
rashi.eng: *I will yet gather.* of the heathens ([Mss. and K’li Paz:] of the nations) who will convert and join them. (

rashi.heb:
*לנקבציו.* 
נוספים על קבוצי ישראל:
rashi.eng: *together with his gathered ones.* In addition to the gathered ones of Israel.)

rashi.heb:
*כל חיתו שדי.* 
כל גירי האומות אתיו והתקרבו אלי ותאכלו את כל חיתו ביער את גבורי האומות שאמצו את לבם מלהתגייר:
rashi.eng: *All the beasts of the field.* All the proselytes of the heathens ([Mss. and K’li Paz:] All the nations) come and draw near to Me, and you shall devour all the beasts in the forest, the mighty of the heathens ([Mss. and K’li Paz:] the mighty of the nations) who hardened their heart and refrained from converting.

rashi.heb:
*חיתו שדי.* 
חית השדה אין כחה רב כחית היער חית השדה חלשה ותשות כח מחית היער ועל שאמר עוד אקבץ עליו אמר המקרא הזה:
rashi.eng: *the beasts of the field.* [The beast of the field is not as strong as the beast of the forest.] The beast of the field is weaker and of weaker strength than the beast of the forest. Since he stated, “I will yet gather others to him,” he stated this verse.

notes.2370: (sn): The “watchmen” are probably spiritual leaders, most likely prophets and priests, responsible for giving the people moral direction.
notes.2371: (tn, Heb): “they do not know”; KJV “they are all ignorant”; NIV “they all lack knowledge.”
notes.2372: (tn): The Hebrew text has הֹזִים (hozim), which appears to be derived from an otherwise unattested verbal root הָזָה (hazah). On the basis of alleged cognates, BDB 223 s.v. הָזָה offers the definition “dream, rave” while HALOT 243 s.v. הזה lists “pant.” In this case the dog metaphor of the preceding lines continues. The reference to dogs at the beginning of v. 11 favors the extension of the metaphor. The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa has חזים (“seers”) here. In this case the “watchmen” are directly identified as prophets and depicted as lazy.

rashi.heb:
*צופיו עורים כולם.* 
לפי שאמר דרשו ה' וכל הענין והם אינם שומעי' חוזר ואומר הנה הנביאים צועקים להם ומכריזים על התשובה ותיטיב להם והרי פרנסיהם כעורים כולם ואינם רואין את הנולדות כצופה המופקד לראות את החרב בא להזהיר את העם והוא עור מלראות את החרב באה ואלם מלהזהיר את העם ככלב שמינוהו לשמור הבית והוא אלם מלבנות כך פרנסי ישראל אינם מזהירין אותם לחזור למוטב:
rashi.eng: *His lookouts are all blind.* Since he said, “Seek the Lord,” and the entire section, and they do not heed, he returns and says, Behold the prophets cry out to them ([Mss.:] to you) and announce concerning repentance, so that it will be good for them. Yet their leaders are all like blind men, and they do not see the results, like a lookout appointed to see the approaching army, to warn the people, but he is blind, unable to see whether the army is coming, and dumb, unable to warn the people, like a dog that was appointed to guard the house, but he is dumb, unable to bark. Similarly, the leaders of Israel do not warn them to repent to do good.

rashi.heb:
*הוזים שוכבים.* 
פי' דונש נרדמים שוכבין ויונתן תירגם ניימין שכבין ואין לו דמיון:
rashi.eng: *they lie slumbering.* Heb. הֹזִים. Dunash (Teshuvoth Dunash p. 24) explained: lying sound asleep, and Jonathan rendered: lying slumbering, and there is no comparable word in Scripture.

notes.2373: (sn): The phrase never full alludes to the greed of the leaders.
notes.2374: (tn, Heb): “for his gain from his end.”

rashi.heb:
*והכלבים עזי נפש.* 
רוצים למלאות כריסם (אינגר"ש בלע"ז):
rashi.eng: *And the dogs are of greedy disposition.* wanting to fill their stomachs [engrote talent in O.F.], sick with hunger.

rashi.heb:
*והמה רועים.* 
כמו שהכלבים לא ידעו שבעה כן הרועים לא ידעו הבין מה יהיה באחרית הימים:
rashi.eng: *and they are shepherds.* Just as the dogs know no satiety, neither do the shepherds know to understand what will occur at the end of days.

rashi.heb:
*כולם.* 
לדרך הנייתם פנו איש לבצעו לגזול את שאר העם שהם ממונים עליהם:
rashi.eng: *they all.* turned to the way of their benefit, each one to his gain, to rob the rest of the people over whom they are appointed.

rashi.heb:
*מקצהו.* 
כמו (בראשית י״ט:ד׳) כל העם מקצה מקצה מניינם ועד קצהו כולם נוהגי' כן:
rashi.eng: *every last one.* Heb. מִקָּצֵהוּ, [lit. from its end.] Comp. (Gen. 19:4) “all the people from the end (מִקָּצֶה),” from one end of their number until its other end, they all behave in this manner.

notes.2375: (tn): The words “each one says” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.2376: (tn, Heb): “great, [in] abundance, very much,” i.e., “very great indeed.” See HALOT 452 s.v. יֶתֶר.

rashi.heb:
*אתיו אקחה יין.* 
כך היו אומרים זה לזה:
rashi.eng: *Come, I will take wine.* So would they say to one another.

rashi.heb:
*והיה כזה יום מחר.* 
במאכל ובמשתה:
rashi.eng: *and tomorrow shall be like this.* with feasting and drinking.

notes.2377: (tn): Or “righteous” (KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT); NAB “the just man”; TEV “Good people.”
notes.2378: (tn, Heb): Or perhaps, “understands.” “and there is no man who sets [it] upon [his] heart.”
notes.2379: (tn, Heb): “Men of loyalty are taken away.” The Niphal of אָסַף (’asaf) here means “to die.”
notes.2380: (tn): The Hebrew term בְּאֵין (b�’en) often has the nuance “when there is no.” See Prov 8:24; 11;14; 14:4; 15:22; 26:20; 29:18.
notes.2382: (tn): Or “righteous” (KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT); NAB “the just man.”
notes.2383: (tn, Heb): “are taken away.” The Niphal of אָסַף (’asaf) here means “to die.”
notes.2384: (tn): The term מִפְּנֵי (mipp�ne, “from the face of”) often has a causal nuance. It also appears with the Niphal of אָסַף (’asaph, “gather”) in 2 Chr 12:5: אֲשֶׁר־נֶאֶסְפוּ אֶל־יְרוּשָׁלַם מִפְּנֵי שִׁישָׁק (’asher-ne’esphu ’el-y�rushalam mipp�ney shishaq, “who had gathered at Jerusalem because of [i.e., due to fear of] Shishak”).
notes.2385: (tn): The translation assumes that this verse, in proverbial fashion, laments society’s apathy over the persecution of the godly. The second half of the verse observes that such apathy results in more widespread oppression. Since the next verse pictures the godly being taken to a place of rest, some interpret the second half of v. 1 in a more positive vein. According to proponents of this view, God removes the godly so that they might be spared suffering and calamity, a fact which the general populace fails to realize.

rashi.heb:
*הצדיק אבד.* 
כגון יאשיהו:
rashi.eng: *The righteous man.* such as Josiah.

rashi.heb:
*ואין איש שם על לב.* 
למה נסתלק:
rashi.eng: *but no one takes it to heart.* why he departed.

rashi.heb:
*באין מבין.* 
אין בנותרים מבין מה ראה הקב"ה לסלקו:
rashi.eng: *with no one understanding.* what the Holy One, blessed be He, saw to take him away.

rashi.heb:
*כי מפני הרעה.* 
העתידה לבא אל הדור נאסף הצדיק:
rashi.eng: *that because of the evil.* destined to befall the generation, the righteous man perished.

notes.2386: (tn, Heb): “he enters peace, they rest on their beds, the one who walks straight ahead of himself.” The tomb is here viewed in a fairly positive way as a place where the dead are at peace and sleep undisturbed.

rashi.heb:
*יבא שלום.* 
כי כן אמר הקב"ה יבא הצדיק הזה אל אבותיו בשלום ואל יראה ברעה:
rashi.eng: *He shall come in peace.* for so says the Holy One, blessed be He, Let this righteous man come to his forefathers in peace, and let him not see the evil.

rashi.heb:
*ינוחו על משכבותם.* 
בהיות הרעה זה שהיה הולך נכוחו ביושרו כמו עשות נכוחה (עמוס ג):
rashi.eng: *they shall rest in their resting place.* when the evil occurs, he who was walking נְכֹחוֹ, in his uprightness. Comp. (Amos 3:10) “To act rightly (נְכֹחָה).”

notes.2387: (tc): The Hebrew text reads literally, “offspring of an adulterer [masculine] and [one who] has committed adultery.” Perhaps the text has suffered from transposition of vav (ו) and tav (ת) and מְנָאֵף וַתִּזְנֶה (m�na’ef vattizneh) should be emended to מְנָאֶפֶת וְזֹנָה (m�na’efet v�zonah, “an adulteress and a prostitute”). Both singular nouns would be understood in a collective sense. Most modern English versions render both forms as nouns.

rashi.heb:
*ואתם קרבו הנה.* 
הנותרים משנסתלקו הצדיקים ותקבלו פורענותיכם:
rashi.eng: *And you, draw near hither.* The survivors after the righteous have departed, and receive your sentences.

rashi.heb:
*בני עוננה.* 
בני כשפים:
rashi.eng: *children of sorcery.* Heb. בְּנֵי עֹנְנָה, children of sorcery.

rashi.heb:
*זרע מנאף.* 
שהזכר מנאף:
rashi.eng: *children who commit adultery.* That the male commits adultery.

rashi.heb:
*ותזנה.* 
הנקבה:
rashi.eng: *and played the whore.* the female.

notes.2388: (tn, Heb): “Are you not children of rebellion, offspring of a lie?” The rhetorical question anticipates the answer, “Of course you are!”

rashi.heb:
*על מי תתענגו.* 
מאחר ששבתם מאחרי על מי תשענו להתענג בטובה אילו זכיתם אז תתענגו על ה' אבל עכשיו על מי תתענגו:
rashi.eng: *On whom will you [rely to] enjoy yourselves.* Since you have turned away from following Me, on whom will you rely to enjoy yourselves with good. Had you merited, you would then enjoy yourselves with the Lord, but now, on whom will you rely to enjoy yourselves?

rashi.heb:
*על מי תרחיבו פה.* 
כשאתם מתעתעים ומלעיבים בנביאיו:
rashi.eng: *against whom do you open your mouth wide.* when you scorned and mocked His prophets.

notes.2389: (tn, Heb): “inflame yourselves”; NRSV “burn with lust.” This verse alludes to the practice of ritual sex that accompanied pagan fertility rites.
notes.2390: (sn): This apparently alludes to the practice of child sacrifice (cf. TEV, CEV, NLT).

rashi.heb:
*הנחמים באלים.* 
המתחממין בש"ז תחת אלה ואלון:
rashi.eng: *You who inflame yourselves among the terebinths.* Who stimulate themselves with semen under the אֵלִים, they are the terebinth and the oak.

rashi.heb:
*שוחטי הילדים.* 
לקרבן עכו"ם:
rashi.eng: *who slaughter the children.* for a sacrifice to the idols.

rashi.heb:
*סעיפי.* 
נקרת הצורים וכן (שופטים ט״ו:י״א) אל סעיף סלע:
rashi.eng: *clefts.* Heb. סְעִפֵי, the clefts of the rocks. Comp. (Jud. 15:11) “to the cleft (סְעִיף) of the rock.”

notes.2391: (tn, Heb): “among the smooth stones of the stream [is] your portion, they, they [are] your lot.” The next line indicates idols are in view.
notes.2392: (tn): The text reads literally, “Because of these am I relenting?” If the prefixed interrogative particle is retained at the beginning of the sentence, then the question would be rhetorical, with the Niphal of נָחָם (nakham) probably being used in the sense of “relent, change one’s mind.” One could translate: “Because of these things, how can I relent?” However, the initial letter he may be dittographic (note the final he [ה] on the preceding word). In this case one may understand the verb in the sense of “console oneself, seek vengeance,” as in 1:24.

rashi.heb:
*בחלקי נחל.* 
אבנים אשר בנחל:
rashi.eng: *Of the smooth [stones] of the valley.* [Lit. of the smooth ones of the valley, i.e.,] among the smooth stones that are in the valley.

rashi.heb:
*חלקך.* 
בהם ירגמו אותך:
rashi.eng: *your portion.* With them they will stone you.

rashi.heb:
*הם הם גורלך.* 
להתעצב בהם למה כי גם להם שפכת נסך:
rashi.eng: *they, they are your lot.* to be saddened with them. Why? For to them too you have poured out libations.

rashi.heb:
*העל אלה אנחם.* 
מלהרע לך:
rashi.eng: *in the face of these shall I relent.* from doing harm to you?

rashi.heb:
*שמת משכבך.* 
משכב ניאופך לעכו"ם על ההרים הרמי':
rashi.eng: *you placed your couch.* The couch of your adultery to idolatry on the high mountains.

notes.2393: (tn): The precise referent of זִכָּרוֹן (zikkaron) in this context is uncertain. Elsewhere the word refers to a memorial or commemorative sign. Here it likely refers to some type of idolatrous symbol.
notes.2395: (tc): The Hebrew text reads literally, “from me you uncover.” The translation assumes an emendation of the Piel form גִּלִּית (gillit, “you uncover”), which has no object expressed here, to the Qal גָּלִית (galit, “you depart”).
notes.2396: (tn, Heb): “you make wide your bed” (NASB similar).
notes.2397: (tc, Heb): “and you [second masculine singular, unless the form be taken as third feminine singular] cut for yourself [feminine singular] from them.” Most English translations retain the MT reading in spite of at least three problems. This section makes significant use of feminine verbs and noun suffixes because of the sexual imagery. The verb in question is likely a 2nd person masculine singular verb. Nevertheless, this kind of fluctuation in gender appears elsewhere (GKC 127-28 �47.k and 462 �144.p; cf. Jer 3:5; Ezek 22:4; 23:32; cf. J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah [NICOT], 2:473, n. 13). Secondly, when this verbal root signifies establishing a covenant, it is normally accompanied by the noun for “covenant” (בְּרִית, b�rit). Finally, this juxtaposition of the verb “to cut” and “covenant” normally is followed by the preposition “with,” while here it is “from.” The translation above assumes an emendation of וַתִּכְרָת (vatikhrah, “and you cut”) to וְכָרִית (v�kharit, “and you purchase”) from the root כָּרָה (kharah); see HALOT 497 s.v. II כרה.
notes.2398: (tn): The Hebrew text has simply חָזָה (khazah, “gaze”). The adverb “longingly” is interpretive (see the context, where sexual lust is depicted).
notes.2399: (tn, Heb): “[at] a hand you gaze.” The term יָד (yad, “hand”) probably has the sense of “power, manhood” here, where it is used, as in Ugaritic, as a euphemism for the genitals. See HALOT 387 s.v. I יָד.

rashi.heb:
*ואחר הדלת והמזוזה שמת זכרונך.* 
למי שהוא מדמה אותה לאשה מנאפ' אשר נואפי' צופים וממתינים לפני פתח ביתה והיא לבה וזכרונה אל הדלת והמזוזה איך תפתח ותצא אליהם:
rashi.eng: *And behind the door and the doorpost you have directed your thoughts.* Since he compares her to an adulterous woman, for whom her paramours look and wait before the door of her house, while she, lying beside her husband, directs her heart and her thoughts to the door and the doorpost, how she will open the door and come out to them.

rashi.heb:
*כי מאתי גלית ותעלי.* 
אצלי היית שוכבת וגלית הכיסוי שהיו מכוסי' יחד ותעלי מאצלי:
rashi.eng: *for while with Me, you uncovered [us] and went up.* You were lying beside Me, and you removed the cover with which we were covered together, and you went up from beside Me.

rashi.heb:
*הרחבת משכבך.* 
לקבל בו נואפי' הרבה:
rashi.eng: *you widened your couch.* to accommodate many adulterers.

rashi.heb:
*ותכרת לך.* 
ברית מהם:
rashi.eng: *and made for yourself.* a covenant with them.

rashi.heb:
*אהבת משכבם.* 
כשחזית לך יד ומקום להראות להם אהבתך:
rashi.eng: *you loved their couch.* when you chose for yourself יָד, a place, to demonstrate to them your love.

rashi.heb:
*יד.* 
אייש"י בלע"ז וכן ראו חלקת יואב אל ידי (ש"ב יד):
rashi.eng: *a place.* Heb. יָד, aise or ajjse in O. F., a side. Comp. (II Sam. 14:30) “See Joab’s field is near mine יָדִי) (עַל.”

notes.2401: (tn, Heb): “the king.” Since the context refers to idolatry and child sacrifice (see v. 5), some emend מֶלֶך (melekh, “king”) to “Molech.” Perhaps Israel’s devotion to her idols is likened here to a subject taking tribute to a ruler.
notes.2403: (sn): Israel’s devotion to her idols is inordinate, irrational, and self-destructive.

rashi.heb:
*ותשורי למלך בשמן.* 
ואני מתחלה גדלתיך והיית מקבלת פני מלכך בכל מיני תפנוקים, ותשורי לשון ראיית פנים כמו אשורנו ולא קרוב (במדבר כ״ד:י״ז) וכן (שמואל א ט׳:ז׳) ותשורה אין להביא דורון של הקבלת פנים:
rashi.eng: *And you brought a gift to the king with oil.* Heb. וַתָּשֻׁרִי. Originally, I aggrandized you, and you would greet your king with all sorts of delights. וַתָּשֻׁרִי is an expression of an audience. Comp. (Num. 24:17) “I see him (אֲשׁוּרֶנוּ) but he is not near.” [Also] (I Sam. 9:7), “And there is no present (תְּשׁוּרָה) to bring,” [i.e.,] a gift for an audience.

rashi.heb:
*ותשלחי ציריך.* 
שלוחייך למרחוק לגבות מס ממלכי האומות:
rashi.eng: *and you sent your ambassadors.* Your messenger afar to collect tribute from the heathen kings. ([Manuscripts and K’li Paz read:] the kings of the nations.)

rashi.heb:
*ותשפילי.* 
את חזקי האומות עד שאול כן תרגמו יונתן:
rashi.eng: *and you humbled.* the laws of the heathens (of the nations [Mss. and K’li Paz]) to the grave. Jonathan rendered it in this manner.

notes.2404: (tn, Heb): “by the greatness [i.e., “length,” see BDB 914 s.v. רֹב 2] of your way you get tired.”
notes.2405: (tn, Heb): “it is hopeless” (so NAB, NASB, NIV); NRSV “It is useless.”
notes.2406: (tn, Heb): “the life of your hand you find.” The term חַיָּה (khayyah, “life”) is here used in the sense of “renewal” (see BDB 312 s.v.) while יָד (yad) is used of “strength.”

rashi.heb:
*ברוב דרכך יגעת.* 
נתעסקת בצרכייך למלאות תאותך להרבות הונך:
rashi.eng: *With the length of your way you became wearied.* You engaged in your necessities, in the filling of your lust, to increase your wealth.

rashi.heb:
*לא אמרת נואש.* 
אתייאש מאלו ולא אחיש עוד לעסוק בהן כי בתורה ובמצות אתן לב:
rashi.eng: *you did not say, “Despair.”.* I will despair of these and I will no longer care to engage in them, but I will pay my attention to Torah and precepts.

rashi.heb:
*חית ידך מצאת.* 
צורך ידך מצאת הצלחת במעשיך:
rashi.eng: *The power of your hand you found.* Heb. חַיַּת, the necessity of your hand you have found; you have succeeded in your deeds.

rashi.heb:
*על כן לא חלית.* 
לא נחלה לבך לדאג על עבודתי לעסוק בתורה חית. לשון ערבי הוא צורך:
rashi.eng: *therefore, you were not stricken ill.* Your heart was not stricken ill to worry about My service, to engage in the Torah. חַיַּת is an Arabic word, meaning necessity.

notes.2408: (tn, Heb): “you do not place [it] on your heart.”
notes.2409: (tn, Heb): “Is it not [because] I have been silent, and from long ago?”
notes.2410: (sn): God’s patience with sinful Israel has caused them to think that they can sin with impunity and suffer no consequences.

rashi.heb:
*ואת מי דאגת.* 
ממי נתייראת:
rashi.eng: *And whom did you dread.* Of whom were you afraid?

rashi.heb:
*כי תכזבי.* 
כי פסקת לך מעבודתי וכזבת בי כמו לא יכזבו מימיו (לקמן נח) כל האדם כוזב (תהילים קט״ז:י״א) פליינצ"א בלע"ז וכן כל לשון כזב מי שבוטחין עליו והוא כוזב ובוגד:
rashi.eng: *that you failed.* Heb. תְּכַזֵּבִי, that you ceased to worship Me and you betrayed Me. Comp. (infra 58:11) “Whose water shall not fail (יְכַזְּבוּ).” Comp. also (Psalms 116:11) “Every man is a traitor (כֹּזֵב).” Falajjnc in O.F., to fail. Likewise, every expression of כָּזָב means one upon whom people rely, and he fails and betrays them.

rashi.heb:
*הלא אני מחשה.* 
שהחשתי על כמה פשעים שפשעת בי:
rashi.eng: *Indeed, I am silent.* I kept silent in the face of many transgressions that you transgressed against Me.

notes.2411: (tn, Heb): “I, I will declare your righteousness and your deeds.”

rashi.heb:
*אני אגיד צדקתך.* 
אני תמיד מגיד לך דברים שאם תעשי אותם תצדקי:
rashi.eng: *I tell your righteousness.* Constantly, I tell you things to do, so that you will be righteous.

rashi.heb:
*ואת מעשיך.* 
שאתה עושה שלא ברצוני לא יועילוך בעת רעתך:
rashi.eng: *and your deeds.* that you do against My will shall not avail you at the time of your distress.

notes.2412: (tn): The Hebrew text has קִבּוּצַיִךְ (qibbutsayikh, “your gatherings”), an otherwise unattested noun from the verbal root קָבַץ (qavats, “gather”). Perhaps this alludes to their religious assemblies and by metonymy to their rituals. Since idolatry is a prominent theme in the context, some understand this as a reference to a collection of idols. The second half of the verse also favors this view.
notes.2413: (tn, Heb): “all of them a wind lifts up.”
notes.2415: (tn): Or “seeks refuge in me.” “Seeking refuge” is a metonymy for “being loyal to.”
notes.2416: (tn, Heb): “possess, own.” The point seems to be that he will have free access to God’s presence, as if God’s temple mount were his personal possession.

rashi.heb:
*בזעקך יצילוך קבוציך.* 
יקומו נא קבוצו' אלילי' ופסילים ומכחישי תורה אשר קבצת ויצילוך בזעקך מצרתך הלא את כולם ישא רוח ולא יוכלו להציל:
rashi.eng: *When you cry out, let your collections save you.* Let the collection of your idols and your graven images [and those who deny the Torah] that you collected, rise and save you when you cry out from your distress. Indeed, wind will carry all of them off, and they will not rise, neither will they be able to save.

notes.2417: (tn): Since God is speaking throughout this context, perhaps we should emend the text to “and I say.” However, divine speech is introduced in v. 15.

rashi.heb:
*ואמר סלו סלו.* 
כה אמר הנביא בשמי לעמי כבשו מסילה סלולה פנו יצר הרע מדרכיכם:
rashi.eng: *And he shall say, “Pave, pave”.* So will the prophet say in My name to My people, “Pave, pave a paved highway, clear away the evil inclination from your ways.”

rashi.heb:
*הרימו מכשול.* 
סלקו האבנים שאתם נכשלי' רגליכ' בהם הם הירהורי רשע:
rashi.eng: *remove the obstacle.* Remove the stones upon which your feet stumble; they are wicked thoughts.

notes.2418: (tn, Heb): “the one who dwells forever.” שֹׁכֵן עַד (shokhen ’ad) is sometimes translated “the one who lives forever,” and understood as a reference to God’s eternal existence. However, the immediately preceding and following descriptions (“high and exalted” and “holy”) emphasize his sovereign rule. In the next line, he declares, “I dwell in an exalted and holy [place],” which refers to the place from which he rules. Therefore it is more likely that שֹׁכֵן עַד (shokhen ’ad) means “I dwell [in my lofty palace] forever” and refers to God’s eternal kingship.
notes.2419: (tn, Heb): “and also with the crushed and lowly of spirit.” This may refer to the repentant who have humbled themselves (see 66:2) or more generally to the exiles who have experienced discouragement and humiliation.
notes.2420: (tn, Heb): “to restore the lowly of spirit and to restore the heart of the crushed.”

rashi.heb:
*מרום וקדוש.* 
אני שוכן ומשם אני עם דכא ושפל רוח שאני מרכין שכינתי עליו:
rashi.eng: *“With the lofty and the holy ones”.* I dwell, and thence I am with the crushed and the humble in spirit, upon whom I lower My Presence.

rashi.heb:
*שפלים.* 
נדכאים סובלי עוני וחליים:
rashi.eng: *humble… crushed.* Suffering from poverty and illnesses.

notes.2421: (tn): Or perhaps, “argue,” or “accuse” (so NAB, NIV, NRSV).
notes.2422: (tn, Heb): “for a spirit from before me would be faint.”

rashi.heb:
*כי לא לעולם אריב.* 
אם אביא יסורין על האדם אין תחרותי עליו לאורך ימים ולא קצפי לנצח:
rashi.eng: *For I will not contend forever.* If I bring afflictions upon a person, My contention with him is not for a long time, neither is My anger forever.

rashi.heb:
*כי רוח מלפני יעטוף.* 
כאשר רוח האד' שהוא מלפני שניתן בו מאתי יעטוף יודה ויכנע על מעלו כמו (איכה ב׳:י״ט) העטופים ברעב, בעטף עולל (שם) והנשמו' שאני עשיתי:
rashi.eng: *when a spirit from before Me humbles itself.* Heb. יַעֲטוֹף. When the spirit of man, which is from before Me, humbles itself, confesses and humbles itself because of its betrayal. Comp. (Lam. 2:19) “humbled (הָעֲטוּפִים) with hunger”, “when the small child and the suckling are humbled (בֵּעָטֵף).” And the souls which I made.

rashi.heb:
*כי רוח מלפני.* 
כי זה משמש בלשון כאשר כמו כי תראה כי תבא כלומר כשרוחו נעטפת והוא נכנע אני מבטל ריבי וקצפי מעליו:
rashi.eng: *when a spirit from before Me.* Heb. כִּי. This instance of the word כִּי is used as an expression of “when.” Comp. (infra 58:7) “When you see (כִּי תִרְאֶה);” (Deut. 26:1) “When you come (כִּי תָבוֹא).” That is to say, when his spirit is humbled, and he is humbled, I terminate My quarrel and My anger from upon him.

notes.2423: (tn, Heb): “and I struck him, hiding, and I was angry.” פָּנַיִם (panayim, “face”) is the implied object of “hiding.”
notes.2424: (tn, Heb): “and he walked [as an] apostate in the way of his heart.”

rashi.heb:
*בעון בצעו.* 
גזלתו:
rashi.eng: *For the iniquity of his thievery.* Heb. בִּצְעוֹ, his thievery.

rashi.heb:
*קצפתי.* 
תחלה ואכהו הסתר פני תמיד מצרתו ואקצוף ועל כי הולך שובב בדרך לבו וסרס את המקרא וכן פירושו בעון בצעו וילך שובב בדרכי לבו קצפתי ואכהו:
rashi.eng: *I became wroth.* at the beginning and I smote him, always hiding My face from his distress and I was wroth for he went rebelliously in the way of his heart. Transpose the verse and explain it thus: For the iniquity of his thievery and the fact that he went rebelliously in the way of his heart, I became wroth and smote him.

notes.2425: (tn, Heb): “his ways” (so KJV, NASB, NIV); TEV “how they acted.”
notes.2426: (tn, Heb): “and I will restore consolation to him, to his mourners.”

rashi.heb:
*דרכיו ראיתי.* 
כשהוא נכנע מלפני שבאתהו צרה:
rashi.eng: *I saw his ways.* when he humbled himself before Me, when troubles befell him.

rashi.heb:
*וארפאהו ואנחהו.* 
אוליכו בדרך מרפא, או ואנחהו ל' הנחה ומרגוע:
rashi.eng: *and I will heal him, and I will lead him.* Heb. וְאַנְחֵהוּ. I will lead him in the way of healing. Alternatively, וְאַנְחֵהוּ is an expression of rest and tranquility.

rashi.heb:
*לו ולאבליו.* 
למצטערים עליו:
rashi.eng: *him and his mourners.* to those who are troubled over him.

notes.2427: (tc): The Hebrew text has literally, “one who creates fruit of lips.” Perhaps the pronoun אֲנִי (’ani) should be inserted after the participle; it may have been accidentally omitted by haplography: נוּב שְׂפָתָיִם[אֲנִי] בּוֹרֵא (bore’ [’ani] nuv s�fatayim). “Fruit of the lips” is often understood as a metonymy for praise; perhaps it refers more generally to joyful shouts (see v. 18).
notes.2428: (tn, Heb): “Peace, peace.” The repetition of the noun emphasizes degree.

rashi.heb:
*בורא.* 
ניב שפתים בורא אני לו ניב שפתים חדש כלפי שבאתהו צרה עד עתה והכל קראו עליו תגר יקראו לו שלום שלום:
rashi.eng: *[I] create the speech of the lips.* I create for him a new manner of speech. In contrast to the trouble that befell him, and everyone was degrading him, they will call, “Peace, peace.”

rashi.heb:
*לרחוק ולקרוב.* 
שניהם שוין מי שנתיישן והורגל בתורתי ועבודתי מנעוריו ומי שנתקרב עתה מקרוב לשוב מדרכו הרעה אמר ה' ורפאתיו מחליו ומחטאיו:
rashi.eng: *to the far and to the near.* Both are equal; he who aged and was accustomed to My Torah and My worship from his youth, and he who drew near now, just recently to repent of his evil way. Said the Lord, “I will heal him of his malady and of his sins.”

rashi.heb:
*והרשעים.* 
שאין נותנין לב לשוב:
rashi.eng: *But the wicked.* who do not give a thought to repent.

rashi.heb:
*כים נגרש.* 
הים הזה גליו מתגאים לרום למעלה ולצאת חוץ לגבול החול אשר שמתי גבול לים וכשמגיע שם הוא נשבר על כורחו וכל זה גל חבירו רואה ואינו חוזר בו כך הרשע רואה את חברו לוקה ברשעו ואינו חוזר בו ומה הים רפשו וסריותו על פיו כך הרשעים סריותם בפיהם כגון פרעה אמר מי ה' (שמות ה׳:ב׳) סנחרב אמר מי בכל אלהי הארצות (ישעיהו ל״ו:כ׳) נבוכדנצר אמר (שם יד) אדמה לעליון:
rashi.eng: *like the turbulent sea.* This seaits waves raise themselves high and strive to go out of the boundary of sand that I made as a boundary for the sea, and when it reaches there, against its will it breaks. The next wave sees all this, yet does not turn back. Similarly, the wicked man sees his friend being punished for his wickedness; yet he does not turn back. Also, just as the sea has its mud and its offensive matter on its mouth, [i.e., on its surface,] so do the wicked have their offensive matter in their mouth; e.g., Pharaoh said, (Exodus 5: 2) “Who is the Lord?” Sennacherib said (supra 36:20), “Who are they among all the Gods of the lands…?” Nebuchadnezzar said, (supra 14:14) “I will liken myself to the Most High.”

rashi.heb:
*כים נגרש.* 
כים אשר נגרש שגורש כל היום רפש וטיט:
rashi.eng: *like the turbulent sea.* Like the sea, which is turbulent, that casts up all day mud and dirt.

rashi.heb:
*אין שלום.* 
כלפי שאמר לצדיקים ולבעלי תשובה שלום שלום לרחוק וגו' חזר ואמר אין שלום לרשעים:
rashi.eng: *There is no peace.* In contrast to what he said to the righteous and the repentant, “Peace, peace to the far, etc.,” he returned and said, “There is no peace for the wicked.”

notes.2429: (tn, Heb): “declare to my people their rebellion.”
notes.2430: (tn, Heb): “and to the house of Jacob their sin.” The verb “declare” is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).

rashi.heb:
*והגד לעמי פשעם.* 
אלו תלמידי חכמים שכל שגגתם פשע ששגג' תלמוד עולה זדון:
rashi.eng: *and relate to My people their transgression.* These are the Torah scholars, whose every inadvertent sin is counted as a transgression, for an error in study is accounted as an intentional sin.

rashi.heb:
*ולבית יעקב חטאתם.* 
אלו עמי הארץ שאף זדונם שגגה:
rashi.eng: *and to the house of Jacob their sins.* These are the ignorant people, whose willful sins, are accounted inadvertent.

notes.2431: (tn, Heb): “ways” (so KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, TEV); NLT “my laws.”

rashi.heb:
*ואותי יום יום ידרשון.* 
כענין שנא' ויפתוהו בפיהם (תהלים עח):
rashi.eng: *Yet they seek Me daily.* Like the matter that is stated (Ps. 78:36): “And they beguiled Him with their mouth.”

rashi.heb:
*ודעת דרכי יחפצון.* 
חפצים לשאול הוראות לחכמים כאילו רוצים לקיימם:
rashi.eng: *and they wish to know My ways.* They wish to ask instructions of the wise men as if they wished to fulfill them.

rashi.heb:
*כגוי אשר צדקה עשה וגו'.* 
כך שואלים אותי תמיד משפט צדק ואין דעתם לקיימם וכשהן צמים ואין נענין אומרים למה צמנו ולא ראית ואני אומר הן ביום צומכם תמצאו חפץ כל חפצי צרכיכם אתם עמלים למצוא ואף בגזל וחמס:
rashi.eng: *like a nation that performed righteousness, etc..* In this manner they constantly ask Me ordinances of righteousness, but they do not intend to fulfill them, and when they fast and are not answered, they say, “Why have we fasted, and You did not see?” But I say, “Behold, on the day of your fast you pursue business,” all the affairs of your necessities you toil to pursue, even robbery and violence.

notes.2432: (tn): The words “they lament” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.2433: (tn, Heb): “you find pleasure”; NASB “you find your desire.”
notes.2434: (tn): Or perhaps, “debtors.” See HALOT 865 s.v. * עָצֵב.

rashi.heb:
*וכל עצביכם.* 
בעלי חוב שלכם הנעצבים על ידכם אתם נוגשים אותם ביום צומכם:
rashi.eng: *and [from] all your debtors.* Heb. עַצְּבֵיכֶם [lit. your griefs.] Your debtors, who are grieved because of you; you exact payment from them on the day of your fast.

notes.2435: (tn, Heb): “you fast for” (so NASB); NRSV “you fast only to quarrel.”
notes.2436: (tn, Heb): “and for striking with a sinful fist.”

rashi.heb:
*לא תצומו כיום.* 
כמשפט היום לשבור לבבכם כדי שישמע קולכם במרום:
rashi.eng: *Do not fast like this day.* like the manner of this day, to break your hearts in order that your voice be heard on high.

notes.2438: (tn, Heb): “a day when man humbles himself.” The words “Do I want” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*הלכוף.* 
ה"א זו תמיהא כלו' שמא לכוף כאגמון ראשו אני צריך, אגמון הוא כמין מחט כפוף וצדין בו דגים וקורין לו איי"ם בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *Is it to bend.* Heb. הֲלָכֹף. This ‘hey’ is the interrogative. That is to say, “Perhaps I require bending the head like a fishhook (כְּאַגְמֹן)?” אַגְמֹן is a sort of bent needle with which they catch fish, and they call it ajjm in O.F.

rashi.heb:
*הלזה תקרא צום.* 
ל' תמיהא לפיכך הה"א נקודה חטף פתח:
rashi.eng: *Will you call this a fast.* Heb. הֲלָזֶה. An interrogative form. Therefore, the ‘hey’ is punctuated with a ‘hataf-pattah.’

notes.2440: (tn, Heb): “Is this not a fast I choose?” “No” is supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.2441: (tn): The words “I want you” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*חרצובות.* 
ל' קישור ואיסור:
rashi.eng: *fetters.* Heb. חַרְצֻבּוֹת, an expression of tying and binding.

rashi.heb:
*מוטה.* 
הטיית משפט:
rashi.eng: *perverseness.* Heb. מוֹטָה, perversion of justice.

rashi.heb:
*וכל מוטה תנתקו.* 
ת"י וכל דין מסטי תסלקון:
rashi.eng: *and all perverseness you shall eliminate.* Heb. וְכָל מוֹטָה תְּנַתֵּקוּ. Jonathan renders: And all perversion of justice you shall eliminate.

notes.2443: (tn, Heb): “Is it not?” The rhetorical question here expects a positive answer, “It is!”
notes.2444: (tn, Heb): “and afflicted [ones], homeless [ones] you should bring [into] a house.” On the meaning of מְרוּדִים (m�rudim, “homeless”) see HALOT 633 s.v. *מָרוּד.
notes.2445: (tn, Heb): “and from your flesh do not hide yourself.”

rashi.heb:
*ועניים מרודים.* 
נאנחים ונאנקים על צרתם כגון עניי ומרודי (איכה ג׳:י״ט) אריד בשיחי (תהלים נה):
rashi.eng: *moaning poor.* Heb. מְרוּדִים. Sighing and moaning about their distress. Comp. (Lam. 3:19) “my affliction and my sighing (וּמְרוּדִי);” (Ps. 55:3) “I mourn (אָרִיד) in my grief.”

rashi.heb:
*ומבשרך.* 
ומקרובך:
rashi.eng: *and from your flesh.* And from your kinsman.

notes.2446: (tn, Heb): “will burst out like the dawn.” Light here symbolizes God’s favor and restored blessing, as the immediately following context makes clear.
notes.2448: (tn): Or “righteousness.” Their godly behavior will be on display for all to see.
notes.2449: (sn): The nation will experience God’s protective presence.

rashi.heb:
*יבקע כשחר.* 
כעמוד השחר הבוקע בעבים:
rashi.eng: *as the dawn.* Like the ray of dawn that breaks through the clouds.

rashi.heb:
*וארוכתך מהרה.* 
ורפואתך מהרה כמו אעלה ארוכה לך (ירמיהו ל׳:י״ז):
rashi.eng: *and your healing.* Heb. וַאֲרֻכָתְךָ, and your healing shall quickly sprout. Comp. (Jer. 30:17) “I will bring up healing (אֲרֻכָה) for you.”

notes.2450: (tn, Heb): “if you.” In the Hebrew text vv. 9b-10 are one long conditional sentence. The protasis (“if” clauses appear in vv. 9b-10a), with the apodosis (“then” clause) appearing in v. 10b.

notes.2451: (tn, Heb): “if you.” See the note on “you must” in v. 9b.
notes.2452: (tn, Heb): “If you furnish for the hungry [with] your being, and the appetite of the oppressed you satisfy.”
notes.2454: (tn, Heb): “and your darkness [will be] like noonday.”

rashi.heb:
*ותפק לרעב נפשך.* 
בתנחומי דברים טובים:
rashi.eng: *And you draw out your soul to the hungry.* with consolations of good words.

notes.2455: (tn, Heb): “he will satisfy in parched regions your appetite.”
notes.2456: (tn, Heb): “and your bones he will strengthen.”

rashi.heb:
*בצחצחות.* 
בעת צמאון ובצורת כך ת"י:
rashi.eng: *in drought.* Heb. בְּצַחְצָחוֹת, at the time of thirst and drought. So did Jonathan render.

rashi.heb:
*יחליץ.* 
יזיין כמו חלוצי צבא (במדבר לא):
rashi.eng: *strengthen.* Heb. יַחֲלִיץ [lit. arm.] Comp. (Num. 31:5) “Armed (חֲלוּצֵי) for war.”

notes.2457: (tn, Heb): “and they will build from you ancient ruins.”
notes.2458: (tc): The Hebrew text has “the one who restores paths for dwelling.” The idea of “paths to dwell in” is not a common notion. Some have proposed emending נְתִיבוֹת (n�tivot, “paths”) to נְתִיצוֹת (n�titsot, “ruins”), a passive participle from נָתַץ (natats, “tear down”; see HALOT 732 s.v. *נְתִיצָה), because tighter parallelism with the preceding line is achieved. However, none of the textual sources support this emendation. The line may mean that paths must be repaired in order to dwell in the land.

rashi.heb:
*משובב נתיבות לשבת.* 
תירגם יונתן מתיב רשיעיא לאורייתא:
rashi.eng: *restorer of the paths, to dwell in.* Heb. מְשׁוֹבֵב. Jonathan renders: restorer of the wicked to the Torah.

rashi.heb:
*משובב.* 
כמו משיב:
rashi.eng: *restorer.* מְשׁוֹבֵב is like מֵשִׁיב.

rashi.heb:
*לשבת.* 
ליישובו של עולם:
rashi.eng: *to dwell.* to the Torah, which insures the settlement of the world.

notes.2459: (tn): Lit., “if you.” In the Hebrew text vv. 13-14 are one long conditional sentence. The protasis (“if” clauses appear in v. 13), with the apodosis (“then” clause) appearing in v. 14.
notes.2460: (tn, Heb): “if you turn from the Sabbath your feet.”
notes.2461: (tn, Heb): “[from] doing your desires on my holy day.” The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa supplies the preposition מִן (min) on “doing.”
notes.2462: (tn, Heb): “and call the Sabbath a pleasure”; KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV “a delight.”
notes.2463: (tn, Heb): “and [call] the holy [day] of the Lord honored.” On קָדוֹשׁ (qadosh, “holy”) as indicating a time period, see BDB 872 s.v. 2.e (cf. also Neh 8:9-11).
notes.2464: (tn, Heb): “and you honor it [by refraining] from accomplishing your ways, from finding your desire and speaking a word.” It is unlikely that the last phrase (“speaking a word”) is a prohibition against talking on the Sabbath; instead it probably refers to making transactions or plans (see Hos 10:4). Some see here a reference to idle talk (cf. 2 Sam 19:30).

notes.2465: (tn): For a parallel use of the phrase “find joy in” (Hitpael of עָנַג [’anag] followed by the preposition עַל [’al]), see Ps 37:4.
notes.2466: (tn, Heb): “and I will cause you to ride upon the heights of the land.” The statement seems to be an allusion to Deut 32:13, where it is associated, as here, with God’s abundant provision of food.
notes.2467: (tn, Heb): “and I will cause you to eat the inheritance of Jacob your father.” The Hebrew term נַחֲלָה (nakhalah) likely stands by metonymy for the crops that grow on Jacob’s “inheritance” (i.e., the land he inherited as a result of God’s promise).
notes.2468: (tn, Heb): “for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.” The introductory כִּי (ki) may be asseverative (as reflected in the translation) or causal/explanatory, explaining why the preceding promise will become reality (because it is guaranteed by the divine word).

rashi.heb:
*נחלת יעקב אביך.* 
נחלה בלא מצרים כמה שנא' ופרצת ימה וקדמה וגו' (בראשית כ״ח:י״ד) לא כאברהם שנאמר (שם יג) הארץ אשר אתה רואה ויעקב שמר את השבת שנא' (שם לג) ויחן את פני העיר שקבע תחומין עם דמדומי חמה כך פי' ר' שמשון:
rashi.eng: *the heritage of Jacob your father.* An inheritance without boundaries, as it is said (Gen. 28:14): “And you shall spread to the west and to the east, etc.” Not like Abraham, about whom it is stated (ibid. 13:15): “The land that you see…” And Jacob indeed kept the Sabbath, as it is said (ibid. 33:18): “And he encamped before the city,” i.e., he established the Sabbath limits at twilight. So did Rabbi Samson explain it.

notes.2470: (tn, Heb): “or his ear too heavy [i.e., “dull”] to hear.”

rashi.heb:
*הן לא קצרה.* 
את אשר לא נושעתם לא מקוצר ידו הוא:
rashi.eng: *Behold, the hand of the Lord is not too short.* Your failure to be delivered is not due to the shortness of My hand.

notes.2471: (tn, Heb): “and your sins have caused [his] face to be hidden from you so as not to hear.”

rashi.heb:
*הסתירו פנים.* 
גרמו לכם שהסתיר פניו מכם:
rashi.eng: *have caused [Him] to hide [His] face.* They caused for you that He hid His face from you.

rashi.heb:
*נגאלו.* 
לשון טינוף וכן לחם מגואל (מלאכי א):
rashi.eng: *were defiled.* Heb. נְגֹאֲלוּ, an expression of defilement. Comp. (Mal. 1:7) “polluted bread (מְגֹאָל).”

notes.2475: (tn, Heb): “that which is pressed in hatches [as] a snake.”

rashi.heb:
*צפעוני.* 
מין נחש רע:
rashi.eng: *vipers.* a species of harmful snake.

rashi.heb:
*בקעו.* 
אישקלורש"ט בלע"ז כלומר מעשים מכוערי' שאינם לטובתם עשו:
rashi.eng: *hatched.* Heb. בִּקְּעוּ, eskloterant in O.F. That is to say that they committed ugly deeds, from which they did not benefit.

rashi.heb:
*וקורי עכביש.* 
איריניי"ש בלע"ז וקורי אורטור"ש בלע"ז, קורי הם כלי האורג שהשתי מוסך בהן, ומנחם חברו במחברת קורות ע"ש שהעכביש מיסך אריגותיו בקורות:
rashi.eng: *and… spider webs.* Irajjne in O.F., spider, and קוּרֵי is ordiojjrs in O.F., warp. קוּרֵי are the implements of the weaver, those upon which the warp is mounted. Menahem (Machbereth Menahem p. 158) classifies it in the class of קוֹרוֹת, beams, since the spider mounts the warp of his weavings on beams.

rashi.heb:
*והזורה.* 
ת"י משחנן לשון חימום שקורין בלע"ז קובי"ר המחממן יוצא מהן כשהוא מבקע הקליפה, ועיקר לשון והזורה לשון עיצור הוא להוציא הבלוע בתוכו כמו ויזר את הגזה (שופטים ו׳:ל״ח) ועיצורו של זה הוא חימומו:
rashi.eng: *and what hatches.* Heb. וְהַזּוּרֶה. Jonathan renders: וּמְשַׁחְנָן, an expression of warming, called in O.F. kover [couve], hatching when one warms them, it emerges from them when he cracks the shell. The original meaning of וְהַזּוּרֶה is an expression of pressing to extract what is absorbed within. Comp. (Jud. 6:38) “And pressed (וַיָּזַר) the fleece.” The pressing of this one is its hatching.

rashi.heb:
*אפעה.* 
מין נחש שהוא רע כך לא ישתלמו במעשיהם אלא רעה:
rashi.eng: *viper.* Heb. אֶפְעֶה, a species of snake that is harmful, so will nothing result from their deeds but evil.

notes.2476: (tn, Heb): “their deeds are deeds of sin, and the work of violence [is] in their hands.”

notes.2478: (tn, Heb): “they quickly pour out innocent blood.”
notes.2479: (tn, Heb): “their thoughts are thoughts of sin, destruction and crushing [are] in their roadways.”

notes.2480: (tn, Heb): “a way of peace they do not know, and there is no justice in their pathways.”
notes.2481: (tn, Heb): “their paths they make crooked, everyone who walks in it does not know peace.”

rashi.heb:
*ואין משפט במעגלותם.* 
כלומר אין במעגל דרכיהם דבר נשפט באמת כמשפטו:
rashi.eng: *and there is no justice in their paths.* That is to say that in their paths there is nothing judged truly according to its law.

rashi.heb:
*נתיבותיהם עקשו להם.* 
הם העוו את דרכם לעצמם:
rashi.eng: *they have made themselves crooked paths.* They made their road crooked for themselves.

notes.2482: (tn): מִשְׁפָּט (mishpat), which refers to “justice” in the earlier verses, here refers to “justice from God,” or “vindication.” Because the people are unjust, God refuses to vindicate them before their enemies. See v. 11.
notes.2483: (sn): The prophet speaks on behalf of the sinful nation and confesses its sins.
notes.2484: (sn): Light here symbolizes prosperity and blessing.
notes.2485: (tn, Heb): “but, look, darkness”; NIV “but all is darkness.”
notes.2486: (tn): The words “we wait for” are supplied in the translation; the verb is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
notes.2487: (tn): The plural noun form may indicate degree here.
notes.2488: (tn): Or “walk about”; NCV “all we have is darkness.”
notes.2489: (tn): The plural noun form may indicate degree here.

rashi.heb:
*רחק משפט ממנו.* 
שהיינו צועקים חמס מאויבינו ואין הקב"ה שופט לנקום נקמה:
rashi.eng: *justice is far from us.* For we were crying that we were robbed by our enemies, yet the Holy One, blessed be He, does not judge to avenge us.

rashi.heb:
*ולא תשיגנו צדקה.* 
הנחמות הטובות שהבטיחנו אין משיגות אותנו לבוא:
rashi.eng: *and righteousness does not overtake us.* The good consolations that He promised us are not coming to overtake us.

rashi.heb:
*לנגוהות.* 
נקוה ובאפלות נהלך:
rashi.eng: *for brightness.* we hope, but we walk in gloom.

notes.2491: (tn, Heb): among the strong, like dead men.”

rashi.heb:
*באשמנים.* 
מנחם פתר לשון מחשכים, ורוב הפותרי' מודים לו אבל דונש פתר בו לשון שומן והאל"ף נוסף בו כמו אל"ף שבאחותי (איוב יג) ושבאכזב (ירמיה טו) ודרך האתרים (במדבר כא) אף כאן בין האשמני' בין החיים השמני' אנחנו כמתים וי"ת לשון מסגר איתאחד באפנא כמה דאחידין קבריא באפי מיתיא:
rashi.eng: *in dark places.* Heb. בָּאַשְׁמַנִּים. Menahem (Machbereth, p. 35) interpreted it as an expression of dark places, and most exegetes concur with him. Dunash, however, (Tesuhvoth Dunash, p. 93) interprets it as an expression of fat (שׁוּמָן), with the ‘alef’ prefixed to it like the ‘alef’ that is in (Job 13:17) אַחְוָתִי, “my narrative,” [derived from חוה]; and that is in (Jer. 15:18) אַכְזָב, “a failure,” (derived from כזב; and (Num. 21:1) “the way of the spies (הָאֲתָרִים),” [derived from תור]. Here, too, among the שְׁמֵנִים, among the lusty living, we are like dead. And Jonathan rendered it as an expression of locking: It is locked before us as the graves are locked before the dead.

rashi.heb:
*הגה נהגה.* 
לשון יללה:
rashi.eng: *we moan.* Heb. הָגֹה נֶהְגֶה, an expression of wailing.

notes.2493: (tn, Heb): “for many are our rebellious deeds before you.”
notes.2494: (tn, Heb): “indeed [or “for”] our rebellious deeds (are) with us, and our sins, we know them.”

notes.2495: (tn, Heb): “speaking.” A new sentence was started here in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.2496: (tn, Heb): “conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood.”

rashi.heb:
*דבר עשק.* 
כמו לדבר עשק:
rashi.eng: *speaking oppression.* Like: to speak oppression.

rashi.heb:
*הורו והוגו.* 
לירות ולהוציא הורו לשון ירה בים (שמות ט״ו:ד׳) ד"א הורו והוגו הרב והתלמיד שם המקור (סא"א) והוגו כאשר הוגה מן המסילה (שמואל ב כ׳:י״ג) הגו סיגים מכסף (משלי כ״ה:ד׳):
rashi.eng: *sprouting and giving forth.* Heb. הֹרוֹ וְהֹגוֹ to shoot and to give forth. הֹרוֹ is an expression of (Ex. 15:4) “He shot (יָרָה) into the sea.” (Another explanation: הֹרוֹ means: the teacher and the disciple, a gerund.) הֹגוֹ is an expression of (II Sam. 20:13) “When he was removed (הֹגָה) from the highway;” (Prov. 25:4) “Take away (הָגוֹ) the dross from the silver.”

notes.2497: (tn): Or “righteousness” (ASV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); KJV, NAB “justice.”

rashi.heb:
*והוסג אחור משפט.* 
נקמתינו מאויבינו שהיא תלויה בהקב"ה וצדקתו עומדת מרחוק למה כי כשלה אמת ברחובותינו וכיון שהאמת כשלה מארץ אף משמי' אין הצדק והמשפט באין:
rashi.eng: *And justice has turned away backwards.* Our revenge from our enemies, which depends upon the Holy One, blessed be He, and His righteousness stands from afar. Why? For truth has stumbled in our streets, [and since truth has stumbled from the earth, even from heaven righteousness and justice do not come.]

notes.2499: (tn, Heb): “and it is displeasing in his eyes.”

rashi.heb:
*משתולל.* 
מוחזק שוטה על הבריות כמו (מיכה א) אלכה שולל והוא מגזרת שוגג דמתרגמינן שלו וכן (ש"ב י) על השל:
rashi.eng: *is considered mad.* Heb. מִשְׁתּוֹלֵל, considered mad by the people. Comp. (Micah 1:8) “I will go as a mad man (שׁוֹלָל).” This is equivalent to שׁוֹגֵג, inadvertent, which the Targum renders: שָׁלוּ. Likewise (II Sam. 6:7), “For his error (הַשַּׁל).”

rashi.heb:
*וירע בעיניו כי אין משפט.* 
לפיכך הביא עליהם הפורענות:
rashi.eng: *and was displeased for there is no justice.* Therefore, He brought retribution upon them.

notes.2500: (tn, Heb): “man” (so KJV, ASV); TEV “no one to help.”
notes.2502: (tn, Heb): “and his arm delivers for him.”

rashi.heb:
*וירא כי אין איש.* 
ועתה בהנחמו על הרעה לעמו רואה כי אין איש צדיק לעמוד בפרץ:
rashi.eng: *And He saw that there was no man.* And now, when He repents of the evil to His people, He sees that there is no righteous man to stand in the breach.

rashi.heb:
*וישתומם.* 
ויחרש לראות אם יש מפגיע בעדם ואין מפגיע וישתומם ל' אדם העומד ותוהא ושותק בתמהונו ותי"ו וישתומם כתי"ו של משתולל ושניהם כאן משמשות לשון מתפעל וכן דרך התיבה שיסודה הראשון שי"ן או סמ"ך כשהיא נהפכת ללשון מתפעל נתפעל ויתפעל בא התי"ו באמצע אותיות שרש התיבה נמצא וישתומם לשון שמו שמים (ירמיהו ב׳:י״ב) משמים בתוכם (יחזקאל ג׳:ט״ו) נשמו אחרונים (איוב י״ח:כ׳) ל' תמהון:
rashi.eng: *and He was astounded.* He was silent to see whether there was an intercessor, and there was no intercessor. וַיִּשְׁתּוֹמֵם is an expression of a man who stands and wonders and remains silent in his wonder, and the ‘tav’ of וַיִּשְׁתּוֹמֵם is like the ‘tav’ of מִשְׁתּוֹלֵל, and both of them serve here as the reflexive, and this is the procedure of the word whose first radical is a ‘shin’ or a ‘samech,’ that when it is converted into the form of מִתְפָּעֵל, the present reflexive, נִתְפָּעֵל, the past reflexive, or יִתְפָּעֵל, the future reflexive, the ‘tav’ comes in the middle of the letters of the radical. The result is that וַיִּשְׁתּוֹמֵם is an expression from the same root as (Jer. 2:12) “Be admonished (שֹׁמּוּ), O ye heavens;” (Ezekiel 3:15) “appalled (מַשְׁמִים) among them;” (Job 18:20) “the later ones will be astonished (נָשַׁמּוּ),” an expression of wonder.

rashi.heb:
*ותושע לו זרועו.* 
וינקם מאויביו:
rashi.eng: *and His arm saved for Him.* and He will take revenge from His enemies.

rashi.heb:
*וצדקתו.* 
סמכתהו הוא להשיאו ולאמץ ידיו בנקמתו ואע"פ שאין אנחנו הגונים להושיע:
rashi.eng: *and His righteousness, that supported Him.* to entice Him and to strengthen His hands in His revenge, although we are not worthy of being saved.

notes.2504: (tn): Or “righteousness” (KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT); NCV “goodness.”
notes.2505: (tn): Or “a breastplate” (traditional; so many English versions); TEV “a coat of armour.”
notes.2506: (tn, Heb): “and [as] a helmet deliverance on his head.”
notes.2507: (tn, Heb): “and he puts on the clothes of vengeance [as] a garment.”

rashi.heb:
*קנאה.* 
אינפרימנ"ט בלע"ז לקנאות לשמו הגדול:
rashi.eng: *zeal.* enprenmant in O.F., to be zealous for His great name.

notes.2508: (tn, Heb): “in accordance with deeds, so he repays, anger to his adversaries, repayment to his enemies.”

rashi.heb:
*כעל גמולות.* 
כדת להשיב על גמולות האויבים:
rashi.eng: *According to their deeds.* As is fitting to recompense for what the enemies dealt to them.

rashi.heb:
*כעל ישלם.* 
כדת להשיב עליהם ישלם:
rashi.eng: *accordingly He shall repay.* As is fitting to repay them He shall repay.

notes.2510: (tc, Heb): “fear.” A few medieval Hebrew mss read “see.”
notes.2511: (tn, Heb): “and they fear from the west the name of the Lord.”
notes.2512: (tn, Heb): “and from the rising of the sun his splendor.”
notes.2514: (tn, Heb): “the wind of the Lord drives it on.” The term רוּחַ (ruakh) could be translated “breath” here (see 30:28).

rashi.heb:
*כי יבא כנהר.* 
צרה על אויביו:
rashi.eng: *For… shall come like a river.* distress upon His enemies.

rashi.heb:
*נוססה בו.* 
נפלאות בו ל' נס, ד"א נוססה בו אוכלת בו כתולעת בעץ כמו (לעיל י) והיה כמסוס נוסס:
rashi.eng: *is wondrous in it.* Heb. נֹסְסָה, is wondrous in it, an expression of a miracle (נֵס). Another explanation: נֹסְסָה [means:] eats into him like a worm in wood. Comp. (supra 10:18) “And it shall be as a tree eaten to powder by the worms.”

notes.2516: (tn, Heb): “and to those who turn from rebellion in Jacob.”

rashi.heb:
*ובא לציון גואל.* 
כל זמן שציון חריבה עדיין לא בא הגואל סא"א:
rashi.eng: *And a redeemer shall come to Zion.* As long as Zion is in ruins, the redeemer has not yet come.

notes.2517: (tn): Or “my covenant with” (so many English versions); NCV “my agreement with.” The Lord promises the repentant (note “to them”) that they and their offspring will possess his spirit and function as his spokesmen. In this regard they follow in the footsteps of the Lord’s special servant. See 42:1; 49:2; 51:16.
notes.2518: (tn, Heb): “from now and on into the future.”

rashi.heb:
*זאת בריתי אותם.* 
בדבר זה כרתי בריתי להם ואקיים כי אף בגלותם לא תשכח תורתי מהם:
rashi.eng: *As for Me, this is My covenant with them.* In this matter, I made a covenant with them, and I will fulfill it, for even in their exile, My Torah shall not be forgotten from them.

notes.2520: (tn): The verb “covers” is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
notes.2521: (tn): Or “glory” (so most English versions); TEV “the brightness of his presence.”

notes.2522: (tn, Heb): “Lift up around your eyes and see!”

rashi.heb:
*על צד תאמנה.* 
על גססין, כסלים של מלכים תהיינה אמונות:
rashi.eng: *shall be raised on [their] side.* [Jonathan renders:] on the flanks, the flanks of the kings, they will be raised.

notes.2523: (tn): Or “shine,” or “be radiant” (NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).
notes.2524: (tn, Heb): “and it will tremble and be wide, your heart.”
notes.2525: (tn, Heb): “the wealth of the sea,” i.e., wealth that is transported from distant lands via the sea.

rashi.heb:
*אז תראי ונהרת.* 
בכן תחזין ותנהרין:
rashi.eng: *Then you shall see and be radiant.* Heb. וְנָהַרְתָּ, from נְהוֹרָה, [Aramaic for light,] then you shall see and be radiant [from Jonathan].

rashi.heb:
*ופחד ורחב לבבך.* 
ויתמה וירחב לבך:
rashi.eng: *and your heart shall be startled and become enlarged.* And your heart shall wonder and become enlarged.

rashi.heb:
*כי יהפך עליך המון ים.* 
ארי יתחלף ליך עותר מערבא:
rashi.eng: *for the abundance of the west shall be turned over to you.* for the abundance of the west shall be turned over to you [after Jonathan].

rashi.heb:
*חיל גוים.* 
נכסי דפלחי כוכביא:
rashi.eng: *the wealth of the nations.* The possessions of the nations [after Jonathan].

notes.2526: (tn, Heb): “an abundance of camels will cover you.”
notes.2528: (tn, Heb): “and they will announce the praises of the Lord.”

rashi.heb:
*שפעת.* 
רוב:
rashi.eng: *A multitude.* Heb. שִׁפְעַת, A multiplicity.

rashi.heb:
*בכרי מדין.* 
הוגני מדין הם גמלים בחורים וכן בכרה קלה (ירמיה ב):
rashi.eng: *the young camels of Midian.* Heb. בִּכְרֵי. [Jonathan renders:] הוֹגְנֵי. They are young camels. Comp. (Jer. 2:23) “a swift young camel (בִּכְרָה).”

rashi.heb:
*ועיפה.* 
גם הם מבני מדין עיפה ועפר (בראשית כ״ה:ד׳):
rashi.eng: *and Ephah.* They, too, are of the sons of Midian. Comp. (Gen. 25:4) “Ephah and Epher.”

notes.2529: (tn, Heb): “will serve you,” i.e., be available as sacrifices (see the next line). Another option is to understood these “rams” as symbolic of leaders who will be subject to the people of Zion. See v. 10.
notes.2530: (tc, Heb): “they will go up on acceptance [on] my altar.” Some have suggested that the preposition עַל (’al) is dittographic (note the preceding יַעֲלוּ [ya’alu]). Consequently, the form should be emended to לְרָצוֹן (l�ratson, “acceptably”; see BDB 953 s.v. רָצוֹן). However, the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa has both לרצון followed by the preposition על, which would argue against deleted the preposition. As the above translation seeks to demonstrate, the preposition עַל (’al) indicates a norm (“in accordance with acceptance” or “acceptably”; IBHS 218 �11.2.13e, n. 111) and the “altar” functions as an objective accusative with a verb of motion (cf. Gen 49:4; Lev 2:2; Num 13:17; J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah [NICOT], 2:534, n. 14).

rashi.heb:
*אילי נביות.* 
דכרי נביות:
rashi.eng: *the rams of Nebaioth.* Heb. אֵילֵי, rams of Nebaioth [after Jonathan].

notes.2531: (tn, Heb): “fly” (so KJV, NASB, NRSV); NAB, NIV “fly along.”
notes.2532: (tn, Heb): “to their windows,” i.e., to the openings in their coops. See HALOT 83 s.v. אֲרֻבָּה.

notes.2534: (tn, Heb): “the ships of Tarshish.” See the note at 2:16.
notes.2535: (tn, Heb): “to the name of the Lord your God.”
notes.2536: (sn): See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

rashi.heb:
*בראשונה.* 
כמו כבראשונה בימי שלמה כעניין שנא' (מלכים א י׳:כ״ב) כי אני תרשיש למלך בים אחת לשלש שנים תבא אני תרשיש וגו', תרשיש שם הים:
rashi.eng: *as in the beginning.* Like ‘as in the beginning,’ meaning in the days of Solomon, like the matter that is stated (I Kings 10:22): “For the king had at sea ships of Tarshish, etc.; once in three years, the ships of Tarshish would come, etc.” Tarshish is the name of the sea.

rashi.heb:
*לשם ה' אלהיך.* 
שנקרא עליך כי ישמעו שמעו ושם גבורתו ויבואו:
rashi.eng: *in the name of the Lord your God.* that is called upon you, for they will hear a report of Him and the name of His might, and come.

rashi.heb:
*כי פארך.* 
נתן לך פאר:
rashi.eng: *for He has glorified you.* He has given you glory.

notes.2537: (tn, Heb): “in my favor I will have compassion on you.”

rashi.heb:
*וברצוני.* 
ובהריצותי לך אימונ"א פייזמנ"ט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and in my grace.* Because I favored you; in old French, en mon apayemant.

notes.2538: (tn): Or “led in procession.” The participle is passive.

rashi.heb:
*ופתחו שעריך תמיד.* 
ל' פתוח ממשקולת ל' כבד ע"ש שפתיחתן פתיחת עולם פתיחת תמיד כמו שבר מל' שבירה כך מלשון פתיחה טי"ש אובירט"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *And they shall open your gates always.* Heb. וּפִתְּחוּ. This is an expression of opening in the strong conjugation (פִּעֵל), since their opening is a perpetual opening, a constant opening. Just as שַׁבֵּר is an expression of breaking, so is פִּתְּחוּ an expression of opening. Tresoverts in O.F.

notes.2539: (tn): Or “For” (KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT); TEV “But.”
notes.2540: (tn): The infinitive absolute appears before the finite verb for emphasis.

notes.2542: (tn, Heb): “the place of my feet.” See Ezek 43:7, where the Lord’s throne is called the “place of the soles of my feet.”

rashi.heb:
*ברוש תדהר ותאשור.* 
מיני עצי יער לבנון:
rashi.eng: *box trees, firs, and cypresses.* Species of trees of the forest of Lebanon.

notes.2543: (sn): See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

rashi.heb:
*ציון קדוש ישראל.* 
ציון דאיתרעי בה קדישא דישראל ציון של קדוש ישראל:
rashi.eng: *Zion of the Holy One of Israel.* [Lit. Zion the Holy One of Israel. Jonathan renders:] Zion desired by the Holy One of Israel, Zion of the Holy One of Israel.

notes.2544: (tn, Heb): “Instead of your being abandoned and despised, with no one passing through, I will make you.”

notes.2545: (sn): The nations and kings are depicted as a mother nursing her children. Restored Zion will be nourished by them as she receives their wealth as tribute.

rashi.heb:
*ושד מלכים.* 
ל' שדים ותינקי יורה עליו:
rashi.eng: *and the breast of kings.* Heb. וְשֹׁד, an expression of breasts (שָׁדַיִם) and ‘you shall suck’ proves it.

notes.2548: (tn): The words “I will bring you” are supplied in the translation; they are understood by ellipsis (see the preceding lines).
